# VL — Changelog

Shipped work, in rough area order. Each entry is a terse one-liner; detail lives in git
history, linked PRs, and `docs/`. For the forward plan see **`ROADMAP.md`**; for rationale
see **`DECISIONS.md`**.

## Type system (Track A)

- **A UNION OF INLINE ARMS NARROWS ON ITS LITERAL DISCRIMINANT, AS THE NAMED SPELLING ALREADY DID (D1473)** — `type Shape = {kind: "circle", r: f64} | {kind: "rect", w: f64, h: f64}` under `if s.kind == "rect"` was `emitProgram: field access but no struct type declared` on a `vl check` rc 0 program whose named-arm twin prints `2`. It is NOT D1242/D1443's route: `collectAnonShapes` and the `#anon` field coder are not involved, and the variant ROWS already exist — `registerInlineUnion` mints one per struct atom keyed on the atom SPELLING, `collectVariantFields` fills its field table and `uVarHeap` interns its heap type. What was missing is only the REVERSE map: `pushDiscrimNarrow` asked `nominalStructNameOfTy`, which scans the program's `TypeDecl`s for a bidirectionally assignable declared name, so an arm nobody named answered `""`, nothing was pushed, and the read fell past `memIsNarrowed`, the two variant arms and the shared-field plan to the `!sDeclared` floor — which is why the message named a struct DECLARATION for a program that declares none. `variantIndexOfOwnRender(tyToEmitName(dTy))` is the same question asked of canon's own render, and it banks the ROW's spelling so the read side's exact `variantIndexOf` compare cannot miss it. **The fallback also runs when the nominal name RESOLVES but names no variant**: an unused `type Rect = {…}` merely EQUAL to an inline arm is found by the reverse map and registered under no row, which declined a union the emitter could serve. The set-membership guard above the push is unchanged and still refutes an arm borrowed from another union. A 20-cell grid goes 8 → 20 `runs` with zero lost (the 8 already running are the shared-field and named-arm controls), including the soundness cell (two arms with the SAME field set parted only by the literal tag) and two DIFFERENT unions sharing an identically-rendered arm; fixtures `unions/inline-arm-discriminant-narrow.vl` and `unions/inline-arm-discriminant-narrow-neighbours.vl`, both of which refuse on the pre-fix seed.
- **A 70-PROGRAM ORDINARY-PROGRAM SWEEP PUTS THE UNSAMPLED POPULATION AT 88.6% `runs` (D1480–D1486)** — no standing instrument samples "a program a person would write on day one": the capability probes are one program per already-known gap and the distilled corpus is generated over fixed axes. 70 written, **62 ran** (all with the correct answer, hand-checked), 8 did not — 6 filed defects, 1 std gap, 1 diagnostic-quality complaint about a legitimate refusal. Two further defects fell out of the ABLATIONS. The finds cluster at BOUNDARIES between two features that each work alone, which is the shape a corpus over independent axes is least likely to reach; ordinary data-structure code and inline/anonymous types both graded solid. Method, rate and the labelled non-defects: `docs/internals/ordinary-program-sweep-2026-09.md`.
- **THE MIXED-SPELLING LITERAL DISCRIMINANT NOW BUILDS AT EVERY SPELLING, AND THE REFUSAL THAT PRESCRIBED AN EDIT STOPS PRESCRIBING ONE (D1460, D1461 — the last two of D1050's bound)** — D1050 lays a discriminant field whose two arms spell their literal set differently out under one rep, the interned ATOM, and recorded a bound of "both arms carry a 2+-member string set". **Each of the two reasons that bound gave was wrong, and both were wrong about the same thing — reading a rep question off a spelling.** `{kind: K1} | {kind: "a"}` (D1460): the MEMBER COUNT was never the rep's question, since the alias form of that same one-member set (`type KC = "a"`) is a one-member `TyUnion` that codes 0 and emits the interned id today — only the arena SHAPE differed, and `tyIsLitUnionOrLit` (already written, for `emitStrToAtom`'s one-member narrowing) is the predicate that asks what the rep needs. `{kind: K1} | {kind: string}` (D1461): the STRING direction was recorded as needing "the mirror of every atom consumer written from scratch", and **three of the four were already built** — a declared INLINE set beside the same base is two code-3 rows, discriminable as laid out, and runs, so demoting the alias arm's row lands it exactly where a declared inline row sits — **while the fourth is not a mirror at all**: the field's read is already a string, and it is the ATOM-typed destinations that convert, through `strReppedLitUnionAt` → `emitStrToAtom`, one hook in `emitExpr` built for the flattened/inline family and blind to how the value got its string rep. **The alias does not get a rep the module does not use for it**, which was the standing objection: only the FIELD moves, and the disassembly shows one shared `(struct (field (mut (ref <the string struct>))) (field (mut f64)))` beside a `(func (param i32) (result i32))` for `takesK(k: K1): K1` with a real narrow tower at the call. **Two positions were not free and the matrices found both**: an array-literal element (`const xs: string[] = [b.kind]` off a promoted one-member field built the i32 backing into a string-list slot — `arrLitIsStr` reads the recorded element `"a"`, which `nodeArrayElemIsStr` and `nodeArrayElemIsLitUnion` both decline), and a shared-field read over the demoted pair (`shapeFieldTypeCompat` read a `K1` render against a code-3 row as a proven mismatch, so the arm's OWN render named no variant). **The message**: `… this program is type-valid but cannot build; spell both arms the same way` prescribed an edit that fixed NEITHER program it was shown to; over a 144-pair ordered grid of twelve discriminant spellings it now reaches nothing (**42 → 50 `runs`, 8 → 0 emit refusals, no check refusal moved**), so it is a floor that names the field and the two owners of the invariant (`checkUnionDiscriminable`, `unifyMixedLitRepArms`) and claims nothing about the user's program — validated against a control that must trigger it, a compiler built with `unionDiscrimMsgNamed` disabled. The refusal beside it IS live (`same-field-names-i32-vs-boolean-reject.vl`) and keeps its sentence. `--sites` **23 → 22**; capability probes **101/103 → 103/104**. Two 50-cell position matrices, both faces, every cell `emit refuses → RUNS` with 0 silent; the D1050 matrix re-runs 50/50; distilled corpus **0 classes of 255,504 cells**, rep-fuzz exact, mono grid 261/261 identical cell-by-cell. Fixtures `unions/discriminant-mixed-litunion-bare-literal-arm.vl` and `unions/discriminant-set-beside-base-alias-arm.vl` (the latter was the bound's `@emit-error` pin). DECISIONS.md §"a mixed-spelling variant field carries the ATOM".
- **An INFERRED anonymous struct whose field is a LIST of anonymous structs gets a row (D1443).** `const w = { f: [{ f: 1.5 }] }` was `emitProgram: ref valtype with no interned shape`: `collectAnonShapes` mints a row only when EVERY field value has a code, and `anonFieldCodeSyn`'s `ArrayLit` arm coded only NUMERIC-element lists, so an object-literal element fell to -1 and the OUTER literal got no row at all. The declared twin `type P = { f: { f: f64 }[] }` codes the field 5 (reflist) through `fieldCodeOfSpelling` and records the element name in `shapeFieldElemName`; `anonFieldElemName`'s new code-5 arm is that pair asked of the LITERAL, and supplying the companion column is what admits code 5 to the coder — the same bargain D1242's code 16 struck, and the one `anonCodeIsSelfContained`'s own header states. EVERY element must resolve to the SAME row: a heterogeneous list has no single element heap type, so it declines and keeps failing loudly. Position matrix **24 of 40 -> 40 of 40, 16 cells refuse -> RUNS, 0 runs lost, 0 silent**; the unused-`type`-alias rescue it replaces worked only for the OUTER shape, never the element or the element list.
- **AN UNBOUNDED `<T>` IS AN ENTIRELY OPEN HOLE, so the two spellings of one generic answer alike (owner ruling 2026-09-03; D1431, closing D1221 and D1004)** — `function g<T>(x: T): string { x.tag() }` was a check reject while its un-annotated twin `function g(x) { x.tag() }` compiled and ran. A member read on a parameter with no bound now mints the same `HD_FLD` derived hole the hole path mints and defers the check to each call, so both print `fld`; a bad instantiation refuses in the hole's own words, at the argument — `argument 1: expected {tag: _}, got {r: f64}` — byte-identical to what the un-annotated spelling already printed. The demand rides the deferred `memCstr` table, NOT the name-keyed hole-shape table, because two declarations may both spell their parameter `T` and a shared key would let one generic's demand refuse another's calls. A BOUNDED `<T: B>` is untouched (OQ-5 strict bodies stand, and a bound stays the stricter spelling); `tpMemberFloorMsg`'s remaining domain is an annotation that is NOT A BOUND — four sub-cases, three of which have members — and its sentence now says only that, leaving the rule to the instantiation's own diagnostic (the first narrowing said "is not a type with members", false of every field-member alias). `docs/constraints-design.md` §7.7 is the record.
- **AN UN-ANNOTATED PARAMETER IS A GENERIC TOO — a member call on one no longer lands on a `self`-function no instantiation can reach (D1430)** — `dispatchRewrite` read `fnTyParams.length == 0` as "not generic", so the question it asks a generic's call sites (does any instantiation carry this member as a FIELD?) was never asked for the hole spelling: `function g(x) { x.tag() }` beside a `tag(self: Circle)` for a type `g` is never called at was `vl check` rc 0 and invalid wasm. The parameter scan moved ahead of `tyHasTyVar` so the admission costs the fan-out nowhere else. Closed in the same change as D1431 and necessarily so — routing `<T>` onto a hole that miscompiles would have traded a loud refusal for a silent one.

- **THE FIVE-ROW RESIDUE D1180 FILED IS CLOSED, AND IT MEASURED AS FIVE MECHANISMS OFF ONE SHARED GUARD (D1290, D1291, D1292, D1293, D1294)** — an ablation that removes one rung at a time from the finished tree moves EXACTLY the row that rung belongs to, with one exception: `nulFieldInnerCode`'s two new entries (`28 -> 5`, `22 -> 14`) are needed by three of the five, which is the guard D1180 built doing the work it was built for. **D1291**'s recorded price still reproduces (`expected ref but found i32`) but its recorded MECHANISM does not — the disassembly puts the stray `ref.as_non_null` on an `i32` leaf field INSIDE the nested element compare, so `eqChainRecover` is a module global that outlived its chain; `emitListEqAnyRep` now saves, clears and restores it, because a list core starts a fresh chain. **D1292**'s price also still reproduces at both spellings, and the SECOND cause the row named (a non-null stash pair in `emitCloEqCore`) was not real: the frame scan alone closes both, so the arm spelling's different message was the same missing frame presenting differently — `shapeHasCloField` resolves a niche code before asking for code 14, the pairing `leqNoteBin` already had. **D1290** builds no new dispatch: `emitStructUnionEq` splits into `unionBoxEqColumns` (the admission gate, asked before a byte is written) and `emitUnionBoxEqStaged` (the tag-then-arm core over two boxes on the stack), which a code-16 FIELD reaches with two chain reads in both ladders. **D1293's filed axis was wrong** — ablated, the refusal fires on a program that only CONSTRUCTS the arm, so the compare is not an ingredient; it is `collectU` running before `collectS`, because `nameIsRefArray` resolves its element through the struct table while the non-null spelling's array arm ends in a table-free fall-through. Two rungs: the arena decides the code once every name arm has declined, and the code-28 element name is recorded DEFERRED like the shape-text recorder's. **D1294** is a construction gap — `emitVariantStruct`'s null-seed ladder carried every field code the struct literal's did except the nullable scalar-backed lists. Graded on a 15-rep × {struct, arm} × {annotated, inferred} × {same, diff, null, null-null} grid: **92 emit rejects → 0**, 86 → 178 `runs`, zero silent at either end; and on two new position matrices (`box-field-struct-eq`, `nul-ref-list-field-eq`) at 44/50 each, whose
six remaining reds ABLATE TO D1244 (a module-block capture reached by `==` instead of a field
read — a third message over one mechanism, recorded there rather than filed anew). D1311 is
new: the compare-frame pre-pass never recurses into a code-15 field, so a NESTED struct's `string[]` field is check-clean invalid wasm on master today.
- **FOUR NULLABLE-NICHE ROWS CLOSED, AND THEY MEASURED AS FOUR FAMILIES (D1197, D1181, D1114, D1180)** — each was fixed in turn and the other three re-graded UNMOVED before the next was touched, which is the evidence the one-family headline was wrong. **D1197**: `.push` was the one delivery of a narrowed nullable ref that never asked `nulNicheRecoverOwed`, so the value slot — a non-null `(ref $rlElemHeap)`, not the backing, which is nullable — received a `(ref null $H)`; `pushDestVKind` names that slot's rep from the element-kind code and hands it to the one question the eight sibling deliveries already ask. **The filed scope was one cell and the population is twenty**: a rep grid of 11 element reps × 2 faces graded 2/22 `runs` before and 22/22 after, so every ref rep was red there. **D1181**: `i64` and `f32` struct fields had no equality core while `emitVariantFieldEqCore` has carried both since D1096 — one arm now serves all three wide numeric widths and the two ladders agree field code for field code. **D1114**: a nested-struct field read through an `Arm | null` receiver had no layout, because an arm has no `sNames` row, `memIsNarrowed` is about `is`-narrowing rather than a null test, and the `exprVariantIndex` rung answers only for a NON-null variant; `structIndexOfExpr` grew the niche twin, resolving the field's TARGET row through `uFieldTgtStructIdx` (36-cell matrix 18 → 24 `runs`, 0 lost). **D1180 settled a CHECKER question first and the answer is that both spellings owe a compare** — see DECISIONS.md §"`T | null` is value-comparable exactly when `T` is"; the emitter half is ONE guard over the non-null twin's core rather than an arm per rep, and `nulFieldInnerCode` is simultaneously the mapping, the admission gate and the compare-frame pre-pass's key, so a niche can never get a guard with no core or a core with no frame. A 15-type × 2-spelling grid went 2 → 11 `runs` at the plain-struct spelling and 1 → 8 at the arm spelling with ZERO silent cells at either, and the widening exposed a PRE-EXISTING clause-1 trap on the way past: a code-15 field is `(ref null $S)` at both the `Inner` and the `Inner | null` spellings, so the recursion's `struct.get` died on a genuinely null field — that guard is now unconditional. The variant ladder also gained D101's i32-sentinel rung, which it never had, so `boolean | null` and `"a" | "b" | null` arm fields compare too. Residue measured and filed rather than left implicit: D1290 (the value-union box field), D1291/D1292 (the two ref niches whose guarded pair grades invalid wasm, held OUT of the table by measurement), D1293, D1294. `tests/cases/std/error-array-needle-not-equatable.vl`'s full-remedy-clause directive moved for the third time — onto a struct with a MAP field, whose refusal is a design rule and therefore cannot graduate out from under it.

- **AN ELSE-LESS `if` USED AS A VALUE IS `T | null` IN EVERY POSITION, AND LOWERS THERE — the 2×12 scope × rep grid goes 14/48 → 48/48 (D1086 closed, on the owner's ruling)** — the checker used to give TWO answers about one expression: `T | null` at a binding, `void` in return position and as a `??` operand, so nothing downstream could be right and the row was deliberately left open when nine of its ten siblings closed. **The checker rule is now ONE line, not a position table**: `checkIfStmtNode` returns `thenTy | null` whenever the then arm carries a value, and the statement half needs no gate of its own because a statement arm's `thenTy` is already `void` — the two position gates it replaces (`ifTail`, `ix == letInitIfIx`) are gone, and the change is shorter than what it replaced. **The emitter's synthesized else arm is the REP'S OWN NULL at the four value-`if` sinks**, written by `fbRefNullOfKind` — `fbValtypeNullable`'s VALUE twin, the same `match` over `VKind` arm for arm, so a cell's declaration and the null stored into it cannot name different heap types: `emitIfExprRef` writes `ref.null $ht` under a nullable blocktype, `emitUnionIfValue` the null-tagged box, `emitVariantIfValue` `ref.null $(uVarHeap[vi])`, and `emitIfExprAs` the NICHE SENTINEL (2 for `boolean | null`, −1 for a nullable literal union) while still refusing for a bare scalar, whose `T | null` rep is the box. **THE GRID WAS RE-MEASURED BEFORE ANY CODE WAS WRITTEN AND IT HAD MOVED**: master graded **14 of 48** cells running (12 reps × 2 scopes × annotated/inferred), not the row's filed 6 of 24 — `union` had started running at function scope under an unrelated merge, and a citation is a measurement with a date on it. **The nullable blocktype fixed a PRE-EXISTING SILENT CLASS on the way past**: `emitIfExprRef` asked `nodeTyIsNullableStruct`, the nullable question for ONE kind, so `if c { v } else { null }` at every other ref kind was check-clean invalid wasm (`expected (ref $type), found (ref null $type)`) — measured at `str`, `strlist`, `list` and `map`, at both scopes; it now asks `nodeTyIsNullable`, and the 144-program A/B against a `git archive origin/master` build records **8 silent → runs, 42 emit-reject → runs, 0 runs lost, 0 new silent**. **The UN-ANNOTATED face landed in a different clause, four for four with the week's other rows**: with the annotated half green, five composite reps still failed inferred and one of them SILENTLY — `const x = if c { mkList() }` classified an i32 local and the `if` pushed a `(ref null $lTypeIdx)` into it at `vl check` rc 0, because the annotation was pinning the rep; one rung per classifier in the `exprNullable*` family (`nulArmIfThenValueIx`: an `if` whose OTHER ARM IS NULL yields the then arm's rep made nullable) makes the two spellings agree — and it serves the absent arm and a bare `else { null }` alike, because they are the same value, taking the explicit-`else { null }` grid from **29 to 45 of 48** on the way. **A VOID ARM IS NOT A VALUE, and the exemption hiding that is gone**: `const x = if c { voidCall() }` was check-clean and crashed the emitter with `if-expression requires an else arm` — a sentence about the wrong ingredient, since an `else` does not give a void arm a value — and now draws the checker's own `cannot bind the void result of 'x'`. **Position matrix 20 of 21**, each cell constructing AND discriminating (taken proves 7, untaken proves −1): binding at both scopes, explicit `return`, return tail, argument, struct-field init, array element, local assignment, module-GLOBAL assignment (`emitAssign`'s `global.set` arm — D965's own missed delivery), map value, nested element, closure result; negative controls hold, with an else-less `if` as a CONDITION still `if-condition must be boolean, got boolean | null` and statement position still `void` (pinned by its own must-RUN fixture, because the next change to "fix" it into a value would break every void-tail body). Distilled corpus **0 classes moved of 255,504 cells**, filed witnesses 484 graded · 484 as filed · 0 MOVED, capability probes 70/84 → 72/85 (both `if-expr-no-else-*` probes GAP → RUNS, one new probe for the residue). The one residue is **D1250**: `??` over an if-expression written IN PLACE, which refuses at the explicit-`else` spelling too — a `??` defect this ruling only made reachable, ablated to "the arm reads `unionNameOfExpr` of the `??` NODE, whose checked type is the coalesced scalar". Fixtures: `tests/cases/types/if-expression-no-else-scope-rep-grid.vl` (96 cells), `…/if-expression-no-else-value-positions.vl`, `…/if-expression-no-else-statement-position.vl`. DECISIONS.md §"An else-less `if` used as a VALUE is `T | null` in every position".

- **A CODED DIAGNOSTIC'S PAYLOAD RIDES A REAL DATA CHANNEL — the `code` is a bare CATEGORY again** — D1230's answer shipped PACKED INTO THE CODE (`ufcs-not-imported;member=toEqual;modules=std:test;recv=Expectation<i32>`) because the diagnostic ABI had one string channel, and the cost is the shape of the mistake rather than a bug: **every consumer owed a `diagCategory(code)` cut at the first `;` before it could compare a code at all** — an `===` against `ufcs-not-imported` silently stops matching the day a payload is added, which is exactly what happened — and the framing lived in the VALUES (`recv=` had to be last, `modules=` needed specifiers holding no `,`, each new field another character some value must never contain). `TDiag` now carries **`tdata`**, exported as **`diagDataLen`/`diagDataByte`** beside the code pair (`typecheck` -> `driver` -> `entry`), read by `wasmChecker.ts` into **`VLDiagnostic.data`** and decoded once by `compiler/diagnostics.ts` `decodeDiagData`. The wire format is netstrings — `<byte-length> ":" <bytes> ","` — read as alternating KEY and VALUE, so the length is authoritative and a value may hold ANY byte with nothing escaped and no field order to preserve; **a repeated key is a LIST**, which is how `modules` carries every candidate without a `,`-joined value to re-split. The length is a UTF-8 BYTE count, which is why the decoder takes bytes and not a string: `{a: i32, tag: "a;b,c|d" | "éè"}` is 31 JS characters and 33 bytes, and it round-trips exactly (the round-trip witness carries `;`, `,`, `|`, `"` and non-ASCII at once). A malformed payload decodes to `{}` and never a partial read — half an answer would write an import from a module the compiler never named. **`diagCategory` stays as a tolerant reader that nothing depends on**, kept because the mistake is cheap to make again. Two things fell out: the quick-fix stopped re-running `ufcsCandidatesAt` per lightbulb and converting module KEYS back to specifiers in the host — the compiler decided both at the raise — so **`onCodeAction` is synchronous**; and the Rust host needed no change at all, because it never read the code channel either (verified: the unchanged binary against the new seed prints the same sentence and the same `--json`). `--json` still omits both code and payload for a COMPILE diagnostic, deliberately (`compiler/cli.vl`): the payload is an editor's answer and the fix is an edit no batch reporter performs. Emitted wasm is unaffected; the seed gains two exports and the fixpoint holds byte-identical. (`tests/selfhost_native_diag_code_test.ts`, `tests/lsp_ufcs_import_test.ts`; DECISIONS.md §"A diagnostic code is a bare CATEGORY")

- **AN UN-EXPORTED `self`-FUNCTION IS NO LONGER CALLABLE FROM ANOTHER MODULE (D1191)** — `x.f(…)` resolves `f` only against names IN SCOPE (DECISIONS.md §"UFCS is never implicit"), and the merge's plain→mangled alias table was keyed by NAME and global to the whole program: any module spelling `b.hidden()` banked `hidden → hidden$mN`, and every other module's `b.hidden()` — having no per-site row of its own — fell through to that map and COMPILED, calling a function it never imported and could not name directly (`hidden(b)` was `undeclared identifier` in the same file). D1120 built the per-call-site table for the two-module ambiguity and left the fallback answering callers that should get nothing. Measured before deleting it: over `tests/cases` + `std/` (2,684 programs) and the compiler's own 26-module source through check AND emit, the member-call fallback changed the answer **0 times** and the generic-bound reader (`witnessOf`) **3 times, all in one file, on a name that file imports**. So the name-keyed map is gone and what replaces it is the merge's own per-module scope — `ufcsScope*`, one row per (module, plain name) the module binds to a `self`-function, walked out of the rename map `modBuildRename` already computes (declarations, then each import local, alias included), with `ufcsModBound` mapping a node back to its module. `ufcsAliasAtSite` is now the site's own row else the CALLER's module scope; `witnessOf` resolves in the PIN's, which is what its refusal already claimed. A `not-runs → runs` fell out: `modSelfFnTarget` asked `modRenamed`, which consults the lexical SHADOW stack, so a `const shown = 5` in the calling function made an IMPORTED `b.shown()` refuse — a property is not a value reference, and module scope has no shadow stack. Native fixpoint byte-identical at both bootstrap levels; `regress.py` 0 of 255,504 cells moved. (`tests/cases/modules/ufcs-unexported-not-callable/`, `ufcs-unexported-third-module/`, `ufcs-unexported-bound-witness/`, `ufcs-import-shadowed-local/`)

- **A UFCS METHOD WHOSE FREE FUNCTION IS EXPORTED BUT NOT IMPORTED NAMES THE MISSING IMPORT (D1230/D1230)** — `import { expect } from "std:test"` + `expect(1 + 1).toEqual(2)` was refused `no field 'toEqual' on Expectation<i32>`: true, permanent, and useless, because UFCS is EXPLICIT by ruling (DECISIONS.md §"UFCS is never implicit") and `Expectation<i32>` will never grow that field. The program stays illegal; the SENTENCE now says why — ``'toEqual' is not imported — a free `toEqual(self: …)` accepting Expectation<i32> is exported by "std:test"; a UFCS call resolves only names in scope, so import `toEqual` from there``. The quick-fix's whole answer travels in machine form so no consumer parses English: the code is the bare category `ufcs-not-imported` and the member, the candidate modules and the receiver ride the DATA channel beside it (see the entry above; it shipped packed into the code and was moved the same day). ONE diagnostic lists every candidate module. The merge already knew every module's exported free `self`-functions (`modCollectSelfFns`); what is new is a registry carrying them across the phase boundary (`ast.ufcsImp*`) and `ufcsWouldDispatch`, which mirrors `ufcsCallTy`'s GATE arm for arm — lookup, `self`-name rule, arity RANGE, `assignable(recvTy, params[0])` — and deliberately nothing after it, since it runs speculatively over every same-named candidate. Scoped by what a quick-fix can correctly WRITE: the file's own import text, or a `std:` key (absolute from every file); a relative module the file does not import, an un-exported self-function, and a same-file out-of-scope one all keep the plain sentence. (`tests/cases/modules/ufcs-not-imported*/`, `tests/cases/strings/ufcs-no-such-method-control.vl`, `tests/cases/objects/ufcs-nested-self-fn-out-of-scope.vl`, `tests/selfhost_native_diag_code_test.ts`)
- **DEEP `is` OVER A `Json` VALUE — `r is string[]` / `r is Cfg` is now a runtime SHAPE WALK plus a conversion, and D1035 is closed** — `is` over a union was an arm-membership TAG test, so a refinement of an arm (`["xyz"] is string[]`) was check-clean and answered `false` for every value, and a struct on the right (`r is Cfg`) was refused as "not a variant of Json". Both halves are one build: the checker decides which sites are deep (`jsonUnionRootOf` resolves the canonical `Json` a receiver is a VIEW of — a complement narrowing after `if r is boolean` is still a `Json` tree — and `jsonShapeBad` says whether the target has a JSON shape), and `driver.jwSecondPass` generates one `__vlJsonIs_<k>` + `__vlJsonGet_<k>` pair per distinct target as ordinary **VL source**, parses that fragment onto the same token stream and arena, appends its declarations to the program root, rewrites each site into a call, and re-checks. **Nothing in `wasmEmit.vl` learned a rep and no delivery position had to be wired**, because the arm's binding is an ordinary local of the target type — D965's rule met by construction rather than by a nine-cell matrix. S1 (the arm binds one converted COPY; mutating it does not write back to the tree), S2 (an integer target matches iff integral and in range — the walk asks `v as? i32`, so it IS the exact-or-fail numeric rule) and S3 (RULED: an ABSENT key matches a `T | null` field as `null`) all hold, at both the annotated and the un-annotated spelling of every cell. The 11-position × 13-target matrix runs: `if` / `while` / `&&` / `!` / `else if` / a closure body, over a struct field, an index, a call result and a map read; `string[]`, `i32[]`, `f64[]`, `Cfg`, `Cfg[]`, `{[string]: i32}`, `{items: Item[], total: f64}`, `Cfg | null`, a `string | null` field, a `Json`-typed field. **Memoised on (target, receiver)**: two `is Cfg` sites emit ONE pair, pinned by a function-count differential in `tests/vl_deep_is_walker_test.ts`. **A program with no deep `is` pays nothing** — the second pass returns on its first line, and five control programs emit byte-identical modules before and after. Refusals name the offending component of `T` (a closure field, a non-string map key, a newtype brand, an ambiguous union of shapes rendered structurally). **The receiver may be WIDER than the tree**, which is what makes the design's own example work: `const doc = text.parseJson()` is a `Json | JsonError`, so the walker's PARAMETER is the receiver's type (a `Json | JsonError` is not assignable to `Json`) while the shape predicate and the arm spellings are read from the tree — and an arm of the receiver stays a TAG test, so a JSON-shaped type that is also an arm is discriminated rather than walked. A MODULE build needed one thing more, and only a witness found it: the merge renames `Json` → `Json$m1` and `$` is not an identifier character, so handing the lexer that render was forty parse errors on a program that had compiled the day before — the generator writes a lexable stand-in and the driver restores the `$` ON THE TOKEN STREAM before the fragment parses, which is what keeps `TypeRef.tyName` and the annotation spelling tree from drifting (`tests/cases/std/json-deep-is-parse-result.vl`). Two faces the first cut did not grade were found by review and fixed before merge, both somewhere the two-faces rule had not been applied: the ENCLOSING FUNCTION'S RETURN (an un-annotated return is checked twice, so one `is` was recorded twice and the second worklist row met a node the first had already rewritten — `internal: deep \`is\` site is not an \`is\` expression` on a program whose annotated twin ran; the worklist is now deduped by node index), and the COMPLEMENT VIEW after an earlier guard, which has TWO PRODUCERS and is why the first cut looked fixed and was not (`applyNarrows` installs the else-arm / `while`-body / match-arm / `&&`-conjunct complement and banks the shadowed declaration; the POST-GUARD FALL-THROUGH — `if r is JsonError { return }`, the shape a std:json consumer writes first — narrows the rest of the block with a bare `declare` and banked nothing, as does the `else if` chain hand-up. Both bank under a third kind, `NAR_KIND_POSTGUARD`, so `narGuardSlot`'s retirement and the dead-`??` reader see exactly the rows they saw before; and the reader takes the OUTERMOST banked row, because `narDeclaredTy` answers the innermost — already-narrowed once two guards stack — and "most union members" is backwards, `Json | JsonError` having two members against its flattened complement's seven). **Cost, and it needed one more control than it looked like**: `vl check` best-of-12 on a shared box reads 10 ms with no deep `is`, 23 ms with one (one top-level function, `Json` only), 41 ms with one more declared type — and **10 ms again once any second, unrelated top-level function is added**. So the added cost does not track the number of deep `is` sites (four sites / three targets measured 14 ms) and is not simply the second check pass: it is a shape sensitivity a one-function program exposes. On a file with more than one function the measured cost is ~0–4 ms; the worst reading is +31 ms on a five-line single-function file; a file with no deep `is` pays nothing. Two positions match the language rather than extending it: a `while` condition gives the boolean and no binding (`checkWhileStmt` carries only null strips into a loop body), and so does a call-result receiver. The `as` trio (S4) is NOT built and is the remainder in `ROADMAP.md`. Priced and named: a deep `is` arm that rebinds or writes the tested place is now a loud refusal positioned at the `is` site where master ran it and printed the wrong answer (**D1190**), a recursive shape target is refused because the generator inlines each level (**D1198**), and `.push` dropping the non-null recovery for a narrowed nullable ref (**D1197**, the only red cell of nine positions) is why the walker is a PAIR rather than one `T | null` function. `docs/serde-design.md` §"WHAT WAS BUILT"; DECISIONS.md §"Deep `is` over a `Json` value is a SHAPE WALK".

- **A UNION MINTED AT A GENERIC PIN IS REGISTERED, AND A LITERAL `is` NARROWS BOTH BRANCHES (D1042 and D1193 closed)** — `orErr<T>(x: T, bad: boolean): T | "err"` at `T = i32` was `vl check` rc 0 and `emitProgram: union box atom test on a union with no recorded members: i32|"err"`, and the same union spelled directly ran. **The mechanism was a chain of two, and the fix has to close both at once or it ships a different sentence.** (1) `collectU` is the only pass that mints a union row and the pass table orders it BEFORE `monomorphize`, so a union that exists only because a generic was pinned had no row under ANY spelling — `unionRowOf` read -1 for `i32|"err"` and for `i32|string` alike. (2) The two producers SPELL ONE UNION TWO WAYS: `monoSubstAnn` substitutes into the DECLARED annotation text and asks for `i32|"err"` with the literal verbatim, while every source annotation has been through `canonEmitTypeNames`, which softens a literal member to its base scalar at `RC_ROOT` — so the direct `function f(bad: boolean): i32 | "err"` registers `i32|string`, and adding it to the same module did NOT rescue the generic. `monoMakeInstance` already substitutes the return annotation per instance, so the registration goes THERE, rendered through `canonEmitName` first: the clone's key IS the direct spelling's key, `registerInlineUnion`'s `isUName` gate then REUSES the existing row rather than minting a second one (a union's box tags are positional over its member set, so two rows for one type is a value boxed under one tag slice and read under the other), and `assignTags()` re-runs only when the registration pushed a variant. **The row's own note that there is no per-instance return NODE described the CALLBACK clone (`name$cbN`), not the generic one.** **And closing the registry alone would have shipped loud → silent at seven of nine delivery positions**, which is how **D1193** was found: `if r is "err"` over `i32 | "err"` narrows NEITHER branch in the emitter — the else complement looks for a member spelled `"err"` in the softened `i32|string` and subtracts nothing, the then push banks a bare `TyLit` that `tyIsLitUnion`'s `TyUnion` test declined — so every position that READ the narrowed value (`r * 2`, `b.r`, a re-bind) was check-clean invalid wasm, at the direct and annotated spellings too, with `const r: i32 | "err" = 21` as a two-line witness and no generic anywhere. `print(r)` masked it by dispatching on the box tag. The complement is now asked of the DECLARED ARENA type, which is the only place the literal survives — remove the member whose own lexeme is the tested literal, narrow only when exactly one survives, render the survivor as its consumer resolves it — and that rule is the CHECKER's arm for arm: `"a" | "b" | i32` minus `"a"` leaves two and pushes nothing, `i32 | string` matches no lexeme and pushes nothing (and the checker rejects its else-branch arithmetic anyway, the control proving the language never narrowed there). **Graded on 46 cells against a `git archive origin/master` build: 30 not-runs → RUNS, 0 runs → not-runs, 0 → silent.** The delivery matrix runs whole — binding, argument, struct field, array element, module global, global-to-global assignment, an `f64` pin, a `Circle` pin, one generic pinned twice with no cross-talk, and the direct spelling beside the pin in one module. Distilled corpus 0 classes moved; capability probes 63/77 → 65/77 (two new probes, one per row). The one residue is filed as **D1194**: an INFERRED return that takes its union from a callee's declared `i32 | "err"` is still a loud check reject conceding codegen, while the plain-`string` twin and the annotated twin both run.

- **A UNION WHOSE TWO ARMS SPELL THEIR LITERAL DISCRIMINANT DIFFERENTLY NOW BUILDS — the mixed field is laid out under ONE rep, the interned ATOM (D1050 closed)** — `type K1 = "circle" | "round"` in one arm beside an inline `"x" | "y"` in the other is legal by D1023's ruling and the checker always accepted it; the emitter refused, because a registered litunion ALIAS reps as the interned `i32` atom and an inline set as a `(ref $string)`, so the two arms had no single heap type to share. **The wasm is the check that this is a rep change and not a relaxed gate**: master emitted two struct types for the pair and could fold neither, the candidate emits one — `(type $0 (struct (field (mut i32)) (field (mut f64))))`, `kind` the interned id in BOTH arms. `unifyMixedLitRepArms` runs at the end of `collectS`, where both field tables are complete, and rewrites the string-coded row's CODE and its D5 arena sidecar in the variant table AND in the arm's declared struct row — moving only the first gives one declaration two heap types and any value crossing between them is a module the engine refuses. **The atom side was chosen by measurement, not preference**: its four conversion sites are already built (`emitDiscrimFieldEq`'s code-0 compare, `emitVariantStruct`'s `variantFieldIsLitUnion` construct intern, `exprIsLitAtom`'s member-read claim, `emitAtomToStr`'s widen back), so the unification costs no new lowering; the string side would need all four written from scratch for the alias arm. **And the "rep cliff" was smaller than its name** — D1023 stopped here because closing it "means unifying the two litunion reps", assumed to be a whole-tree change; scoped to the arms of a mixed pair it moves **0 classes of 255,504 corpus cells** and the candidate compiler emits master's OWN source byte-identically, so the global unification (design β) stays unbuilt and unneeded. `assignTags` — one pass before the struct table exists — ADMITS on the acting pass's own predicate (`variantLitRepUnifiable`), while `variantLitDiscriminable` keeps asking the strict question `buildVariantTwins` needs after the re-lay; both are arms of one walk so the three answers cannot drift. **The bound is `tyIsLitUnion` on both arms and keeps two legal pairs refused on purpose**: `{kind: K1} | {kind: string}` (the base arm holds an arbitrary string with no interned id) and `{kind: K1} | {kind: "a"}` (a bare `TyLit`, which the read classifier does not treat as a litunion) — so `--sites` stays at **22** literals, correctly, the site having narrowed rather than cleared, while the probe runner moves 63/75 → 64/76. A 48-cell matrix over spelling (alias/inline/inverse/three-arm), delivery position (binding, return, argument, struct field, array element, module global, `Map` value, concatenation) and BOTH annotated and un-annotated faces goes **9 → 42 `runs`**, each row printing the member TEXT so an atom leaking as its raw id would show. Zero `runs` lost, `regress.py` 0 classes moved and 0 into silent, rep-fuzz exact, native fixpoint holds, filed witnesses 470 graded · 470 as filed · 0 MOVED · 0 not graded. **Two residue rows, and one of them was already master's**: D1195 (a NARROWED arm delivered to a param annotated with the arm's own inline SHAPE mints a second heap type — check-clean invalid wasm on master at BOTH same-rep spellings, so D1050's refusal was a loud FLOOR standing over an older defect) and D1196 (the ANNOTATED rebind off a promoted field, `only i32 locals are supported`; the one-line classifier fix was built and REFUSED because it trades that loud reject for check-clean invalid wasm — the reservation scan does not see the new atom slot). Fixtures: `tests/cases/unions/discriminant-mixed-litunion-spelling.vl` and `…/error-discriminant-mixed-rep-no-atom.vl` (the bound, pinned as an `@emit-error`). DECISIONS.md §"a mixed-spelling variant field carries the ATOM".
- **`std:json` DROPS ITS FLAT-FIELD ERROR CARRIER — both carriers are now one `err: JsonError | null`, and `parseJson` returns the object the scanner raised (D1031 closed in #2385)** — the module carried its scanner's and its renderer's failure as four and three FLAT fields plus a `live` flag, because a struct field typed at a type that is a union ARM elsewhere in the program was a loud emit reject and `JsonError` is an arm of both public return types. #2385's D1093/D1094 fixes closed that, so `Scan` loses `live`/`at`/`kind`/`path`/`msg` for one `err`, `Rend` becomes `{ err: JsonError | null }`, `raise`/`rendFail` build the error once, and `parseJson`/`toJson` hand back the same object instead of copying four fields into a fresh one. **No exported name, signature or documented behaviour moves** — the 7 `tests/vl_std_json_test.ts` suites pass unchanged, and a 32-case error-surface oracle (all four kinds, every pointer shape including `/users/1`, `/0/0`, `/a~1b`, the three 128-segment cycle paths, the render side's always-zero `at`) prints BYTE-IDENTICAL output under master's std and this one on one seed. **Every read of `err` narrows IN PLACE (`if p.err != null { … p.err … }`) and never through a rebind, and that is measured**: a position × spelling matrix over the four positions the module needs found NO working rebind — an ANNOTATED rebind is a loud emit reject wherever the narrowed value is a field-ASSIGNMENT receiver (**D1161**, filed here with an eight-row ablation: it needs the arm-membership, the annotation and the assignment; a read runs) and an UN-ANNOTATED one is check-clean invalid wasm wherever it is RETURNED into `Json | JsonError` / `string | JsonError` (D1112). The matrix is in the module header because the compiler ACTIVELY suggests the refused annotated spelling with a `redundant type annotation` hint. **The std review also turned the `kind` deviation right way round**: the reason `kind` stays an inline literal set is NOT that a private `JsonErrorKind` alias refuses — a std copy with the alias at all five sites builds and answers all 32 cases identically — but that against that std a CALLER rebinding at the module's own documented spelling is `vl check` rc 0 then `emitProgram: map key is not a string`, so the alias moves D1050's rep split to the module boundary; the plain two-rep reduction RUNS, so the mechanism is recorded as a prediction and the measurement is what the choice rests on.
