The error's single allocation MOVED from the return to the raise; it did not appear.
- **A `type` DECLARED IN A FUNCTION BODY IS LEXICALLY SCOPED (D1045 + D1046, #2391)** — ruled legal by the owner on 2026-09-02 and built the same day; the interim loud refusal (#2369) is removed with it. Every declaration form the grammar admits is admitted in a body — struct, union, literal union, recursive, generic alias, nominal `new`, `flat` — scoped to the block, shadowing outer names, and free to name the enclosing function's type parameters. **The mechanism is the MODULE MERGE'S, one scope in, and that was the design decision.** A type name here is answered by more than one producer (the checker's `cUserTypes`, canon's rendered spelling, the emitter's per-name tables), so a scope CHAIN in the checker would have them agreeing about the TYPE and disagreeing about the REP; the merge already faced the identical problem — two modules may each declare a `Pair` — and answered it by renaming, which `tyToStr`'s own header states as `Pair$m1` and `Pair` being different types to the tables that hold them. Two FUNCTIONS may each declare a `P`, so: the parser mints the declaration under a unique name (`P` → `P$b7`), spells every reference in its lexical extent at that name, and HOISTS the node into `progStmts` — measured to be sufficient because the checker's passes 0a–0d and every emitter registry build (`collectS`, `collectU`, `gaeCollectDecls`, `resolveFlatLayouts`, …) read `root.progStmts` and only that. In the PARSER because recursive descent is lexical by construction, and `parseTypeAtom`'s IDENT arm is the ONE substitution site every type-position name reaches, so the coverage is a property of the grammar rather than of a list of positions. TYPE-PARAMETER CAPTURE IS A GENERIC ALIAS: `type P = {a: T}` in `f<T>` becomes `type P$b7<T>`, reusing the substitution a module-scope `Pair<A>` applied at a type parameter already performs (measured to run at two pins before the build began). Only MENTIONED parameters are captured, decided by a bounded token lookahead — the answer is needed before the body is parsed so a recursive `type N = { next: N | null }` spells itself at the right arity, and capturing unconditionally was refused because a local `type Id = new i32` in a generic body would become a generic newtype and silently stop being nominal. THE NOMINAL-ESCAPE ERROR (the owner's sub-ruling) at three spellings — explicit `return`, implicit trailing expression, and a nominal buried in the inferred type (a returned closure `() => Id`, which is why the escape predicate descends a `TyFunc` where its `nodeTyHasRepTyVar` sibling does not); the other two escape positions were TESTED and need no rule, since an outer container is already refused by nominal distinctness and a local structural type escapes as its shape. THE DECLARATION IS REACHABLE TWICE (its lexical position and `progStmts`) and both consumers that must not double-count it were found by RUNNING them: `vl fmt` printed a stray second copy of the declaration at the end of the file, and the module merge would have renamed an already-mangled name's `P` segment with the enclosing type parameters unshadowed. `vl fmt` also prints three names from the NODE — an `Ident`, an `is` check-type, an `as` target — so `TV$b1.size` and `11 as Id$b1` made `vl fmt` fail outright on a legal program; demangled there, with the scan given one home in the zero-import leaf. **D1046 closes with it**, and was under-filed: a nested NAMED `function` naming the enclosing `T` was one loud emit reject and TWO check-clean invalid-wasm spellings (a return-only `T`, and a concrete signature capturing a `T`-typed local — D943's defect at the named spelling), none reachable by narrowing `checkParams`, which reads parameters only. `monoPinBodyLambdas` gains the `FuncDecl` statement arm it never had; the clone keeps its source name because a named function is reached BY NAME through the frame chain, and the first instance REPLACES the template's slot because that lookup takes the first child of a frame. `fnName != ""` is NOT the test for "named" — `collectFns` rewrites an anonymous lambda to `__lambda_N` before monomorphize runs — and reading it as one cost a `runs` (a capture-only lambda), which is why the slot lookup now has one home. Zero `runs` lost, distilled corpus unmoved, rep-fuzz exact, filed witnesses 451/451 before and after. `types/body-scope-type-decl-{shadows-module,forms,positions}.vl`, `types/body-scope-local-struct-escapes.vl`, `types/error-body-scope-nominal-escapes-return.vl`, `generics/nested-named-fn-names-enclosing-typaram.vl`, and a `vl fmt` round-trip.
- **THE RULING'S SECOND HINT — `is <literal>` OVER A COLLAPSED OPERAND (#2404)** — the subsumed-arm ruling asked for two non-blocking hints and only the first arrived free (`string | "err"` now infers as `string`, so the existing redundant-annotation hint fires at the written spelling). The second fires at the `is` DOWNSTREAM of the collapse, which is where the loss bites: `r is "err"` over a collapsed `R = string | "err"` is a value compare (`==`) and cannot tell a failure from a `string` that happens to read "err". **It cannot be derived from the type, and that is the whole design problem**: after the collapse the operand IS a `string` — the canonical arena singleton, the canon spelling `string` — so a rule reading the arena, canon, or the rendered message would fire on every legitimate `s is "err"` in the language. So the COLLAPSE records it. The annotation route banks the arena index it collapsed TO (`collapsedTy`, a third bank on `unkTyPart`'s wire: cleared by the outermost `tsToTy`/`nameToTy` frame, restored across `resolveAnnotTs`'s name memo exactly as `annotPart` is — without that restore the pass-1 signature hoist consumes the only un-memoized resolution and every annotation site afterwards reads "no collapse"); the DECLARATION route banks the alias NAME (`collapsedAliases`), re-banked by `declaredTyOfName`, the one door every declared-type reference comes through. A `let`, a parameter and a declared RETURN each compare their OWN resolved type against the bank — so `(string | "err")[]` marks nothing — and an un-annotated `const r = f(…)` inherits from the callee's decl node, marked in the PASS-1 HOIST so the program's statement order does not decide it. Marks are depth-tagged sparse rows dropped by `popScope` and paired with `lookupDepth` at the read, which is what makes an inner plain `const r: string` shadowing an outer collapsed `r` silent while recording nothing itself. **The generic-instantiation decline the ruling asked for is structural, not a special case**: substitution mints its collapsed union on the THIRD union-construction route (`substTyDeep`), which banks nothing, so `orErr<Json>` cannot reach the hint at all. Graded BEFORE/AFTER against a pristine `origin/master` seed on 18 programs — 11 fire, 7 do not, and **every emitted module is byte-identical** (a hint changes no codegen). Exactly ONE existing fixture began firing it (`is-numeric-litunion-membership.vl`'s bare-literal control, whose `K | i32` annotation is load-bearing): the hints are DECLARED, not silenced by deleting the annotation. Neither `compiler/*.vl` nor `std/*.vl` fires it. Non-blocking `hint`, code `collapsed-arm-value-test`, third member of the type-informed finding family beside `redun*` and `rcoal*`. `DECISIONS.md` §"A subsumed literal arm COLLAPSES" (2026-09-02 note, #2404).
- **THE RULING'S MIRROR HALF — `Kind | string` IS `string`, AND IT TOOK TWO PRODUCERS (D1048)** — the litunion-beside-its-base collapse D1024 deliberately deferred, closed by moving the ARENA and CANON together: `homogLitUnionBase` inside `armLiteralBaseTy` so a homogeneous literal UNION arm reports its base exactly as a bare literal arm already did (all three union-construction sites reach it through the shared `unionDropSubsumedArms`, no call site changed), plus `canonDropSubsumedParts` at the TOP of `canonEmitNameTs`'s union arm — ahead of `nulLitUnionPreserve` / `litUnionPreserve` / `mixedUnionLitAliasRegroup`, mirroring where `annUnionInnerTy` puts the collapse, and re-entering on the survivors as that function does. **Each half alone is a `runs → not-runs` veto, measured in both directions on the row's two named fixtures**: arena-only leaves `is-litunion-arm-non-ident-receivers.vl` refusing `struct field type \`K|string|i32\` has no struct-field rep` and `mixed-union-litunion-arm-is-membership.vl` check-clean invalid wasm; canon-only leaves the first refusing `only i32 locals are supported`, the second invalid wasm, **and `x is Kind` answering a silent TRUE for the non-member `"zz"`** — the #1306 wrong answer arriving from the other side. **The third prescribed step was already built and measuring it first retired it**: `is Kind` over a COLLAPSED `string` base is already `emitIs`'s membership ladder, verified on master before any edit by hand-writing both fixtures in the spelling the collapse produces — 20 of 20 correct, the `string | i32` box and the `string | null` niche included. **Only the string-litunion arm needed an explicit canon rule, and that is luck not design**: canon's render already softens a bare literal and a NUMERIC litunion alias (`numLitUnionAliasName`) and its atom dedup then collapses `string|string` / `i32|i32`, so those agreed with the arena BY ACCIDENT — which is exactly why D1024's half needed no canon change. Position matrix, 42 cells, one program per delivery position: **34/42 → 42/42**, closing the parameter (offset 254), a module global, a `+` operand, a generic pin's return, `+` over two `(Kind|string)` elements — and the two NUMERIC controls `N | i32` / `F | f64`, which failed with `union box atom test on a union with no recorded members` because the same disagreement ran the OTHER way there, and which nothing had filed. The un-annotated spellings ran before and still run, so inference was never the ingredient. Named set kept whole and green with byte-identical output; their annotations are redundant BY THE RULING and are `@hint`-declared rather than deleted. `DECISIONS.md` §"A subsumed literal arm COLLAPSES" (2026-09-02 note).

- **A FAILED ASSERTION IS LOCATED AT THE MATCHER, NOT AT `expect` — and with the leading-dot chain shipped, the LINE moves and not just the column (#2386)** — the owner's 2026-09-02 ruling, built the same day, **std-side only**: each `std:test` matcher (`toEqual`, `toBeTrue`, `toBeFalse`) takes a trailing `caller: CallerLoc = __callsite__`, the receipt drops the `caller` it carried from `expect`, and `expect` drops the parameter. The failure is the matcher's — `toEqual` is the thing that decided `false` — and on `expect(build(cfg))` ⏎ `  .toEqual(want)` the `expect` line is SETUP and the `.toEqual` line is the assertion, which is where Jest and Vitest point for the same reason. **Both blockers were gone before it started**: D1044 (a UFCS call omitting a defaulted tail argument, i.e. every matcher call in every test file) closed in #2371, and the leading-dot chain continuation shipped in #2382 — so the ruling's "until the grammar lands, only the COLUMN moves" was already stale when it was built. **The one open choice was the FORWARDING SURFACE, and it moved with the anchor**: the ruling said the receipt drops `expect`'s `caller` but not whether `expect(v, caller)` should survive as a wrapper's hand-in. It did not — two places to hand in ONE location need a precedence rule between them, and every available answer is bad (a forwarded `expect(v, caller)` losing silently to the matcher's own filled default is the worst), so the one-hop pattern is now `expect(v).toEqual(1, caller)`: one hop, still explicit, still ordinary code. `not()` takes NO caller and needs none — it decides nothing, so the FINAL matcher reports (measured, not assumed). **Graded on a twelve-row position grid with every expected column DERIVED from the source rather than counted by hand**: a one-line `expect(x).toEqual(y)` at column 5 → the `toEqual` at **col 15**; `expect(x).not().toEqual(y)` → the final `toEqual`; the two-line spelling → the `.toEqual` LINE; `toBeTrue`/`toBeFalse` at both spellings → their own tokens; a helper forwarding its own `caller` → the helper's CALLER, one that does not → its own matcher in its own FILE; a PASSING assertion → no location at all. **The ruling's own "column 14" was off by one** — that is the DOT's column, and the anchor is the method-name token after it; the arithmetic slipped in the prose, not in the compiler, and it is corrected where it was written. **Cost re-measured both ways with `VL_STD` pinned on both arms**, to the standard the track-caller entry set: ten million passing `expect(7).toEqual(7)` run 0.42–0.43 s anchored at `expect` and 0.41–0.45 s anchored at the matcher, i.e. inside the noise — one `struct.new` either way, just at a different call — and size went **DOWN 10 bytes** unoptimized on a one-assertion module (6,353 → 6,343: the receipt lost a field and `not` lost a copy), **byte-identical at `-O3`** (`cmp`, not `ls -l`: 416 bytes both ways). The assertion SENTENCE is untouched, so every message pin stayed a prefix match and only the two position pins moved. `testDiscovery.ts`'s wire format is unchanged — only its doc comment, which named the `expect` token as the anchor and was thereby false. **std-api review: approve-with-changes, every finding documentation, nothing in the code changed** — and two of them changed the argument rather than the prose. The header's "no honest answer for which wins" reads as taste; the truth is stronger, because the obvious precedence rule (*an explicit `expect` caller beats a default-filled matcher caller*) is **UNWRITABLE** under defaults v1 — a default is filled AT THE CALL in the caller's frame, so a callee cannot tell a supplied argument from an omitted one, which is DECISIONS §"Default arguments v1"'s own ABI finding read one consumer later. And the track-caller ruling's supersession banner sat 80 lines below its own heading, so a reader grepping `CallerLoc` met the superseded signature as current fact — the repo's "claims about the tree" failure, committed by the PR creating the staleness; the banner now leads the entry. Two measurement corrections it forced: the 2026-09-01 and 2026-09-02 SIZE paragraphs quote absolutes from different seed-days and different programs, so only their DELTAS compare (596 vs 416 reads as a 30% regression otherwise), and the `wasm-opt --closed-world -O3 --gufa -O3` command the header recorded **refuses this tree's output** without `--all-features` (`all used types should be allowed`) — the numbers came from `vl build -O3`, which is what is named now. The review also noted the repetition the move costs (a helper making N assertions repeats `, caller` N times) and that it is safe by construction rather than convention: `vltFail`'s `loc` stays REQUIRED, so a fourth matcher physically cannot report without a location. (`std/test.vl` header §`CallerLoc`, DECISIONS.md §"A failed assertion is located at the MATCHER, not at `expect`")
- **FIELD PRECEDENCE IS THE CHECKER'S PREDICATE IN EVERY SCOPE, AND A UFCS ALIAS BELONGS TO ITS CALL SITE (D1070 + D1120 closed as `runs`)** — **two mechanisms, two fixes, measured in both directions**: a compiler carrying only the D1070 half leaves all four of D1120's witnesses refused with their original messages, and a compiler carrying only the D1120 half grades D1070's 51-cell grid byte-for-byte as master does (0 movements). They ship together because they were briefed together, not because either serves the other. **D1070** was `a.toString()` meaning the callable FIELD at module top level and the free `self`-function inside any function body — `vl check` rc 0 and INVALID WASM when the free function's `self` could not take the receiver, and a silent disagreement with the ruling (DECISIONS ~1127, "field first, then a UFCS free function") when it could. The row predicted "the body path reaches a different resolver, the one `ufcsAliasOf` feeds"; **that is refuted** — single-file programs never populate that table, and D1120's fix to exactly it moves 0 of these cells. Both scopes reach the same arm of `drwWalk`; only its ANSWER differs. Printing the arm's inputs on the pre-fix seed, one program per scope: top level `si=0 isClo=T`, function body `si=-1 isClo=F`, while `tyFieldTyOf(nodeTyIxOf(recv), prop)` returned a real field type in BOTH. `structIndexOfExpr` resolves an emit-side struct-table ROW — it answers for a module global (`globalStructIndexSid`, filled before `dispatchRewrite`) and for a param, and -1 for a body-local, because `declaredStructIndex` reads `localNames` and `buildLocals` fills that during `emitModule`; `exprIsClosure`'s Member arm hangs off the same lookup, so the `si < 0` fallback could not see the callable field either and read "no field, so UFCS". The fix is ONE predicate with two callers: `ufcsCallTy`'s caller spelled its `ufcsHasField` gate inline (`TyObj` + `objFieldType`) when that is exactly the already-exported `tyFieldTyOf`, so the checker now calls it and `drwWalk` calls it on the receiver node's recorded type ahead of the row lookup — **strictly narrowing**, so an unrecorded receiver and a `TyVar` receiver inside a generic body (`drwEveryInstanceTakesField`'s question, not this one) keep today's classification. Graded on a 51-cell grid over the row's own axes (receiver scope × field-present × self-fn admits/disjoint/none × annotated-or-not) and a 12-position delivery matrix: against `origin/master` 6a737f4d the grid had **6 cells check-clean invalid wasm and 6 more printing `UFCS` where the rule says `field`**, and the matrix was **10 of 12 wrong**; after, **0 clause-1 violations, 12 of 12 `field`, and `runs → not-runs` NONE**. The two positions already right were the closure (receiver captured, so `capturedStructIndex` resolved it) and the parameter cell — the signature of a rule enforced through a row lookup rather than through the rule. **D1120** was two merged modules each exporting a `self`-function called `area`: `ufcsAliasAdd` held a row for each (it dedupes only identical pairs) and `ufcsAliasOf` answered with the FIRST, so the dependency-first rewrite walk let a dependency's call site decide the ENTRY's, refused `no field 'area' on Box` — a message about a field that is really a wrong-alias lookup. Measured before it was built, dumping the registry as code points because `demangleMsg` STRIPS `$mN` from diagnostics and two rows print identically without it: `[area -> area$m3] [area -> area$m1]`, banked by `c.vl`'s node 53 then `main.vl`'s node 65 — so `modSelfFnTarget` had already computed the right answer AT EACH SITE and only the flat read lost it. Closed by a per-call-node column `ufcsSiteTo` (the node-index sidecar shape `callSiteLoc` uses), written beside the existing `ufcsAliasAdd` and read through one entry point `ufcsAliasAtSite` by all three consumers — `ufcsCallTy` (which already takes the Call node's `ix`), `drwWalk`, and `emitCall`'s unrewritten-member fallback. The plain-name map STAYS as the fallback for readers with no call node (`witnessOf` answers a bound before any call exists; a monomorphized clone or the emitter's rebuilt direct call has no banked row), so every site the walk did not see is unchanged. **And the double import is now a duplicate-binding refusal, which cost exactly one corpus case.** `import { area } from "./a"` beside `import { area } from "./b"` binds one name to two declarations; the checker says so at the second import, naming both specifiers, in the wording `modCheckDupBindings` already uses for import-vs-declaration. The rule is narrow on purpose — it fires only when the two resolve to different merged targets, so the same name twice from the same module (or through a re-export chain landing on one declaration) still RUNS. Swept repo-wide: exactly ONE pre-existing program imported a local name from two specifiers (the other 126 duplicate-local imports, all in `compiler/*.vl`, repeat one specifier), `tests/cases/modules/duplicate-import-first-vs-last/`, whose own header documented that VALUE references took the FIRST rename row while TYPE positions took the LAST — `tag` from one module and `Tag` from the other, in one program. It is converted to an `@error` pin; the ruling and what that case no longer witnesses are in `DECISIONS.md`. Gates: all eleven green on the merged tree, filed witnesses **436 graded · 436 as filed · 0 MOVED · 0 not graded · 0 UNPARSED** (both rows re-graded to their new status), distilled corpus 0 classes moved, rep-fuzz exact, native fixpoint holds. Fixtures: `tests/cases/objects/field-precedence-in-function-body.vl` (the witness, un-annotated), `field-precedence-receiver-scope-grid.vl`, `field-precedence-delivery-positions.vl`, `ufcs-dispatch-when-no-such-field.vl` (the counter-pin that field precedence must not swallow UFCS), and `tests/cases/modules/{ufcs-same-name-two-modules,ufcs-same-name-two-modules-mirror,ufcs-same-name-three-modules,err-duplicate-import-two-modules,duplicate-import-same-declaration}/`.
- **`is T` AGAINST THE TYPE PARAMETER ITSELF (D951)** — the capability the owner asked for by name (*"can we do `is T` rather than having to do like `is T<string | boolean | i64>` (spelling out the full type)"*). It failed in two directions at once and the filed row recorded the rarer one: at a NULLABLE instantiation the emitter refused loudly (`emitProgram: `is` names a type that is not a union variant`, `vl check` rc 0), and at every other instantiation the same test was **check-clean and silently FALSE** — `function f<T>(v: T) { v is T }` printed `false` at `i32`, `string`, `f64`, `boolean`, `i64`, a struct, a list, a map and a litunion. Probed at both rungs, each RECEIVES the declaration's `TyVar`, which renders as the empty string: `monoStaticIsResult` compared the receiver's correct per-instance name (`i32`) against the node's spelling (`T`) and folded to `i32.const 0`, while the union-variant floor asked `variantIndexOf("T")`. The fix is a SUBSTITUTION, not a second ladder — under monomorphization `T` is concrete per instance, so `monoFoldTyParamLayout`'s `IsExpr` arm rewrites the check SPELLING at the pin and `recordClonedIsVarTy` banks the resolved row on the minted node (`isVarTyIx` is sized at `checkProgram` entry, so a node minted later reads -1 for ever). Measured: **`y is T` at `T := i32` emits byte-identical wasm to the hand-written `y is i32`**, and the same at `string`, so the whole existing ladder serves the new spelling. Three other `IsExpr` mint sites were dropping the same bank and now carry it; the lambda clone's shared body is substituted too. ONE instantiation cannot be banked from a spelling — at `T := (i32) => i32` the binding is the `$fnsig` KEY (`=>i>i`), which `nameToTy` has never parsed back, so `monoStaticIsResult`'s sigkey arm had no arena rows and answered `false` where the hand-written spelling ran; it now falls back to comparing the key, which is sound exactly there. Found by running the CONCRETE twin of every instantiation, which is the only test the design can fail. 20 delivery positions measured, 18 moved; the two that did not are D1116/D1117, the lambda-TEMPLATING rule, equally wrong with no `is` in the program. Discrimination pinned at both arms of a declared union. 0 corpus classes moved, `mono-tyaram-grid` identical cell-for-cell. `tests/cases/generics/is-type-parameter-itself.vl`.

- **`is A` OVER SAME-SHAPE STRUCT ARMS TESTS THE DISCRIMINANT'S VALUE (D1023, #2365)** — the owner's 2026-09-02 ruling built: two struct arms sharing a field-NAME set and differing only in a literal-typed field are a LEGAL union, and `s is Circle` is true iff the tag names the shared shape AND the value's literal fields are members of `Circle`'s sets. The TypeScript idiom was an EMIT REJECT with no `is` in the program at all (`cannot be discriminated — same field names but different field types`), and multi-member sets folded into one variant and took the wrong arm silently. **The fold and the reject were ONE column.** `variantFieldIdText` restores a bare `TyLit`'s own text, so `"circle"` and `"square"` PART there and reject — but a MULTI-member set reaches that column already softened by canon to the base its members share, so `"x" | "y"` and `"p" | "q"` both render `string`, compare EQUAL, and were folded as the layout-equal twins the comparison exists to admit. Softening is right for IDENTITY and useless for MEMBERSHIP, so the row now banks the field's ARENA TYPE beside the text (`uFieldLitTyIx`, one writer in `pushFieldRow`, two readers) rather than trying to recover members from a text column. `variantLitDiscriminable` admits the pair, `emitIs` adds the membership compare after the tag test, and `checkUnionDiscriminable` (pass 0d, plus `resolveAnnotAt` for the INLINE spelling) takes over the no-discriminant refusal — a DESIGN rule the guide always promised, so the checker owes it and `assignTags`' reject becomes an unreachable floor. **Three things the ruling left open, settled by measurement.** (1) The recommended one-heap-type rep needed NO rep change, because `internAtom` is one module-global map keyed by the literal's TEXT: `"y"` is the same `i32` in `type KA = "x" | "y"` (position 1) and `type KC = "y" | "z"` (position 0), read off a disassembly — per-type positions would have forced interning per BASE type first. A literal set also has two reps and only one is a sentinel (an inline `kind: "x" | "y"` is a `(ref $string)` holding the member's own characters, a registered ALIAS the interned atom), so the compare is picked off the field's STORAGE and the answer is independent of spelling. (2) The membership test must be a GUARD, not a conjunct — both operands of an `i32.and` evaluate, so conjoining it onto the tag ran the discriminant read's `ref.cast` on values of every OTHER arm; a two-arm union hides this completely because both arms share the shape and the cast always succeeds, and it takes a THIRD arm with different field names to see it. Lowered as `if (result i32) … else 0`. (3) A shared tag with two heap types is not a representation: tags key on the field-name signature so these arms always shared one, while `buildVariantTwins` keys on a canon id that PRESERVES each arm's literal set — the box is built under whichever row the field-name match hits first, so the other arm's `ref.cast` trapped. One predicate now answers for both callers so they cannot drift. **A peer's 17-cell ablation refuted two filed claims and caught a hole here.** "The literal SETS differing is not enough" named the wrong ingredient — two IDENTICAL arms also answer `true`/`true`, and there that is CORRECT under structural typing, so the checker's rule needs the same same-type exemption or `variant-twin-scalar-spellings.vl` is refused. And field ORDER is not a defence: the arena keeps a `TyObj`'s fields in SOURCE order while `variantSig` sees them SORTED, so `{v: i32, w: string}` and `{w: string, v: boolean}` share a tag with their arena rows misaligned — the new rule paired fields BY INDEX, called them two signatures, and let the pair through to the emit floor. Pairs by NAME now. **Owner's amendment, same day: a literal set beside its own BASE is legal.** `{kind: "x" | "y"}` next to `{kind: string}` is the overlapping-set case with B's set being the whole base — `v is A` ≡ `v.kind ∈ {"x","y"}`, `v is B` is true for every value of the shared shape, `else` after `is A` narrows to B; the "BOTH arms carry a literal set" sentence is superseded for this pair, while a pair with NO set in either arm still refuses at check and one whose BASES differ is untouched. The asymmetry is what grades it — only the arm with a set gets a compare, so the `"z"` value (a B that is not an A) is the cell a bare tag test would fail. **Residue named as D1050 with a probe**: a named litunion ALIAS in one arm beside an inline set in the other is legal by the ruling and still refuses, because an interned atom and a string ref share no layout (the litunion rep cliff); its refusal now concedes the program is type-valid instead of claiming the field types differ, so `--sites` counts it (22 → 23). Eleven gates green, `regress.py` 0 runs lost / 0 → silent / no cell changed class, filed witnesses 418 graded · 418 as filed · 0 MOVED · 0 not graded, capability probes unchanged on every program that ran before. Fixtures: `tests/cases/unions/discriminant-value-is.vl` (the ruling's table, each print naming the arm taken), `…-positions.vl` (nine delivery positions), `…-ablation.vl` (the peer's cells), `…-set-beside-base.vl` (the amendment, both spellings and both bases), `no-discriminant-check-reject.vl`, `no-discriminant-field-order-reject.vl`, and `same-field-names-literal-tags.vl` / `…-numeric-tags.vl` — the two `@emit-error` fixtures this ruling REVERSED into runs, whose old headers argued the pair had to stay loud until a rep decision was made.
- **THE SUBSTITUTION ROUTE IS THE THIRD UNION-CONSTRUCTION SITE, and a bare literal beside a litunion is ONE literal union (D1049, D1043)** — two spellings-disagree defects with one shape: a union type the compiler was building two different ways. **D1049**: D1024's subsumed-arm collapse is called from `annUnionInnerTy` and from `fillTypeDeclAt`'s `UnionDecl` arm, and a union minted by SUBSTITUTION at the pin reached neither, so `pick<T>(v: T): T | "err"` at `T = string` still minted the duplicate `string` atom — `vl check` rc 0 and `expected struct type at index 0, found (array (mut i32))`, D1024's message byte for byte, while the DIRECT spelling ran. `substTyDeep`'s `TyUnion` arm is now a third caller of the same shared rule; the ARENA-INDEX dedup already there could not see it, because `string` and `"err"` are different rows and what is duplicated is the VALUE SET. Seven `T = string` cells move to `runs` with the correct value at both `is` arms; `T = i32` and `T = Circle` are byte-for-byte unchanged, so D1042's domain NARROWS without the row closing. **D1043**: `Kind | "err"` over `type Kind = "a" | "b"` IS the three-atom litunion `"a" | "b" | "err"`, and neither route was building it — the INLINE spelling was a loud emit reject while the DECLARED one ran. **The filed mechanism was a prediction and it was wrong, and so was a second one in circulation.** Probed at `emitIs` on both spellings, every reading was identical (`exprIsLitAtom=N`, `exprUnion=Y`, `tyIsLitUnion=N`, `tyLitUnionAliasIx=-1`) except `unionNameOfExpr`: `R` for the declared spelling, `""` for the inline one — and `emitUnionLitIs`' FIRST gate disjunct is `uname == ""`. The declared spelling was running on the NAME CHANNEL over an arena shape neither route could rep. Deleting that gate entirely — strictly stronger than the proposed one-disjunct widening — moves the program to a different refusal and it still does not run. The fix is the FLATTEN, at the shared helper, so neither spelling needs a name: `litUnionFlatMembers` now admits a bare `TyLit` member of the COMMON BASE. 0 / 12 → 12 / 12 on a delivery matrix (global ASSIGNMENT included), the numeric twin `KN | 3` comes with it, and the mixed-base `Kind | 3` still declines. Distilled corpus: 0 classes moved either way; capability probes 35/36 → 37/37.

- **A BODY-SCOPE `type` IS REFUSED AT THE DECLARATION — D1045's interim, one message for all three faces (#2369)** — `parseStmt` is one production shared by module and block scope, so `type P = …` inside a function body has always PARSED; the checker registers type names only from the module-level walk, so it was then silently DROPPED, and one mechanism wore three faces: `unknown type 'P'` at the USE (line 3, never the declaration), a `vl check`-CLEAN program dying at `emitProgram: unsupported statement in body` when the name was never used, and — the face that was WRONG rather than merely refused — a local `type P` that resolved to a MODULE-scope `P` of another shape and complained about a field the local declaration declares. The owner RULED it legal and lexically scoped on 2026-09-02; until that scoping is built the checker refuses the DECLARATION with `` a `type` declaration is module-scope only for now (D1045 — ruled legal, not yet built); move `P` to module scope ``, at the `type` keyword's own line, naming its own name, and NOTHING else fires. **The refusal is an ARENA SCAN, not a statement-walk arm**, and deliberately so: the declaration can stand anywhere a statement can (function body, nested named function, arrow-lambda body, `if`/`while`/`for` block, `match` arm) and the checker has several statement-list readers, so enumerating positions is the position-matrix mistake in miniature — a missed reader is a SILENT hole, check-clean and dying at emit. "Declared, and not a top-level statement" decides it without naming a position, and the module-scope set comes from EVERY `Program` node in the arena because the driver merges the module graph into a synthesized root while each module's own root stays behind. **The single-diagnostic property is a second mechanism, not a consequence of the first**: a NAME SET consulted by `declaredTyOfName` and `applyGenAliasArgs` before their registries poisons the declared name to the error type, or the used-by-name and shadowing spellings would keep their old diagnostics and the new one would be a THIRD. It banks both `Pair<A>` and `Pair` for a generic alias, since the declaration and application registries reach it under different names. Anchored at the node's START (`tErrAtNodeStartCoded`, a new category-coded twin of `tErrAtNodeStart`) because the default anchor is the LAST token — a multiline declaration would otherwise report at its closing brace. Measured on every form the parser admits in a body (struct, union, literal union, recursive, generic alias, nominal `new`, `flat type`) plus both nesting positions; controls unchanged (a module-scope `type` runs, a nested NAMED `function` in the same position still returns `42`). **It pays its own price on the scoreboard**: the message is on the `unsupported-lowering` channel and `not yet built` joins the CONCEDES phrase list, so `goal-scoreboard.py --sites` moves 22 → 23 — a gap moved from the emitter into the checker is the direction that hides, and `scripts/capability-probes/body-scope-type-decl.vl` is the standing witness that flips to RUNS when the build lands. `wasmEmit`'s `unsupported statement in body` is now unreachable for these node kinds and stays as the floor it is over every other kind. The row stays OPEN for the scoping build. `DECISIONS.md` §"A `type` declared in a function body is legal and lexically scoped"; D1045.
- **A SUBSUMED LITERAL ARM COLLAPSES — `string | "err"` is `string`, and D1024 closes with it** — the owner's 2026-09-02 ruling built at TYPE CONSTRUCTION rather than in the emitter, because a union box's tags are POSITIONAL over the member set: `string | "err"` widened its literal to a DUPLICATE `string` atom (the refusing sibling printed the member list as `...|string|...|string`), and the only sound answers were "never mint the duplicate" or "renumber every tag". A union is a set of values and an arm that adds no values adds no arm, so the collapse is exact — decided PER ARM, AFTER FLATTENING and THROUGH ALIASES (`type Name = string` gives `Name | "err"` = `Name`; `Json | "err"` is `Json`) — and **nothing collapses that adds a value**: `i32 | "err"` stays a genuine two-arm box and `Kind | "err"` stays the three-atom litunion, because flattening `Kind` reaches its LITERALS and never the `string` ARM. **The BARE-LITERAL half only** — the ruling's mirror (`Kind | string`) is one line away and is deferred as D1048 with its price measured, because it makes two RUNNING fixtures stop running (`mixed-union-litunion-arm-is-membership.vl` and `is-litunion-arm-non-ident-receivers.vl` pin `x is K` over a `K | string` box as MEMBERSHIP over the payload, and collapsing the arm leaves `K | string | i32` reaching the emitter as `string | i32`). It ships once `is K` over a collapsed base lowers as the membership test `emitIs` already emits for a standalone litunion receiver — the build-the-lowering-first order, applied to a rep collapse. **The bug that actually cost a gate run was on the NO-COLLAPSE path**: the shared helper was given the contract "fills `out` only when it dropped something", which is unimplementable — the loop must walk every member to know the answer, so `out` is full by then — and the declaration route appended `surviving` to a list that already held it, doubling EVERY union in the module until the compiler's own source failed with `non-exhaustive match — missing` every arm it plainly had. The D1024 witness stayed green throughout. `unionDropSubsumedArms` is the shared home and BOTH union routes call it, the annotation route through `annUnionInnerTy` (re-entering itself on the survivors so the one-member arm decides the degenerate case once, and placed AHEAD of the `null` early-out or the duplicate atom rides into the niche) and the declaration route in `fillTypeDeclAt`'s `UnionDecl` arm, whose `declMemberIxs` registration list is filtered by the SAME predicate rather than rebuilt from the survivors — it is a SUPERSET of `surviving`, and a dropped arm left in it registers a variant member of a union that no longer has that arm. **Five more spellings came with it**, none of them filed on D1024: the numeric faces `i32 | 3` and `f64 | 1.5` (`union box atom test on a union with no recorded members`), `is <literal>` over the collapsed union (`literal \`is\` over a struct union is not supported`), the parameter position's second validator message, and the nullable spelling. The ruling's first hint arrives free — the existing redundant-annotation machinery now says the collapsed signature's annotation is redundant, and the fixture DECLARES those hints rather than deleting the annotations, which would have removed the two positions D1024 actually filed. Found on the way out and filed rather than folded in: D1043, the same litunion `Kind | "err"` refusing at its INLINE spelling while the DECLARED one runs — measured pre-existing on a `git archive origin/master` build, and the reason D1024's probe and that one are two probes. `DECISIONS.md` §"A subsumed literal arm COLLAPSES".
- **Member dispatch inside a generic body is decided PER INSTANTIATION — D1002 and D1005 closed together** — two filed clause-1 rows sharing one root: `x.m()` inside `g<T>(x: T)` was resolved by NAME before any instance existed, in two layers. **The checker half (D1005)**: `ufcsCallTy` gates dispatch on `assignable(recvTy, params[0])` and `assignable` answers TRUE for a `TyVar` on either side, so the receiver's FIT was never re-asked at the pin — `g({s: 2.0})` beside `toString(self: Circle)` was `vl check` rc 0 over invalid wasm while the one-annotation-different direct spelling was a positioned `no field 'toString' on {s: f64}`. A NINTH deferred table (`ufcsCstr*`) beside `memCstr*` records the hole receiver plus the `self` parameter's own type; both pins re-ask it under substitution and report the DIRECT spelling's sentence plus the contract the receiver missed. **The field-precedence guard the row filed as its blocker is writable, and the recorded blocker was a reading of the wrong receiver**: asked of `substTyDeep(recordedHole, bNames, bTys)`, `Boxed = {r: f64, toString: () => string}` IS a `TyObj`, `tyFieldTyOf` answers the field and `memberFloorMsg` is EMPTY for it — the September attempt had recorded that same floor answering `no field 'toString' on Boxed`. **The emitter half (D1002)**: `dispatchRewrite` runs before `monomorphize`, so `drwWalk` meets the call while the receiver is still a type parameter (PROBED: `si=-1 hasTv=y`, where the concrete spelling reads `si=0 hasTv=n`) and the `si < 0` arm read "no struct row" as "no field", rewriting to a direct call for every instance. `drwEveryInstanceTakesField` asks the CALL SITES what the body cannot answer — the checker has typed every argument node, so the receivers a type parameter will hold are readable at rewrite time; when they unanimously carry the field the rewrite declines and the field-closure lowering, which resolves per FUNCTION, is right at each instance. **The ORDERING did not move**; the decision did. Unanimity is a measured bound, not caution: deferring unconditionally buys the disagreeing pair and costs NINE `runs -> not-runs` cells on a 35-program position matrix, because the pre-mono rewrite is what makes the local-kind, print-routing and tail-statement paths see a plain named call — filed whole as **D1063** with a standing capability probe. Measured over a 47-cell matrix: 6 silent invalid-wasm cells -> runs, 1 SILENT WRONG CALLEE (a generic printing the free function's `C` for a receiver whose own field says `fld`) -> correct, 2 -> positioned check reject, ZERO runs lost; distilled corpus 0 of 255,504 cells changed class. **The added work is bounded and counted, not timed** — a counter build reports the call-site scan entered **0 times** compiling `compiler/entry.vl` (365,360 AST nodes) and once, over 3,689 nodes, on the witness; a wall-clock A/B on this box says nothing (load average 193 on 24 cores gave the fixed arm both a 15% win and a 39% loss). Three fixtures: two under `tests/cases/constraints/` and `tests/cases/modules/generic-member-field-precedence/` for the merge axis, where the same shape printed the wrong callee with NO diagnostic at any layer.
- **TRACK-CALLER — a failed `expect` names the line it was WRITTEN at (#2235)** — the second half of the defaults-v1 ruling, and it needed **no compiler change**: `std:test` exports `type CallerLoc = { file: string, line: i32, col: i32 }`, `expect` becomes `expect<T>(value: T, caller: CallerLoc = __callsite__)`, and a failure grows a SECOND LINE, `  at <file>:<line>:<col>`, under the unchanged assertion sentence. The intrinsic is checked STRUCTURALLY against those three fields, so the alias satisfies it and the compiler never learns the name (confirmed both ways — a user-declared alias of the same shape takes `__callsite__` too). **ONE HOP, never a chain** (the owner's ruling): a helper that wants its caller's position takes its own `caller: CallerLoc = __callsite__` and forwards it EXPLICITLY — ordinary code, no transitivity machinery — and one that does not forward reports its own `expect`, which may be in another FILE. Measured, all of it new: the extra parameter survives monomorphization at **14 of 14** receiver classes (i32/i64/f64/boolean/string, struct, `i32[]`, `string[]`, `Circle[]`, a literal union, a value union, nullable i32/i64/f64), and the anchor is the `expect` token at every spelling — `expect(x).toEqual(y)`, `expect(x).not().toEqual(y)` and the non-UFCS `toEqual(expect(x), y)` all report the `expect(`, never the `.toEqual` and never the `it` line. **The location render is LAZY where the receipt's is EAGER**, and the reason is the distinction the receipt design turns on: `shown` is T-DEPENDENT and its lazy spellings are the D941-family miscompiling ones, while `caller` is a concrete `CallerLoc` at every instantiation, so it is carried raw and rendered only on the failure path. Cost, dated 2026-09-01: **+325 bytes** (5,873 → 6,198) on a one-assertion module unoptimized and **byte-identical at `-O3`** (596 both ways — Heap2Local scalarizes the struct, reproducing the `__callsite__` finding through std); **~11 ns per PASSING assertion** (10M iterations, ~0.33 s → ~0.44 s), which is the receipt copy plus the call site's `struct.new`. **Not a message rewrite**: the assertion sentence is byte-identical to v2, so every existing message pin stayed a prefix match and `tests/vl_test_runner_test.ts` needed no edit to one — only new assertions for the location. - **Default arguments v1 — completed and RULED (owner, 2026-09-01: "let's do A — schedule in defaults, then we can do tracking")** — the admitted default set grows from a literal to a literal, a **module-scope `const`**, and the new **`__callsite__`** intrinsic (a `{ file: string, line: i32, col: i32 }` value, legal ONLY as a default), and **UFCS stops disagreeing with the plain spelling about arity** (`5.scale(2)` now takes the tail default that `scale(5, 2)` always did — B15a's `error-default-param-ufcs-arity.vl` is deleted and replaced by a running case). The semantics in one sentence: **a default expression comes from the DECLARATION and its names resolve THERE; only its EVALUATION POSITION is the call site** — so a dependency's `sep: string = SEP` takes LIB's `SEP` even when the entry module declares its own, while `__callsite__` reports the caller's module and line. Both halves are mechanised rather than hoped for: the merge now rewrites parameter defaults (`modRwFunc`), and a same-module `const` default is MARKED so neither the checker's `Ident` arm nor `emitIdentNode` can let a caller-local of the same name capture it. `const` and not `let` specifically, so "evaluated at the declaration" and "evaluated at the call" stay indistinguishable and v1 owes no answer about which it meant. **Fixed arity is untouched** — the wasm signature carries every parameter, mono and `$fnsig` never see arity variance, no overload resolution enters the language, and a function VALUE keeps its full signature (pinned). `__callsite__` is the one default whose node is minted PER CALL SITE, by a usage-gated pre-pass at the top of `checkProgram` — before `nodeTyIx` is sized, so the synthesized object literal is typed, collected and lowered by the ordinary machinery (D969 is what minting it later would have cost). Its anchor is the callee's own token via `nodeToks`, NOT `tokIndexAt`, whose binary search is invalid on the merged token stream (module offsets restart — measured: every call in a module build missed). Three things it broke or surfaced, all fixed: a const named only by a default read as "Unused variable" (`lint.bindScan` never walked defaults; it now walks them BEFORE binding the parameters); top-level binding PROMOTION became unsound for such a const because one SHARED default node is reachable from the top level and from a function body at once (`computeGlobalPromotion` now vetoes it); and putting the checker's UFCS gate beside the rewrite's found they had ALREADY drifted on a second axis — the rewrite has always required the first parameter to be NAMED `self` and the checker never asked, so `function pair(a, b)` made `5.pair(2)` check-clean and then `emitProgram: callee is not a function name` (identical on the pre-change compiler; the checker asks now, which is clause 2's second horn rather than a relabel — UFCS in VL *is* the `self` rule, so the program is illegal and the checker owed the diagnosis). Unblocks track-caller, which is now one std line: `expect(value: T, caller: CallerLoc = __callsite__)`. `DECISIONS.md` §"Default arguments v1". (#2225)

A second draft said "neither the accumulator nor the list needs care any more", and `A = Circle` beside an exact layout twin is `emitProgram: ref valtype with no interned shape` — loud, pre-existing, and scoped by the LAYOUT TWIN rather than by scope or by the accumulator pairing (`{ q: i32 }` and `{ r: string }` both run). A third quoted the nullable-read CHECK error as evidence of a missing map-value rep, when that message fires identically for a plain struct and the real refusal is one narrow later. All three are corrected and pinned. **D30 merged in parallel and had pinned D32's exact witness as `INVALID_MODULE_SRC`**; that file's own instruction for the day it starts passing is carried out (deleted, `@run` row graduated), and the constant now names D33 — so the "there may be no live member of the class left" note it replaces was true of the FILED rows and false of the tree, which is the reusable finding. - **The literal-union BOUNDARY class — four directions, one unstated rule, and it was NOT one rung** — `ctxKeepsLitUnion` PRESERVES a literal union's members in a CONTAINER (an interned i32 ATOM at an element / field / map value) and SOFTENS them as a scalar (a string ref), so a value CROSSING that boundary needs a conversion and the two sides can disagree about which rep they hold. Four filed items — a monomorphized ARGUMENT (`xs.indexOf("b")` over a `K[]`), a function-value CALL RESULT (`const f: (i32) => ("a" | "b") = toAB` then `f(1)`), a callback reaching a call through a BINDING (`std:array.mapIndexed`), and a call result stored into a LIST or MAP (D13) — three of them silent invalid modules `vl check` called clean, one loud. **The hypothesis that they were one rung is REFUTED, and the cross product is what showed it**: a 210-cell grid over DELIVERY (by name / lambda / binding / annotated binding) × SPELLING (alias / inline / inline beside an unused same-layout alias) × POSITION (argument / result / element / map value / return / local / push / indexed store) went 173 → 210 running, and it took FOUR separate rungs, each with its own witness. **(1)** `nominalizeFnTypeOfTy` — the pin a generic takes for a function-type parameter — is a THIRD hand-written copy of the renderer's `TyFunc` arm and had neither of that arm's literal-union-ALIAS legs, so `(K, i32) => K` rendered `(string, i32) => string` and one alias got two reps inside one signature. **(2)** `cloCallResultLitUnion` is the RESULT twin `cloCallParamLitUnion` never had: a `$fnsig` cannot carry it (a litunion result's token is `i`, byte-identical to a plain i32's), and inside a monomorphized instance `exprIsLitAtom`'s other arms are blind, so a value call's atom result was staged into the string-narrow slot. **(3)** The monomorphizer's pin named a literal-union array's REP rather than its TYPE — `nameIsI32Array` accepts `K[]`, so `exprArray` spelled it `i32[]`, `T` bound to plain `i32`, and `needle: T` was declared an i32 over a caller pushing a string ref; at FUNCTION scope the same call was instead a loud `monomorphize: expected an array argument for `self``, which took the documented remedy down with it. **(4)** `ctxKeepsLitUnion` is now false at `RC_FN_RES`: the three surviving preserve positions are CONTAINERS, and a function RESULT is the same scalar position a DECLARATION's return annotation occupies (`RC_ROOT`), so the interned signature and the declaration bound to it stop disagreeing — the retraction `compiler/typecheck.vl` carried ("not reachable as a miscompile") is now a closed defect rather than a live one. **D13's severity split was an artifact, not a second root**: it was loud only because at a container store the emitter could SEE the reps disagree and refuse, and the narrow it refused (a `select` tower that re-reads its operand once per member) is wrong for a CALL by evaluation COUNT, not by value. A non-place value is now STAGED at the narrow's single entry point (`emitExpr`'s `pendingLitUnion` hook), which serves the array-literal element, the indexed store and the map-value store at once — the "a reservation walk per destination" that `emitDestStrToAtom`'s header predicted was not needed, because all three are EXPRESSION positions and `exprPopBits` already walks those. **`std/array.vl`'s over-promise ledger went 7 → 8 and every subject is now retired**: both carve-outs closed (the DISHONEST `needle` argument and the HONEST `reduce` accumulator), and the eighth over-promise — the `mapIndexed` fix claim's missing DELIVERY axis — is the one that says why the class had to be worked as a cross product rather than defect by defect. Two further rows fell out without being aimed at: `generics/error-litunion-list-arg-not-pinned.vl` was the file DECLINING this exact widening for want of a measurement, and it now runs and prints its own stated oracle; the print widen needed the same declaration fallback its two sibling consumers already had. All three `@no-instantiate` pins graduated, the class was briefly EMPTY, and `tests/vl_check_codegen_test.ts`'s specimen moved out of the literal-union family to a `u8[]` generic argument (pre-existing, recorded unpinned in `std/array.vl` since #1927, now pinned) — its "read nothing" guard is now on the SCAN rather than on the class, which the old form would have reddened on a tree with no defect in it. **The `std-api-reviewer` verdict was INCONSISTENT and it was RIGHT**, against this change's own clearance: `sorted` / `sort` / `reduce` / `mapIndexed` handed a NULLABLE callback narrowed with `is` is `vl check`-clean and an invalid module. Re-derived before acting — it is not a literal union defect at all (an `i32` callback fails identically), not a std defect (a NON-GENERIC function taking a function parameter reproduces it), and not the monomorphizer's (calling the narrowed value in place runs): a narrowed nullable function value keeps its `(ref null …)` valtype across the ARGUMENT boundary while the parameter declares the non-null one. Pre-existing, byte-identical on master's compiler, now `tests/cases/soundness/xfail-miscompile-narrowed-nullable-fn-arg.vl` — so `soundness/` and `std/` each refilled from unrelated causes in the same commit. The review also found the fixed `mapIndexed` delivery enumeration was an UNDER-claim in the other direction: three more deliveries (a list element, a struct field, a function result) were broken on the parent seed and run now, and are pinned. Corpus 1,691 of 1,707 byte-identical; rep-fuzz exact. Re-measured after rebasing over D14 and D9, which also land in `emit_classify.vl`: the grid's before/after and its 37-cell mover set are unchanged, so neither closure overlaps this one.

- **`std:array.mapIndexed` with a string literal-union result `U` — one instance was spelling `U[]` two ways** — `vl check` rc 0 — the only command that misses it — and the engine refusing the module at load (`type mismatch: expected (ref $type), found (ref $type)`), for EVERY receiver: the predicate was `U` alone and only for the string family. **The mechanism is two binding columns.** A monomorphized instance substitutes its RETURN annotation through the ARGUMENT's arena rows (`pinTys`) and its body's annotated locals through the pin re-resolved from the pin's NAME (`pinnedTyIx`), and that column's own header said the two "differ in coverage, not in meaning". They differ in MEANING at exactly one parameter shape — a FUNCTION-TYPE parameter, whose pin name is rendered by `monoSubstAnn` from each type parameter's BOUND NAME, and a literal union's bound name is the SOFTENED `string` (`ctxKeepsLitUnion` is false at `RC_ROOT`). So `f: (T, i32) => U` over an `"a" | "b"`-returning callback pinned `(i32, i32) => string` and bound `U := string` for the body while the return bound `U := "a" | "b"`: the signature said `("a"|"b")[]` (an i32 ATOM-backed list — `ctxKeepsLitUnion` holds at `RC_ELEM`) and `const out: U[]` said `string[]`. The staging slot is reserved by the SAME body walk that reserves the push quad (`stmtPushBits` bit 256, on scope-free inputs and deliberately over-claiming), so a `.push` the walk missed is already invalid for want of its quad and the slot cannot go missing on its own; `gLitUnionUsed` gates it, so every module without a string literal union — the self-hosted compiler included — is byte-identical. **`std/array.vl` loses BOTH `mapIndexed` carve-outs**, the inline one (an invalid module) and the alias half of the other (an emit refusal), deleted rather than softened. **A std review then found the deletion had been written up as a clearance it is not** — "a literal-union ELEMENT is admitted with NO carve-out at all", against which `xs.indexOf("b")` over a `K[]` is four lines, imports only std, and writes an invalid module `vl check` calls clean. That is the ARGUMENT boundary of a monomorphized instance (the substituted `needle: T` is the interned ATOM, the bare literal is a string ref), it reaches the four exports taking a `needle: T` and no others, and it is triggered by the atom REP rather than by your spelling — an inline `("a"|"b")[]` is fine until any same-layout alias exists anywhere in the program, so `std:fs`'s `FileKind` breaks a `("file"|"dir")[]` by import alone. Pre-existing, reproduces on a hand-written generic importing nothing, pinned as `xfail-miscompile-array-litunion-needle.vl`; remedy, measured, is to bind the needle first. It is over-promise number SEVEN in that header's ledger and the first on the dishonest failure kind — caught by the rule the same header already stated two paragraphs down. **The surviving honest carve-out was also re-scoped on a measured axis**: it is `reduce`'s accumulator, it is not about the ALIAS, and it is not a `reduce` bug — a hand-written generic importing nothing reproduces it, the deciding property is PARAMETER ORDER (`A` is first bound at the CALLBACK parameter; move `init: A` ahead of `f` and the identical body runs), and the inline spelling is NOT a remedy because an unused same-layout alias anywhere in the program brings the refusal back. The remedy that holds, measured in a module that declares the alias: type the accumulator `string` and narrow at the use site. The order property predicts *that* something breaks, not *which way*: `mapIndexed`'s `U` is first bound at a callback too and is fine, and a hand-written `once<A>(f: (A) => A, init: A)` over an alias writes an INVALID module rather than refusing — so "honest" is a measured statement about `reduce`, not about the defect underneath it. **Inert elsewhere, measured cell-by-cell**: all 9,126 cells of the silent-class grid grade identically against a seed built from master's `compiler/` — 0 moved, SILENT TOTAL 4 either way. Ids follow first **interning** — first appearance in the emitted code — so the answer tracked neither member text nor declaration order. Valid module, exit 0, wrong answer, and the whole ordering family inherited it: `sorted` over a `K[]`, and a hand-written minimum loop importing nothing. **The hazard scope was the compiled PROGRAM, not the module**: an inline `("a"|"b")[]` registers as a same-layout alias declared anywhere in the graph, so `import { pathKind } from "std:fs"` alone flipped a `("file"|"dir")[]` sort, because `std/fs.vl` declares `FileKind = "file" | "dir"`. The rule is ANNOTATION-INDEPENDENT, which is the whole point: `function loop(n: i32): i32 { return loop(n + 1) }` produced no diagnostic at all, while dropping the annotation produced `cannot infer a return type for 'loop'` — so the fix people reach for silences the message and leaves the infinite recursion. The analysis is a clean-PATH existence question, not "does the body contain a self-call": each statement reports whether some path through it reaches a function EXIT or the NEXT statement without a self-call, and the rule fires only when the body has neither. That keeps real recursion quiet — a base case is a clean exit (an `if` with no `else` is itself a clean fall-through past the guard), a self-call in a `while`/`for` body is a path that skips it (a loop may run zero times), and a self-call on the RIGHT of `&&`/`||`/`??` is a path that short-circuits before it. FIRES on: both `if`/`else` arms recursing, the self-call as the LEFT operand of `&&`, as a call ARGUMENT, as the block's implicit-return tail, in a `const` initializer, in every `match` arm, followed by a `return`, and a nested function that recurses on itself. SCOPE is DIRECT self-recursion keyed by the declaration's own name over ONE body — the walk never descends into a nested `FuncDecl` (whose body runs only when IT is called; the shared walker analyses it separately against its own name), and mutual recursion (`f` → `g` → `f`) needs a must-call graph over the module and stays out. A base case unreachable only by VALUE (`if n != n { return 0 }`) is a clean exit path syntactically and stays quiet — the lint does no constant folding beyond the literal booleans `constant-condition` already handles. Severity is `warning`, not `error`: an error would make `vl check` reject programs it accepts today. Zero findings across `compiler/*.vl` + `std/` (`scripts/lint-self.sh`). The three pieces already shipped — `flat`'s folded `TValue.size`/`TValue.tt` constants, B14's free index operator, and P1.5 newtypes giving the bracket a branded RETURN type — compose with nothing added. `st[i].tt()` is `cmp`-identical, byte for byte, to the hand-written `tt(slotAt(st, i))` at BOTH `-O0` and `-O3 --closed-world`, where both accessors inline away entirely and the loop body is `(i << 4) + base + 8; i32.load` with no call remaining. The brand is load-bearing twice: it is what the bracket dispatches its result into, and it is what stops a bare `i32` from being read as a row. The spec's paren-less `stack[i].tt` is a LOUD checker reject (`member access '.tt' on non-object RowAddr`) and that is deliberate — branding over a STRUCT instead would make the wrong spelling compile and be slower. The design doc's "the bracket deletes two accessors PER FIELD" was corrected by building it: it deletes NONE (a 2-field record needs the same 5 functions), it deletes the CONTAINER axis — one accessor set serves N containers, N×M → N+M. (`docs/internals/flat-records-design.md` §9, `tests/cases/memory/flat-fused-row-*.vl`)

- **A16 litunion COMPACT REP — DESIGNED AND FILED, and its own rationale REFUTED by measurement** — the preserve ruling (#1300) was justified partly by a door it kept open: a mixed union box could store its litunion member as the compact interned ATOM id instead of a string ref, *"cheaper allocation, faster equality"*, and that is only spellable once the vocabulary distinguishes `K` from `string`. Walked through and measured, the allocation half is **wrong**: `collectStrPool` interns every distinct literal into an immutable global, so `const x: K | f64 = "aa"` emits `i32.const 2 / global.get 0 / struct.new 0` — **exactly ONE `struct.new`, the box itself, and a payload that is a `global.get` rather than an allocation**. No rep allocates less; the obvious compact encoding (the existing `$vbI32` scalar box round the atom id) allocates **twice**, and only `ref.i31` — of which the emitter has **zero** today — matches one. The brief's ship bar was *"show a witness program's WAT losing the string-ref path"*; there is no such witness because that path does not allocate, so the verdict is FILE. The equality half survives intact (a `ref.cast` + an O(len) `__str_eq__` CALL becomes one `i32.eq`). **What the measurement DID find is 81 broken cells of 244**, all `vl check` rc 0 — **42 SILENT wrong answers**, 34 invalid wasm, 5 loud — with ONE root cause: **`valueAtomKind` has no code for a literal-union member** (it returns `-1`; `emit_base.unionHasValueAtom` carries the workaround with the reason written out), and **35 of its 42 call sites have no compensating litunion leg**. Four families: storing an atom-typed VALUE into `K | f64` emits `f64.convert_i32_s` **on the atom ID** and tags it f64 (24 cells); reading a narrowed arm back into a `K`-typed position is invalid wasm in **9 of 9** spellings (16 cells); `K | string` puts two members on one tag, so `const x: K | string = "zz"; x is K` prints **K** in six lines — refuting the invariant `tests/cases/unions/litunion-value-union-is.vl` has asserted in a comment since #845; and `K | K2` reps as a bare string with `is K` **const-folded to `i32.const 0`**. **A loud reject is not available for the collision shapes** — counted, not assumed: it would move **12** and **4** `RUN-OK` cells DOWN, so they are BLOCKED on the rep. Three owner rulings gate the build (the tag scheme — a 14th value-atom kind bumps both slot bands by a constant where a per-set slot band re-bases them wholesale, renumbering every union box tag in every program; whether `ref.i31` enters the emitted vocabulary — measured available in wasm-tools' shipped set, V8, and wasmtime 47, the last proved by a module that reaches IMPORT resolution; and what `K | K2` should mean), plus the `repCanonKeyGo` mix-widen inversion that fragments struct-twin rows. **The `K | K2` answer turns out to need no ruling at all and is the slice to take first**: a union all of whose members are literal unions IS a literal union, and the flattened target already runs on master with ZERO compiler changes (`type KA = "aa"|"bb"|"cc"|"dd"`, `x is K` → `K` for `"aa"` and `O` for `"cc"`), because `emitIs`'s membership ladder tests the tested type's own members over the interned atom — so slice C's runtime half is free and only the checker's render (which today spells `K | K2` as `string`) has to move; a CHECKER-level reject is not an alternative, since §4's never-move-down arithmetic does not care which phase a reject comes from. **Two method corrections shipped with it**: this slice's own first grid greened falsely on #1304's control rule — an inline `("aa"|"bb")` spelled in a file declaring `type K = "aa"|"bb"` let the alias answer the inline lookups and hid **10 cells**, including a narrowed read that is invalid wasm in 5 of 6 spellings; and the fuzzer's litunion-in-mixed-union reach is **real** (26 and 14 of 800 cases on two seeds, correcting the standing "zero reach" note) but **vacuous on every defect family** — it only ever stores a member LITERAL, which is the cell that already passes. No compiler file changed; the working cells are pinned. (`docs/internals/litunion-compact-rep-design.md`, `docs/internals/destringify-types-program.md`, `tests/cases/literal-unions/mixed-union-litunion-arm-floor.vl`)
- **Contextual f32 literals (webcraft P2)** — `let x: f32 = 0`, `f(1)`, `return 2`, `{v: 1}`, `[1]`, `xs[0] = 1`, `xs.push(1)`, `fv + 1`, `fv > 1`, `f32 | null = 1` and the `"[]="` operator all take a bare literal. Measuring the ask first SPLIT it: the `.`-literal half was ALREADY shipped in all 32 positions grid-tested, while the INTEGER half was missing in **18 of 18**, every one of which the f64 twin already compiled. The two halves take deliberately DIFFERENT rules, forced rather than chosen for symmetry — a `.` literal is **context-typed** (f32 from birth, rounding ONCE at 24 bits) because an exactness gate would reject `0.1`/`0.2`/`3.14` and leave nothing to admit; an INTEGER literal is **exactness-gated** (`intLexemeIsExactF32`, a closed-form bit test: `bitlen <= 128 && bitlen - trailingZeros <= 24`, where the 128 bound is EXACT because the largest finite f32 and the largest 128-bit integer with ≤24 significant bits are the same number) because it denotes an exact integer and silently turning `16777217` into `16777216` is the lossy implicit conversion the lossless-only rule forbids. So `16777216` and `33554432` are admitted while `16777217` and `9000000000` reject, with both one-token escape hatches (`16777217.0`, `as f32`) intact. **`as f32` is NOT the oracle for what the sugar lowers to**: for `1.00000017881393432617187` the bare literal encodes `0x3F800001` (one rounding) and the cast `0x3F800002` (decimal→f64, then ties-to-even on the demote) — *different numbers* — and the cast is a runtime `f64.const` + `f32.demote_f64` that cannot sit in a `const` global initializer at all. Both halves now funnel through ONE `isF32AdoptingLitExpr` so they cannot drift position by position; the mixed-arithmetic lattice (`mixesNumeric`/`widerNumeric`/`binMixHardF64`) is untouched, since the literal retypes before it runs. Corpus: 1 of 1,656 files moved, +2 bytes, all values identical (`i32.const 7; f32.convert_i32_s` → the shorter, constexpr-valid `f32.const 7.0`). (`docs/internals/contextual-f32-literals-design.md`, `tests/cases/numerics/f32-contextual-integer-literal.vl`, `f32-integer-literal-exactness.vl`, `f32-integer-literal-inexact-reject.vl`, `f32-literal-single-round.vl`)
- **fix: a radix literal in a FLOAT context was a silent wrong value** — `const x: f64 = 0x10` printed **7210** and `const x: f64 = 0b101` printed **50101**, rc 0 with `vl check` clean. `ieeeBytes` — the shared decimal→IEEE-754 encoder — folded mantissa digits with a hard-coded `* 10` and `c - '0'`, walking straight over the `0x` prefix (0, then `'x' - '0'` = 72, then 721, then 7210). Only the CONSTEXPR path was wrong: a float context lowers an integer literal directly as `f64.const`/`f32.const` so a `const` global initializer stays a valid wasm constant expression, whereas the call-ARGUMENT spelling `f(0x10)` converts from i32 and was always right — which is why it hid. Fixed in the encoder, so both widths and every position take it at once. (`tests/cases/numerics/float-literal-radix-constexpr.vl`)
- **fix: an integer literal boxed into a float-only union was invalid wasm** — `const x: f64 | null = 1` emitted `type mismatch: expected anyref, found i32`, `vl check` clean, in the GLOBAL, LOCAL and ARGUMENT positions alike. `emitUnionCoerce`'s value-atom ladder promotes its i32 default to `i64` when the union has no i32 atom — but the LIST arm of the SAME ladder promotes an i32-element list to `i64[]`/`f64[]`/`f32[]`, three targets, on identical reasoning. The scalar arm had been taught only the first, so an integer flowing into a float-only union kept the i32 code and boxed an i32 into the float value box. The two spellings that WORKED localize it exactly: `i64 | null = 1` took the taught half and `f64 | null = 1.0` classifies as a float up the ladder and never reaches the default — both are controls in the pin. (`tests/cases/unions/nullable-float-integer-literal.vl`)
- **`m.set(k, v)` takes the assignment path's literal narrowing (webcraft P2 polish)** — the map `.set` VALUE argument was the last store position checked with the bare structural `assignable`, so `m[k] = 0.5` over a `{[string]: f32}` compiled while `m.set(k, 0.5)` was `set: expected f32, got f64` — and the same for an exact integer literal, a doubly-signed one, a member literal into a literal union (string OR integer members), an object literal adapting field-wise, an array literal adapting element-wise, and each of those again through a `V | null` / `f32 | string` value slot or a receiver reached from an array element or a struct field. A 146-cell twin grid against the `m[k] = v` control went **16/38 → 38/38** direct and **0/12 → 12/12** nested map-store pairs agreeing on verdict AND stdout, 34 cells moving CHKERR → OK, every one of them printing the value its index-assignment twin prints. The REJECTED side is unchanged and is what makes it a rule: an inexact integer (`16777217`), a non-member literal, and a non-literal `f64` VALUE all still reject. MEASURED AS NEEDING NOTHING: `Set`'s `.add` (7/7 twin pairs already agreed — its argument is a KEY, and keys are `string`/`i32` with no literal to narrow) and the `.set` KEY itself (`checkIndexNode` checks `m[k]`'s key with the bare `assignable` too, so widening it would diverge in the other direction). - **A-infer-null `let x = null` as a nullable hole** — an un-annotated `let x = null` is no longer pinned to the exact `null` type (which made `let x = null; x = 5` error `expected null, got 5`); `null` is now hole-bearing like `[]`. The binding is `T | null` where `T` is a fresh shared inference hole (`Nullable<Infer<Unknown>>`), and a later constraint — a reassignment `x = <expr>`, a `T | null` param, an annotated assignment — FILLS the hole's `T` in place via the same `constrainElementHole` machinery the empty array uses (`x = 5` ⇒ `x: i32 | null`). This is NOT a pin violation: VL still pins COMPLETE types (`let x = 7; x = "foo"` errors — `7` is complete, `null` is not), and once the hole is filled the cell behaves as that complete type (`let x = null; x = 5; x = "foo"` errors). The initializer contributes the `| null`, which is sticky (it reflects that `x` really was null) EXCEPT flow-narrowing strips it on a path where `x` is provably non-null: a straight-line `x = <non-null>` narrows `x` to its non-null base for the rest of the block (no null tax — `let x = null; x = 5; x + 1` runs), threaded through the shared `postGuardNarrowings` entry point so both the type checker's scope overlay and codegen's narrowed overlay get it; an assignment inside an `if` branch stays in that branch, so the conditional-assign idiom (`let x = null; if c { x = f() }`) still requires a null check across the branch. An UNCONSTRAINED `let x = null` (never reassigned/used to pin `T`) resolves to the plain `null` type — a lone `null` IS fully determined, so the inference floor (`reportUninferredBinding`) does NOT raise "cannot infer" for it (distinct from an empty `[]`, whose element is genuinely unknown). A `const x = null` (immutable) keeps the exact `null` type, and an explicit `let x: T | null = null` is unchanged. Also fixes a latent bug exposed here: typing an assignment EXPRESSION (a block-tail `{ x = v }`) whose target is any `T | null` cell (`let n: i32 | null` too) no longer spuriously fails the scalar `=` operator-method lookup. (`tests/cases/types/infer-null-*.vl`)

Capture ROUTES are perfectly uniform (39/8/5 in all five, before and after), so the split-decision-site pattern that bit the for-in loop-var work does **not** apply here; **binding form** is the axis that still splits (param 110/130 with zero invalid wasm, local 85/130 with 25). **Newly accepted: 43 cells**, all struct-union and in-callee-narrowed shapes that master loud-rejected, each producing the oracle's value on every runtime input; **newly rejected: empty**. Sabotage was predicted before running and graded on the run value: killing the declaration-site replay moves **exactly 141** cells and lands the four sub-grids exactly on master's columns while touching **0** in the in-callee grid; killing the box-fetch leg moves 178 (19 short of prediction — the survivors are **exactly** the struct-union cells, whose unbox is a different receiver path); killing the per-frame re-bank moves 18 (24 under — a null-*comparison* guard resolves a local through `valueUnionNullCmpName` rather than `declaredUnion`, so only the `is` spellings need the emit-time table). **0 cells were better under any sabotage than in the fix.** Byte-identity holds where it can (the branch-point compiler sources compile byte-identically under master's compiler, the branch point's and this one; the five plain-scalar controls are byte-identical, never narrowed so never seeded) and is meaningless where the 197 fixed cells differ by construction, a box and an unboxed ref being different heap types. **Measured, diagnosed and NOT fixed (32 cells)**: an un-annotated local capture whose initialiser is a niche-returning call types its env field **i32** and is check-clean invalid wasm in the *enclosing* frame, because `captureValKind`'s un-annotated arm uses `letInitCellKind`, a **shortened mirror** of `collectLocals`' ladder missing all eleven niche arms — the two exist separately only because `emit_classify` cannot import `emit_collect` — and the checker then emits `redundant type annotation` on the very annotation that fixes it, so the compiler advises deleting the load-bearing annotation. The magnitude was right and **the mechanism was wrong**: gutting `findFnDeclIn` to `return -1` outright changes that workload by ~2%. The cost was the **write-effect summary BANK** — `fnWriteEffects` / `fnWriteFreePaths` scanning parallel `weKeys`/`weVals` string arrays that grow one entry per summarised (callee, parameter), so n guarded paths against n *distinct* callees is n lookups over a 2n array. The experiment that separates them holds every axis fixed but the suspected one: **3,000 guards against ONE shared callee costs 60 ms; 3,000 guards against 3,000 DISTINCT callees costs 380 ms** — same guard count, same call count, only the bank differs — and the shared-callee case is **unchanged by the fix (1.0x)**, which is what proves the walk was not the cost there. `findFnDeclIn` *is* quadratic, on an axis the filed input could not reach: the walk runs once per call **inside the body being summarised**, and an intrinsic like `print` asks a name no root holds, so one summary is quadratic in the number of calls that body makes — invisible when every callee body is one line. Both are fixed: the bank becomes a single `weSums` map (with presence asked by `has`, since `""` legitimately means "writes nothing"), and the walk is memoised on **`(subtree root, name)`** including negative answers, because that `-1` is the answer every intrinsic call needs. **The walk is scope-sensitive and BOTH filed candidates FAIL OPEN — measured, not argued**: memoising on the name alone answers the second of two same-named nested declarations with the first one's summary, and a flat module-wide map additionally answers a function *value*'s call with an unrelated nested declaration, destroying the opaque fallback that makes the whole predicate safe. Both were **5–9% faster** and unsound, so exact keying ships; `(root, name)` cannot err, the walk being a pure function of `(P.nodes, root, name)` in a file that never pushes nodes. Measured at load 4.3, best of 5: guard-axis **380 → 120 ms (3.2x)**, call-axis **60 → 10 ms** at 500 calls and **810 → 10 ms (81x)** at 2,000, with the fixed total scaling **2.13 / 2.03 / 2.05 / 2.11x per doubling across a 16x input range** — linear, where the tip ran 2.23 / 2.29 / 2.91x. - **A-missing-return Fall-through totality — implicit `null`, not a trap** — a function whose body can fall off the end without yielding a value implicitly produces `null` there. That is sound exactly when `null` is part of the return type, so the rule is assignability-based, not a blanket reject: a **non-nullable** value return with a reachable fall-through is an error (`function f(n: i32): i32 { if n > 0 { return 1 } }` — the TS `noImplicitReturns` case, which used to type-check and then TRAP at the wasm result-type fallthrough), while a **nullable** return lowers the fall-through AS that null. An un-annotated function widens its inferred return to `T | null` on fall-through (host byline: "types hidden by aggressive inference") — `function f(n: i32) { if n > 0 { return 1 } }` infers `i32 | null`, no annotation needed — and a declared `: T | null` may fall through too (previously a false-positive reject). The totality test (`nodeIsTotal`) is the dual of the definite-assignment `daBranchDiverges`: a block is total iff its last statement is — an explicit `return`, a `break`/`continue` (divergence), an `if`/`else` whose BOTH arms are total (`else if` chains recurse), a `while true { … }` (never falls through), or a bare trailing VALUE expression. It is computed while the body scope is still live (a discriminated param/local's type would otherwise be out of scope) and consumed once the return type is finalized. The emitter pads a live fall-through with the return rep's null via `emitNullForRet` (boolean-niche sentinel `2`, string-niche `ref.null $array`, nullable struct `ref.null $S`, value-union null-box) instead of the dead `unreachable` it still uses for a proven-dead non-nullable fall-through. Box-able value types (`i32`/`i64`/`f64`/`f32` and unions) infer un-annotated; a NICHE (`boolean | null` / `string | null`) inferred return is lifted in **A-niche-inference** below.
