- **A-definite-assign Definite assignment for uninitialized locals** — an uninitialized `let x` / `let x: T` now starts UNassigned and NON-null (NOT implicitly nullable); a READ where `x` is not provably written on every preceding path is a `` `x` is used before it is assigned `` error. This closes a silent-`0` soundness gap (`let x: i32; return x` used to compile and fabricate a `0`). The check reuses the parser's single-pass flow machinery — the same `is`-narrowing fork/join that scopes through `if`/`else`/`while` and lets a diverging branch drop out: a per-`Binding` "unassigned" bit is forked at each branch, joined at the merge (assigned only if written on every surviving path — a `return`/`break`/`continue` branch contributes nothing, reusing `divergesStatement`), and reset to the pre-loop state after a `while`/`for`/`for-in` body (zero-iteration). The declaration itself is fine; only the reads are gated, and the binding's type is unchanged (`let x: i32` stays `i32`, not `i32 | null`). Initialized `let x = …` and every `const` are assigned from the start and untouched. (`tests/cases/variables/definite-assign-*.vl`)
- **A11 Recursive structural types** — `type Tree = { value, left: Tree | null, … }` constructs/traverses/compiles (cycle-safe traversals + self-referential WasmGC rec-group). Mutual recursion across *separate* `type` decls (`type A = { b: B | null }` ↔ `type B = { a: A | null }`) now resolves: a top-level type-name pre-pass hoists every `type` name before any body is parsed, so a forward/mutual reference stays a lazy `Alias` leaf and both aliases tie into one rec-group. (`tests/cases/types/mutual-recursive-type.vl`) Recursion through an **array element type** (`type List = { value: i32, rest: List[] }`) now compiles too — the element struct, its growable-list `{backing,len,cap}` wrapper, and the backing array are discovered as one strongly-connected component and built in a single WasmGC rec group (forward-referencing each other), instead of unboundedly re-entering type lowering and overflowing the stack. (`tests/cases/types/recursive-array-element.vl`) Recursion through a **map value type** (`type Tree = { value: i32, children: { [string]: Tree } }`) now compiles as well — the map's hash struct and its `vals` backing array join the same rec group, so the value-type back-edge is threaded via forward refs instead of overflowing through `mapType`→`mapArrayType`→`refHeapType`. (`tests/cases/types/recursive-map-value.vl`)
- **A12 Soundness corpus (started)** — must-error/must-not-error corpus under `tests/cases/soundness/`; strict by default; known-unsound corners `xfail`-marked.
- **A13 Operator-constraint inference (core)** — fully-inferred structural functions monomorphize per call shape (i32 & f64 from two call sites).
- **A13 fix: the deferred binary-op capability check covers EQUALITY** — a binary op with a hole operand records a deferred `(lt, op, rt)` constraint that each generic call site re-validates under the substituted argument types (`binOpDefinedFor`), but its `==`/`!=` arm returned true for every operand pair. So `function cmp(a, b) a == b` / `cmp(1, "x")` type-checked clean and then emitted an i32 where the module declares a `(ref $type)` — a compile-clean program the engine rejects at instantiation — while the annotated twin `a == "x"` was already a `cannot compare i32 with string` error. The arm now applies the same mutual-compatibility criterion, over what the operands ERASE to (`nomErasedTyIx`), so `id == 0` on a newtype stays comparable while `EntityId == string` rejects. A `null` operand is exempt: a nullness test asks about the storage, not about type agreement. Rejects `i32`/`f64`/`boolean` against `string` and `boolean` against `i32` in all eleven hole-provenance shapes (two-hole, one-hole-one-annotated either side, two-level chain, captured operand, array element, struct field, second instantiation); no program in the 1,770-file corpus changes verdict. (`tests/cases/soundness/equality-hole-operand-reject.vl`, `equality-hole-operand-sound.vl`, `equality-hole-null-test-sound.vl`)
- **A13 fix: a string ORDERING with one annotated operand defers to the call site** — `function f(a, b: string) { a < b }` called `f("a","b")` was rejected *"comparison expects numeric operands, got any and string"* while both its bare twin `f(a, b)` and its fully-annotated twin `f(a: string, b: string)` accepted and printed the same value — so adding an annotation removed a capability, inverting the aim of types hidden by aggressive inference. The ordering arm demanded `isStringTy` on BOTH sides, so a hole on either side fell to `isNumeric`, which refuses a `string`; hole/hole never reached the arm because `isNumeric` admits a `TyVar`. A concrete-string-against-a-hole ordering now DEFERS, the way `+` already does for `s + h`: `noteBinCstr` records the constraint and each call site adjudicates it under substitution through `binOpDefinedFor`, whose ordering rule admits exactly `string`/`string` and numeric/numeric. Population re-derived at **24 cells**, not the filed 8 — the four ordering operators × the two half-annotated directions × **three** string-typed spellings (`string`, a string literal type, a string literal union; the last two reach the arm through `softenLitTy`, which a `string`-only grid never exercises). All 24 print the same value as their bare and fully-annotated twins, as do the same shape through a lambda, a nested generic, a `let` init, a loop condition and an uncalled body — so every newly-accepted program has an accepting fully-annotated twin. Every non-string binding of the hole still rejects (i32, f64, boolean, list, object, `null`, `string?`, and through two generic hops), now at the call that pins it and naming the ARGUMENT types rather than the hole; no program in the 237-case `@error` corpus changes verdict. (`tests/cases/soundness/ordering-hole-string-operand-sound.vl`, `ordering-hole-string-operand-reject.vl`)
- **A14 Named/opaque type crash fix** — bodyless-`type Point` infinite-recursion crash fixed (cycle-guarded `getConcreteType`; now errors cleanly). → `DECISIONS.md`
- **A15 Structural equality** — `==`/`!=` by value; functions by reference; arrays + nested structs recurse via `valueEq`/`isEquatable`. → `DECISIONS.md`
- **A15 fix: structural `==`/`!=` on a value-union operand** — `v == 7` where `v: "x" | 7` no longer crashes codegen (`Have only handled i32 with ==, got Union`); it lowers structurally by reusing the boxed-union `{tag, value}` rep and the `is`-literal machinery — tag-select the matching arm, then `valueEq` the unboxed payload against the other operand (a cross-type arm is structurally unequal, e.g. the `"x"` arm vs an `i32` → `false`). `union == union` lands too (same arm + payload-equal, short-circuiting each unbox on its tag). Reuses `unionInfo`/`findVariant`/`unboxPayload`/`valueEq`; no checker change. (`tests/cases/operators/union-eq.vl`)
- **A15 fix: symmetric `==`/`!=` type-checking for a value-union operand** — `7 == v` (where `v: "x" | 7`) now type-checks and runs just like `v == 7` did; equality is symmetric, but the checker previously gated the structural value-union branch on the *left* operand being the union (`leftType.type === "Union" | "Nullable"`), so the reversed form fell through to the numeric `==` path and reported `expected i32, got "x" | 7`. The branch now fires when *either* operand is a value-union; the comparability test (`validateType` either direction) is already order-independent, and the reversed form additionally tests the union against the *un-softened* left operand so a bare literal (`7`, softened to `i32` for arithmetic) still matches one of the union's arms. A plain mismatch with no union (`"a" == 7`) still errors as before. Codegen already handled both orders (PR #200) — no `toWasm.ts` change. (`tests/cases/operators/union-eq-reversed.vl`, `eq-no-union-mismatch.vl`)
- **A16 Literal-union types (type-level)** — annotations constrain (`"a"|"b"` rejects `"c"`); `==`/`!=` discriminate + narrow; covering `if/else if` chain exhaustive. `flattenType` dedup uses an O(n) value-key set when every variant is a literal (the common case; distinct literals never subsume), replacing the O(n²) pairwise `validateType` scan — a left-folded N-member literal union now type-checks in O(n²) not O(n³) (160 members 485ms→3.8ms). Shared front-end logic (carries to `typecheck.vl`). (`tests/cases/types/literal-union-dedup.vl`)
- **A7b `boolean`-where-`i32`-expected coercion** — a `boolean`-typed VALUE coerces to `i32` (true→1, false→0) at an assignment boundary (binding/argument/return); no-op in codegen (shared i32 rep). One-directional (`i32` ⊄ `boolean`); excludes a bare boolean literal and membership/narrowing queries (`x is boolean` on `string | i32` still rejected).
- **A7b fix: an `i32[]` binding built from boolean-typed elements PRINTED `true`** — `const t = true` / `const e: i32[] = [t]` is check-clean, because the A7b coercion lives at `assignableExpr` — the ONE seam every binding / argument / return / field / element / store / push flows through — so an array LITERAL adapts ELEMENT-WISE into an `i32[]` destination. The checker then types every `e[i]` read as `i32` and says so in its own words (`const x: i32 = e[0]` draws `` redundant type annotation: `x` is inferred as `i32` ``). The EMITTER disagreed: `print(e[0])` rendered `true` while `print(e[0] + 0)` rendered `1` — the same expression over the same value, two formats, `vl check` rc 0. `listElemIsBool` consulted the DECLARED element name only as a positive claim (`== "boolean"` → true) and then walked to the binding's INITIALIZER regardless, where the first element is a boolean-typed value; annotation and initializer legitimately disagree exactly where the coercion fires, and the walk outvoted the annotation. `i32` is now claimed beside `boolean` at that same seam, so the declared element decides in BOTH directions and the initializer walk stays the route only for an un-annotated binding. Only the depth-1 array element was ever wrong — `i32[][]` reads through an `Index` (no binding to walk to), an object-literal field goes through `Member`, and `.push` / index-store leave the initializer alone, so all three already printed `1`. Blast radius: **0 of 1,970** corpus check-verdicts move, **1,901 passed / 0 failed / 7 ignored** on the `@log` oracle, **0** self-host reliance (the fixed compiler is its own self-compilation fixpoint byte-for-byte at 1 compile, and bootstraps from the published master seed in 2). Sabotage: with the fix reverted to the saved pristine artifact, exactly **1 of 1,901** reddens — the new positions fixture, as predicted. (`tests/cases/types/boolean-to-i32-container-positions.vl`, `boolean-to-i32-container-reject.vl`)
- **A17 Forward / mutual-reference return-type inference** — demand-driven (lazy + memoized, cycle-detected) return-type inference; a function calling a later-defined or mutually-recursive function no longer infers `any`; only a genuinely base-case-less inferred cycle still needs an explicit annotation. (#105; detail: `docs/selfhost-gaps.md` §A17)
- **A18 Order-independent module scope + TDZ** — top-level `let`/`const` VALUES are now hoisted (names + types) in a checker pre-pass, exactly as top-level FUNCTIONS already were, so a function body resolves a global declared LATER in the file. This removes the last reason a forward-referenced / demand-inferred function needed an explicit RETURN annotation (its body could previously not resolve a not-yet-declared global, so inference failed — `A17` covered the call graph, not the global it reads). Initialization order is still enforced: each global joins the definite-assignment dead-zone at hoist time and is marked assigned only when its initializer is reached, so a read before initialization — straight-line top-level code, OR one global's initializer reading a later global — is a `` `x` is used before it is assigned `` (temporal-dead-zone) error, NOT a silent read of uninitialized memory. A function body runs at call time, after module init, so its reads are correctly exempt (its own definite-assignment context is cleared). An annotated global hoists its annotation type; an un-annotated one hoists a side-effect-free LITERAL peek (a non-literal initializer stays order-dependent — it carries no manifest type to hoist). A genuine top-level redeclaration is still an error. (`tests/cases/scope/`)

Genuine VOID recursion (no value return position) still infers `void`; a genuinely base-case-less value cycle (`ping`→`pong`→`ping`, no concrete basis) still reports `cannot infer a return type`. ## Codegen, memory & runtime (Track B)

- **A STRUCT LITERAL EVALUATES ITS INITIALISERS IN SOURCE ORDER, NOT LAYOUT ORDER — and the ruling is written for every expression list, not for the one construct that broke (D1510; DECISIONS.md §"Evaluation order is source order")** — reported by the language's first external consumer as VL-018: `{ b: next(), a: next(), c: next() }` printed `2 1 3`, because a struct row's fields are laid out sorted by NAME (D622), `struct.new` takes its operands that way, and `emitObj` called `emitExpr` on each initialiser at the moment it pushed it. **Check-clean, running, wrong answer** — every field gets a value of the right type, so nothing in the type system can see it; in the consumer's program it permuted a nine-byte record read written `{ playerId: c.readU8(), download: c.readU8(), … }` and gave every field its ALPHABETICAL neighbour's byte. `emitObj` and `emitVariantStruct` now evaluate out-of-order initialisers into scratch locals in SOURCE order and push the locals in layout order; the slots ride the LAZY list frame under codes `100 + <field code>`, minted FRESH per field because a nested literal is emitted DURING one of the outer literal's initialisers while the outer's earlier stashes are live. **The gate has two conditions and the second is what keeps the tree byte-identical**: the layout order must actually reorder something AND some initialiser must be observable (`exprEffectFree`, a fail-CLOSED whitelist over literals, identifier reads, places and arithmetic — a permutation of reads alone changes nothing). **Measured over the tree's own source**: **82** object literals in `compiler/*.vl` and `std/*.vl` are written out of layout order and **14** of them have an observable initialiser, so 68 keep the push-in-place lowering and the seed grows **272 bytes** for the 14 that cannot. A single `pushFieldStorage` table now serves both writers — the type section's field list and the stash local that has to hold its value — moved into the byte layer, with `sFieldStorageSlot` / `uFieldStorageSlot` the one place the three tables a field code can name are chosen between (it replaces `emit_sections`'s private copy). **Nine object-literal PRODUCERS graded before and after**, all wrong before and all correct after: plain, annotated, return, argument, nested (inner and outer orders both), union arm at the named and the anonymous spelling, a list of literals, a map value. **And the fixture convention was the blind spot** — every object-literal fixture in the corpus initialises from constants, which cannot tell the two orders apart — so `tests/cases/eval-order/` is a new family with one member per expression-list construct (call arguments, list literal, map store, struct literal plain / annotated / nested / union-arm, binary operands, n-ary string concat, UFCS receiver, and the consumer's own nine-field record read), each driving the same `next()` counter: the five struct-literal members FAIL on master's seed and pass here, and every other construct passes on both. Probe `scripts/capability-probes/struct-literal-source-order.vl` (105 of 105 run).
- **AN INFERRED-EMPTY LIST PUSHED STRUCT LITERALS NOW BUILDS — the ref-list ROW is minted from the CHECKER's element type, not only from a `<shape>[]` SPELLING (D1511, reported by the first external consumer as VL-017)** — `const xs = []` / `xs.push({y: 1, x: 2})` / `print(xs[0].y)` was `vl check` rc 0 followed by `emitProgram: field access receiver is not a struct`, at the direct index read, a bound `const p = xs[0]`, a `for p in xs`, inside a function body and under a closure capture — and the SAME two lines with **no read at all** were check-clean INVALID WASM (`type mismatch: expected i32, found (ref $type)`), so the row is clause 1 as well as clause 2. **Both reps, off `wasm-dis`**: the annotated `const xs: P[] = []` gives the binding `(struct (mut (ref $5)) …)` over `$5 = (array (mut (ref null $0)))` — the ref-list wrapper at the element's own slot — while the inferred spelling took `(struct (mut (ref $1)) …)` over `$1 = (array (mut i32))`, the **i32-list default**, with neither ref-list type present anywhere in the module. **It was "no row", not "a row the read site cannot reach"**, and an `emitFail` probe inside `synthEmptyListAnn` says so in one line: `synElem={y: i32, x: i32} nom=#anon0 rlSlot=-1` — `collectAnonShapes` had minted the `#anon0` struct row and `arrElemNominalOfTy` resolved it correctly; - **STRING BUILDING IS LOWERED, NOT SPELLED — a `+` chain allocates ONCE and a loop-local accumulator appends in place, so the O(n²) shape is gone without a builder in the source** (owner direction: "optimize string building at the compiler level, without the user having to use an actual builder pattern"; `docs/internals/perf-opportunities-2026-09.md` Part D options A and B, C refused). **A — n-ary concat.** `a + b + c + d` was three `__str_concat__` calls, each allocating an exact-fit backing and copying the whole accumulated prefix, and every interpolation is such a chain because `parseTemplate` desugars `"…\{x}…"` into one in the PARSER. `strCatParts` flattens the maximal chain and `emitStrCatN` buys it with ONE sized allocation and one `array.copy` per part; two parts keep the call, so a program with no 3+ chain is byte-identical. The part pool is minted LAZILY into the list frame during lowering (`liBack` code 18), which is why no scan has to predict the arity — a reservation the emitter discovers cannot desync from it. **B — the loop-local accumulator.** `let s = ""` then `s = s + piece` inside a loop now appends IN PLACE into slack the binding's own grow path allocated (capacity doubling). **The buffer is the string's own backing**, so there is no builder local and no materialisation step: `s` is a valid string at every instant, and a read, an alias, a `.slice`, a `break`, a `return` or a nested loop inside the accumulating loop disqualifies nothing. **Exactness is one invariant** — `s` may only hold a literal, a fresh concat result, or one of its own buffers; literals and concat results are exact-fit by construction (`collectStrPool` gives every literal its own `array.new_fixed`), so the first append after either always grows, and every view of `s` has `start + len <= s.len` while the append writes only past it. `strAccScan` enforces it: a function LOCAL declared exactly once as a mutable `let` with a string-literal initialiser, every assignment a self-append or a literal, no part of an append mentioning it, no nested function mentioning it, and at least one self-append inside a loop. **MEASURED**: the compiler's own emitted `call $__str_concat__` sites **2,649 → 399**, `__str_concat__` self% of a self-compile **0.66% → 0.26%**, L2 self-compile CPU **10.04 s → 7.69 s** interleaved at load ~110 (the seed grows 1,833,871 → 1,992,504 bytes and still compiles itself faster), and a 40,000-append loop **0.805 s → 0.02 s** against std's `join` at 0.028 s — pinned as a new RUNTIME pair in `tests/vl_scaling_shape_test.ts` (ratio 16.10 on master, 0.32 now, bar 2.5). **BYTE-IDENTITY** over `tests/cases/**/*.vl` built by both seeds: 2,792 modules, **2,184 identical**, **107 differ and every one carries a 3+ chain or a loop accumulator**, 501 refuse under both, 0 rc-differing. Remainder: a module-GLOBAL accumulator is still quadratic — the analysis is per function — filed in ROADMAP item 7. DECISIONS.md records the naming choice. (#2199)
- **SERDE STAGE 0: VL CAN RENDER AND READ A FLOAT, AND `std:base64` EXISTS** — `docs/serde-design.md`'s stage-0 prerequisites, std-only apart from one blocking compiler fix (below). `std:fmt`'s `toStr` gains an **f64 arm** — shortest round-trip via Steele & White / Burger–Dybvig over exact big integers (no Ryū tables, no 128-bit multiply: 32-bit limbs inside an i64 leave room for every partial product) laid out by **ECMA-262 `Number::toString`**, so `print(x.toStr())` and `print(x)` are the same characters. `parseF64(self: string): f64 | null` is the inverse, correctly rounded at every halfway case — Clinger's fast path (≤15 digits, |exp| ≤ 22, one exact rounding) over an exact num/den fallback with a 55-step binary long division and ties-to-even, significand capped at 800 digits with a truncation flag (the classic 767-digit bound plus slack). Overflow answers ±Infinity and underflow ±0; `null` is the SYNTAX channel only. Graded against the ECMAScript oracle, which is the specification and not a second implementation: **50,000 pseudo-random bit patterns render identically to `String(v)` and round-trip bit-for-bit (0 exceptions, -0 → +0 and NaN → a NaN by the style's own rule), and 205,844 parse inputs — 200,000 random plus 5,844 adversarial (exact midpoints between adjacent doubles, ±1 decimal ulp, 900-zero truncated tails, the subnormal boundary) — agree with `Number(s)` 205,844 of 205,844.** New `std:base64` (RFC 4648 §4, standard alphabet, padded, `encodeBase64`/`decodeBase64`) refuses non-canonical trailing bits so decode∘encode is an exact identity, and answers `u8[] | Base64Error` with a literal-union `kind`. **THE HOST'S `print` IS THE ONE THAT DEVIATES**: `js_number_to_string` re-formats digits from Rust's `{:e}`, which breaks an exact decimal tie away from even where ECMA-262 breaks it to even — 14 of 50,000 vectors, smallest witness bits `4835952189745799117` (exactly 2023347301156851.25) where V8 and `std:fmt` print `…851.2` and the Rust host prints `…851.3`. That is a pre-existing cross-host divergence, pinned by `tests/vl_std_float_text_test.ts` so a host fix flips the test. THREE capability probes filed on the way: `u8[] | null` does not lower (which is why base64 carries an error struct), `.pop()` on an `i64[]` LOCAL is check-clean invalid wasm while the parameter spelling refuses loudly, and — the one this change made REACHABLE rather than found — an `f32` widens losslessly into the new `f64` arm, so `x.toStr()` over an `f32` went from a clean checker error to `vl check` rc 0 plus `emitProgram: union atom has no value box`. - **`print(<literal-union atom>)` evaluated its argument ONCE PER MEMBER — a call argument ran once per member of the type** — the atom→string widen had TWO homes: the shared `select` tower (`emitAtomToStr`, reached by `+` concat, a `string` argument position, a `string` return), which stashes the interned id once and re-reads the STASH per member; and a hand-rolled per-member `if id == <member> { print "<member>" }` chain in the print handler, which re-read the RECEIVER per member. Re-reading a place is free; re-reading a CALL is another call. So `type K = "a" | "b"` with `function f(): K { print("S") return "a" }` printed `S` / `a` / `S` — `vl check` clean, module valid, right value, **wrong number of evaluations**. - **`%` is INTEGER-ONLY — a float operand was type-checking clean and emitting `i32.rem_s` over an f64** — the f32 and f64 slices of `emitBinExprNode` ask their opcode table for the operator, get `-1` because wasm has no `f64.rem`/`f32.rem`, and **fell through to the i32 tail at the bottom of the function**, which emitted an i32 opcode over an operand already on the stack as a float. In a 272-cell grid (17 operators × 16 ordered scalar pairings, annotated params) `%` was the **only** operator with broken cells — **6 of 272**: `f64%f64`, `f64%f32`, `f32%f32`, `f32%f64`, `f64%i32`, `i32%f64`, plus every literal (`5.5 % 2.0`) and inferred-local spelling of the same. Both operands annotated, so this was never an inference gap. **The lowering that looks obvious is not fmod, and measuring it is what decided the fix**: against Rust's `%` on f64 (which IS C `fmod`) the identity `a - trunc(a / b) * b` disagrees on **86,066 of 200,000** random pairs at ordinary magnitudes (43.0%) and **98,980 of 200,000** across |exp| ≤ 300 (49.5%), and on 10 of 33 curated edge cases — every `|a / b|` past 2^53 (`1e17 % 3` → 0, not 1), a `-0.0` dividend (sign lost), an infinite divisor (NaN instead of the dividend), and `f64::MAX % 3` overflows to `-inf`. Accepting through it would have traded a loud invalid-wasm reject for silent numeric corruption. So `%` joins the bitwise/shift family's integer-only rule and reports in its diagnostic shape, naming both operands — `operator '%' is integer-only, got i32 and f64` — and the three mixed pairings that previously said `mixes f32 and i32` now name the actual reason. **Verdicts move in one direction only: the grid's CLEAN count is unchanged at 128 and REJECT is +6, exactly the six formerly-broken cells**; no corpus program uses float `%`. Independently, both wide-scalar slices now `emitFail` on a `-1` opcode instead of falling through, so the i32 tail is unreachable with a float on the stack however that state is entered — verified by removing the checker rule and watching `operator '%' has no f64 form` / `no f32 form` fire at both widths. Exact float remainder needs a scaled shift-and-subtract helper (verified exact: 0 mismatches over the same 400,000 pairs), and when it lands it belongs beside `sqrt`/`trunc`/`copysign` as a float intrinsic — the shape every float operation with no operator spelling already uses. (`tests/cases/arith/float-remainder-reject.vl`, `float-remainder-f32-reject.vl`, `integer-remainder-control.vl`)

The capture-only spelling goes **12 invalid-wasm cells → 1 in every annotation variant** and is now annotation-neutral; the param-taking spelling goes **11 → 1**; the 1 left in each is `f64 %`, which is D7's emitter fall-through and fails fully annotated. **150 running cells print exactly what their fully-annotated twin prints.** What remains is the **i32 arm's loud value-floor reject** (`emitClosureValue`) for a nested function whose own parameter is un-annotated — that one IS the parameter default, it fires whether or not the outer binding is annotated, and it is correct. Each of the three scalar arms was measured failing with it removed, so none is dead. (`tests/cases/functions/capture-scalar-kind.vl`, `capture-only-return-kind.vl`)
- **A top-level scalar `let`/`const` becomes a START-FUNCTION LOCAL, not a module global (#1321)** — the script spelling of a hot loop was **4.13× slower** than the identical loop inside a function, because a top-level binding emitted `global.get`/`global.set` per iteration where an in-function one emitted `local.get`/`local.set`; wasmtime keeps locals in registers but must treat a mutable global as observable state. `wasm-opt --closed-world -O3 --gufa` does NOT promote them (measured: 16.5 s after, 7 global ops still in the loop, and the globals were neither exported nor read by a second function), so this belonged in the emitter. A 10^9-iteration f64 accumulate goes **1,767 ms → 497 ms** and now **converges with the in-function spelling** (572 ms) — the two emit byte-identical loop bodies, which is what makes the convergence the instrument rather than the ratio. **182 of 1,442 buildable corpus programs promote, 538 bindings**; corpus bytes net **−974** with **+0 on every one of the 1,260 programs that promote nothing**. A binding stays a global if it is a ref cell, if its module has no top-level statements, or if its name appears in ANY function body (name-keyed, so a same-named local vetoes conservatively — the walk runs in the direction where a hole costs population, not soundness). Refuted while building: relaxing the no-top-level-statements gate does NOT help the compiler — a probe rebuilt with it relaxed still emits 2,280 globals unchanged, because module state read from function bodies is what a compiler's top level IS, so the self-compile qualifies zero bindings. Also: the behavioural corpus is BLIND to this (a sabotage disabling promotion leaves every `@log` correct), which is why the new suite counts global-section entries; and 8 corpus RUN divergences are the hex address in a wasm trap backtrace, identical after normalizing `0x<hex>` (verified: 27 trap fixtures, 8 differ, 8 address-only, 0 real). (`docs/internals/perf-program.md` §11, `tests/vl_global_promotion_test.ts`, `tests/cases/globals/promoted-scalar-start-locals.vl`)
- **The union box is built at ONE site per function, not one per ARM (#1322)** — a two-armed producer emitted a `struct.new` in each `return`, and binaryen's Heap2Local scalarizes PER ALLOCATION SITE, so two sites merging into one returned value meant neither could own it and the box survived every optimization level. The return path now writes a tag local and a payload local and branches to a single exit that constructs the box once: **box sites 2 → 1 per two-armed producer, 78 removed corpus-wide across 76 functions in 54 modules.** **The win is entirely downstream of `wasm-opt` and must be quoted with its level** — on a 100 M-trip loop, min-of-5: plain `vl build` 535 → 530 ms (a WASH), `-O` 304 → **173 ms (1.76×)**, `-O3` 293 → 176 ms (1.66×). The sink removes a *merge point*, not an allocation — A and B both allocate exactly two objects per trip before the optimizer, since only one of A's two sites executes on any given trip. Four claims of the design doc it implements were refuted by building it: the 2.0–2.2× figure is **V8-only** (natively 1.7×); the box melts at plain **`-O`**, a rung earlier than "closed-world type refinement" predicted, because the ceiling was never binaryen's but the site count; the 309-site population is ~4× what is removable (a *k*-return function loses *k−1*, a single-exit function loses none); and the cost estimate touched none of the 18 construction sites — the fix is a peephole at three return terminators. Bytes +18 per sunk function (corpus +1,379, +0.069%) while the `-O3` artifact gets SMALLER. Does not sink: a `return` of an if-expression (`emitUnionIfValue` still boxes per arm — the largest remaining shape), a `let` assigned on two branches, passthrough returns, single-exit functions. (`docs/internals/unboxed-union-rep-design.md` §10, `tests/vl_union_return_sink_test.ts`)
- **The union box sinks past a BINDING's if-arms too — and this one is worth something WITHOUT `wasm-opt`** — `const u: A | B = if c { a } else { b }` had **three** construction sites, not two, and the third is the finding: the binding's slot is a non-null `(ref $uBox)`, which is not defaultable, and a void-`if` merge does not satisfy the validator's definite-assignment check, so the rep's NULL BOX was built before the `if` and overwritten on every path — allocated every trip, read by nothing. Each arm now writes the tag/payload pair and the single `struct.new` follows the `if`; that one store dominates every read, so the pre-seed is not merely redundant but unnecessary and the shape drops from `arms + 1` sites to ONE. **Box sites 1,551 → 1,498 corpus-wide (53 removed over 6 modules), +55 B (+0.0022%), 6 up 0 down**, and the six byte movers are exactly the six site movers. **The rung story is NOT #1322's and must not be quoted as it** — that sink removes a merge point, so A and B allocate identically and plain `vl build` was a wash; this one removes an ALLOCATION, so on a 100 M-trip loop (CPU ms, min-of-7 interleaved, load 80–88) plain `vl build` is **1.36×** (750 → 551), `-O` **1.68×** (594 → 354), `-O3` 1.50× (558 → 372), distributions non-overlapping at every rung. The two sinks SHARE one reserved local pair, because their live ranges cannot interleave — a sunk `return` branches straight to the exit block, a sunk arm falls straight to the `if`'s `end`, and an arm's value is an expression so no `return` can be emitted between an arm's write and the construction that reads it (witnessed both nestings by `tests/cases/unions/let-if-binding-sink-with-returns.vl`). Two arm shapes DECLINE and the gate is static: a nested if-expression arm ends in a frame `end` rather than a construction, and a PASSTHROUGH arm builds nothing — unlike a declining return, a declining arm cannot be tolerated per-arm, since the single join would have to unbox and rebuild it, trading no site for an allocation that executes every trip. **What is left of §10.4's `let` row is not a sink**: `let u = a; if c { u = b }` writes the slot from two separate statements with no merge point, and collapsing it means holding the pair across a liveness window — a rep question, filed with its before-number rather than forced. (`docs/internals/unboxed-union-rep-design.md` §12, `tests/fixtures/opt-melt/union-sink-let-if.vl`, `tests/cases/unions/let-if-binding-arms.vl`)
- **B0 Numeric literals, i32/f64 arithmetic, if/while, direct calls, start fn, memory builtins.**
- **B1 Allocation = WasmGC** (binaryen 116→130 for GC API). → `DECISIONS.md`
- **B2 Numeric codegen (core)** — i64 & f32 arithmetic + float `/` & comparisons; i64/f32 type mappings; range-aware integer-literal defaults.
- **B2 Value-level bitwise/shift operators** — `& | ^ ~ << >> >>>`, integer-only, i32/i64 → native wasm instructions (#99; H4.2 self-host gap).
- **B2 Explicit numeric casts — `x as T`** — a postfix, CHECKED conversion between numeric scalars (`i32`/`i64`/`f32`/`f64`). Unlike the implicit lossless-widening rule (`numWidensName`, unchanged), `as` permits EVERY direction: widenings + the lossy widenings (`i32→f32`, `i64→f64/f32`), narrowings (`i64→i32` wrap, `f64→f32` demote) and int↔float. Float→int uses the TRAPPING `trunc` family — NaN / out-of-range aborts (traps-are-for-bugs). `as` is a CONTEXTUAL keyword (stays an identifier; `import { a as b }` untouched), binds tighter than every binary operator (`a + b as f64` is `a + (b as f64)`), and is chainable. The lossy-implicit reject now points at `as`. Native fixpoint byte-identical. (`tests/cases/numerics/as-cast-*.vl`)

- **B4 Closures (first WasmGC codegen)** — nested decls, capture analysis, env struct, escaping closures.
- **B5 Objects (core)** — literals, read/write, nested, f64 fields, args/returns, reassignment, captured-in-closures, excess-property width subtyping, function-valued fields + member-call; method-shorthand `{ add(a,b){…} }`.
- **B6 Growable `T[]` (core)** — `{backing,len,cap}` WasmGC struct monomorphized per element type; 2× growth; `[...]` seed; `a[i]`/`a[i]=v` trap on OOB; `.length`/`.get(i)`/`push`/`pop`/`clear`/`+`; for-in + structural equality updated. (`compiler/builtins/lists.ts`; → `docs/collections-design.md`) `.capacity` removed (leaky growth detail; `cap` stays internal). → `DECISIONS.md`
- **B6b Build-loop fusion** — a loop building a fresh local list by one push per iteration — `for i in A to B [step S] { a.push(e) }` or the counter-`while` `while i <cmp> N { a.push(e); i = i ± C }` — lowers to a pre-sized indexed fill, ~3–4× faster than per-element push (elides the frontier bounds-check the engine can't); unified recognizer → one fill core, guard-gated, falls back to push otherwise. (`tests/cases/lists/build-fusion-*`; → `DECISIONS.md`)

(`compiler/builtins/maps.ts`) A map whose VALUE type is the enclosing recursive type (`{ [string]: Tree }`) now compiles — the hash struct + its `vals` array thread into the type's WasmGC rec group (mirrors A11 array-element recursion). Only the hash (a murmur3 finalizer mix — an identity hash clusters fourCC tables into a linear scan) and the compare (`i32.eq` instead of a call into `__str_eq__`) differ; the probe's tombstone skip, the stored-hash gate, `__map_resize__`, the compaction and the insertion-ORDERED iteration are literally shared, so a delete/re-insert interleaving prints the same order under both keys. The pin is **key-BLIND**: the filing named the i32 key, but the string key was refused identically, and the measured population is symmetric. (2) **An inferred key skipped the unsupported-key gate.** The map rep hashes exactly two key types (`mapKeyTySupported`), and only the ANNOTATION was checked against it — so `const m: {[f64]: V} = Map()` is a clean type error while `const m = Map(); m.set(1.5, v)` passed `vl check` and died in codegen as `emitProgram: map key is not a string`. The pin now raises the annotation's own diagnostic (one wording, `mapKeyUnsupportedErr`, shared by both sites; the constructor word follows the flavor, so a `Set()` says `Set`). A hole key (an un-annotated parameter reaching `m.set(k, v)`) is deliberately NOT adjudicated — it is unsolved, and the call site owns it. **The rule for the pinned key is the BASE type**: `m[1] = "x"` pins `i32` and `m["a"] = 1` pins `string`, matching what `.set` has always pinned, so a later `f64`/`string` key is a clean `map key must be i32, got …` rather than a widen. Reject parity: **0 of 251 corpus `@error` cases changed verdict** (1,747 passed / 0 failed / 7 ignored). **Still open, measured here and filed rather than folded in — two EMITTER shape defects that the `.set` spelling already exposed** (the 288 residue, all `ann=OK`): an un-annotated map-returning function (`function mk() { return Map() }`) emits the default shape for the hole and rejects `emitProgram: map values must be i32 / boolean`, and a bare `Map()` inside an object literal (`const s = { m: Map() }`) rejects `emitProgram: ref valtype with no interned shape` — 144 cells each. - **B14 Free INDEX OPERATORS (`function "[]"` / `function "[]="`, webcraft P1.1's bracket)** — `x[i]` and `x[i] = v` on a user type lower to a DIRECT call to a free function whose NAME is the operator. A quoted string is the spelling, because `[` and `]` open an index expression everywhere else so the bracket operators have no operator TOKEN (the form accepts every operator name, so `function "+"(self, b)` and `function +(self, b)` are the same function). **Overloadable by receiver**: a program may declare several `"[]"`, one per receiver type — the parser mints a declaration name carrying the receiver (`[]@F32View`; `@` cannot occur in an identifier, so the encoding is total and a genuine duplicate still collides on the ordinary redeclaration rule), and **dispatch is by the receiver's TYPE** (`assignable` to the `self` parameter, the same test UFCS uses), never by the spelling in the name — which is what lets `F32View` and `I32View`, structurally identical and distinguished only by their A14 brands, carry different operators. The `self` annotation is required. **Merge-safe with no alias**: unlike a UFCS member-call, a bracket names nothing, so the checker's operator registry — built from the already-MERGED program — holds mangled names from the start. The checker BANKS its resolution on the site node and the emitter's rewrite reads it back, so the two can never disagree. Nesting composes (`g[i][j]`); `x[i] += v` works and inherits the native-array rule that a compound assignment re-evaluates receiver and index (measured, not new). **The swallow**: array / map / string / hole indexing is untouched — six-channel corpus differential over 1,638 files reads zero rows differing on any field, with a live inverted control. `std:buffer` gains four one-line operators forwarding to its accessors, which lands P1.1's spelling; `x[i]` vs `getF32(x, i)` build modules differing in TWO bytes (the `call` immediate — one extra forward, which `-O3 --closed-world` inlines). (`docs/internals/index-operator-design.md`, `tests/cases/index/operator-*.vl`, `tests/cases/modules/index-operator-import/`, `tests/cases/std/buffer-view-bracket.vl`)
- **B15a Default + optional parameters (webcraft "API ergonomics")** — `p: T = <literal>` and `p?: T` parse, check and lower. **Defaults subsume optionals**: `p?: T` is desugared IN THE PARSER to `p: T | null = null`, so one mechanism serves both spellings and only a faithful-surface marker (`Param.parOpt`, the `IsExpr.isNeg` pattern) survives for the printer to reprint the `?`. A call that omits trailing arguments — or, when NAMED, skips a middle one (`add(1, c: 5)`) — is normalized to the callee's full arity by `emit_rewrite`'s `drwFillDefaults`, which runs BEFORE monomorphization and signature collection, so mono, `collectCloSigs` and the emitter's per-parameter coercion all see an ordinary full-arity call. **The `$fnsig` value-call ABI is untouched, measured not asserted**: `fnSigKeyOf` derives a closure signature key exclusively from the DECLARATION's parameter list, never from a call site's argument count, and the rewrite resolves its callee with the same `fnIndexOfInScopeChain` classifier `emitCall` uses to choose the direct path — so a function VALUE keeps full arity and `const kv = k; kv(1)` stays the arity error it was. The design's four leak points are closed at the declaration, each with a pinned reject: a default must be a **literal** (it is emitted in the CALLER's frame, so a name in it would either read a parameter that does not exist there or capture a caller-local of the same name — this is what makes an earlier-parameter reference and a call/allocation default rejections rather than surprises); a default must be **annotated** (an un-annotated parameter is an inference HOLE each call site pins, so keeping holes and defaults disjoint leaves the monomorphizer's instance keying untouched); defaults are **trailing-only**; and a defaulted parameter's annotation may not name one of the function's own **type parameters** (an omitted argument would drop a binding site). The call-site arity gate becomes a RANGE and the diagnostic names it (`expected 1 to 2, got 0`). A call's declaration is now resolved through `fnDeclScopes`, a stack parallel to `T.scopes` in the shape `constScopes` already establishes, so a NESTED function takes its defaults too and a local binding shadowing a function name answers "not a declaration" and keeps the exact-arity gate. Out of scope by ruling, with a pinned reject: **UFCS** dispatch still matches a `self`-function by exact arity, because widening it there changes what counts as a method call rather than only which arguments get filled. (`tests/cases/functions/default-params.vl`, `optional-params.vl`, `error-default-param-*.vl`, `error-optional-param-*.vl`)
- **std:str — the string method surface (`strings-design.md` §Methods step 1)** — VL's core string vocabulary is SIX operations (`slice`/`indexOf`/`includes`/`charCodeAt`/`fromCodePoint`/`toString` plus `+`, `==`, `.length`, `s[i]`, `for cp in s`) and **you could not split a string**. A new pure-VL module (`std/str.vl`) closes it with 15 exports — `split`, `join`, `trim`/`trimStart`/`trimEnd`, `startsWith`/`endsWith`, `lastIndexOf`, `replace`/`replaceAll`, `repeat`, `padStart`/`padEnd`, `toUpperAscii`/`toLowerAscii` — every one `self`-first, so they read as UFCS methods on a string receiver (`"a,b,c".split(",").join("|")`). **No compiler change of any kind**: it is written over the six primitives, and the design doc's sequencing reason is that the library is the TEST SUITE for the coming UTF-8 rep swap — 163 pinned corpus lines across `tests/cases/std/str-*.vl`, asserted with `==` and slices rather than `.length` over multi-byte characters, so they survive the swap and go red if it goes wrong. **Every degenerate input is ruled and pinned, following the unanimous JS/Python/Rust/Go precedent** (which `DECISIONS.md` already put the core's string methods in): an empty separator splits into characters so `"".split("")` is `[]` while `"".split(",")` is `[""]`; an empty `from` matches at every boundary so `"abc".replaceAll("", "-")` is `"-a-b-c-"`; matches never overlap so `"aaa".replaceAll("aa", "b")` is `"ba"`; padding never truncates; `repeat(n <= 0)` is `""` rather than the RangeError/panic the references raise, because VL reserves traps for bugs. The law `s.replaceAll(f, t) == s.split(f).join(t)` (non-empty `f`) holds and is a fixture, including its ONE exception. **`toUpperAscii`/`toLowerAscii` are named for their limit** — the design doc rules that an unqualified `toUpper` silently ignoring `é` is the quiet-lie class VL rejects; full mapping needs `std:unicode` (`ß`→`SS` is not even a character map). **`std:fmt` no longer implements `split`/`join`/`repeat`/`padLeft`** — it re-exports the first three from `std:str` and `padLeft` delegates to `padStart`, because VL has no namespace import and two modules exporting `split` makes importing both a HARD PARSE ERROR; measured cost of the delegation is +2,690 bytes on a `toStr`-only program (no cross-module DCE), recorded in the module header. **Two findings the work turned up, both filed in `strings-design.md` §Methods**: (1) the B7b string-accumulation fusion in `DECISIONS.md` shipped only in `compiler/toWasm.ts` and died with it — `s = s + piece` in a loop is measured QUADRATIC on the native compiler (20k/40k/80k appends → 313/1502/7614 ms), so every builder here fills one `i32[]` and calls `fromCodePoints` once, worth **28 ms vs 12,475 ms** on a 40,000-piece `join`; (2) a bare member CALL in implicit-return position (`function f(s: string) { s.slice(1, 2) }`) passes `vl check` and fails at emit with `unsupported member-call statement`, while the adjacent `s.slice(a, b).length` is pinned and works — explicit `return` is the workaround. Native fixpoint byte-identical, `deno task test` 2260 passed, native-align 2257 passed, self-lint + fmt clean. (`std/str.vl`, `std/fmt.vl`, `tests/cases/std/str-*.vl`)
- **std:array — generic array SEARCH helpers (`indexOf`/`lastIndexOf`/`includes`/`count`)** — a new pure-VL std module (`std/array.vl`, the array dual of `std:fmt`), built ENTIRELY on the intrinsic list floor (`.length` / indexing / `==`) — no emitter changes. Each is `<T>`-generic over the element type and takes a `self` first parameter, so `import { indexOf, includes } from "std:array"` then `xs.indexOf(3)` / `ss.includes("b")` read as UFCS methods, one definition serving `i32[]`, `string[]`, … (`==` resolves per element type). This is the SEARCH family (each returns i32 / boolean, building no new collection); the array-BUILDING methods (`slice`, `reverse`, `reduce`, index-aware `map`) are deferred — a generic `const out = []` / a `(x: T) => …` callback inside a generic body does not yet propagate the element type `T` through monomorphization (three distinct generics-monomorphization gaps), so they would mis-lower for a non-i32 element rather than ship i32-only. Native fixpoint byte-identical, deno corpus 542, native sweep PASS=407. (`std/array.vl`, `tests/cases/modules/std-array/entry.vl`)
- **A10 generics: a generic CLOSURE parameter `(A, T) => A` monomorphizes (+ `std:array` `reduce`)** — a `<T>`-generic function may now take a closure parameter whose type rides the type params, so `fold<T, A>(self: T[], f: (A, T) => A, init: A)` instantiates per call shape. The monomorphizer's three type-substitution helpers — `monoAnnHasTyParam` (does the annotation carry a type param?), `monoBindFromAnn` (bind them from the argument's concrete type), `monoSubstAnn` (substitute through the binding) — previously handled bare `T` / `T[]`, a generic-alias application `Head<…>`, and an inline object `{a: T}`, but NOT a FUNCTION-TYPE annotation `(A, T) => A`, so a generic closure param kept its un-substituted annotation and the instance body's `f(…)` value-call resolved no interned `$fnsig`. Each helper gains a function-type branch (recurse into each parameter + the return). The binding is derived from the closure ARGUMENT's function-type NAME, built by a new `monoArgFnTypeName` (`(i32, i32) => i32` from a lambda's concrete params + `cloRetTypeName` result) — distinct from the `"=>sigkey"` pin an UN-annotated closure param wants. This lands `std:array`'s `reduce<T, A>(self, f, init)` (an i32 sum, a string fold) on top of the search family. (An `f64` / `i64` accumulator stays a clean emit error — the non-i32/string closure-value floor, not invalid wasm.) Native fixpoint byte-identical, deno corpus 543, native sweep PASS=408. (`compiler/emit_base.vl`, `compiler/wasmEmit.vl`, `std/array.vl`, `tests/cases/functions/generic-closure-param.vl`)

Outside a generic the checker's node-type bank answers first and MASKS the gap; inside a monomorphized instance the body is a clone the checker never typed, so the substituted parameter ANNOTATION is the only boolean-ness left and the gap is the whole answer — `gtake<T>(x: T) { print(x[0]) }` over a `boolean[]` printed `1` while `x[0] == false` was correct, so the VALUE was right and only the formatter was wrong. `listAnnNameOf` is one home for the four storage classes a list receiver has (param, local, global, one INDEX level). The faithful cut is measured, not assumed: the other three i32-backed list spellings (`K[]`, `(boolean|null)[]`, `(K|null)[]`) keep master's pin and reach a LOUD floor, so declining them fails closed. - **A10 generics: a generic function's BODY may annotate its type parameter (`const x: T`, `const out: T[]`)** — a `<T>`-generic body that names its type param in a `LetDecl` annotation no longer fails `unknown type 'T'`, and lowers per instance against the CONCRETE element type. Two halves: (1) **checker** — the function's type params are kept on the `tpEnv` stack for the WHOLE body (not just around each param/return annotation as `resolveAnnot` did), so `const out: T[] = []` resolves `T` to the same opaque `TyVar` the signature binds; (2) **emitter** — the monomorphizer rewrites the instance body's `LetDecl` annotations through the binding (`const out: T[]` → `const out: f64[]`), via a new `monoCloneBody` that clones only the statement SPINE (blocks / control-flow / `LetDecl`s) and SHARES every leaf expression — INCLUDING a nested lambda, so no function node is duplicated (a clone would not be re-lifted, `collectFns` having run) and a `T`-independent body shares its arena wholesale (byte-identical, usage-gated). This reuses the already-working CONCRETE annotated path for every element type instead of per-rep usage inference, so a generic build-loop (`reverse<T>`) and a generic typed local lower for `i32` / `string` / `struct` (and `f64` LOCALS). (A generic `T[]`-returning BUILD over `f64[]` is still blocked by a SEPARATE bug — a function RETURNING `f64[]` is not yet recognised as an array at the index site — the next follow-up.) That reject names the function, the un-annotated parameters, and the concrete signatures the program's own call sites already pin (`Call sites pin \`add\` at (i32, i32), (f64, f64)`), or says plainly that nothing pins it. - **B17 lints: dead/constant branch + degenerate `for` step** — two more lint rules (`compiler/lint.ts`). **Constant condition** (`code: constant-condition`, `warning`, `unnecessary` tag = grey-out) flags a branch whose literal-boolean condition makes it unreachable: an `if false { … }` body, the `else` (and later arms) of an `if true { … }`, and a `while false { … }` body. Literal-only — no general constant folding; recurses into nested bodies. **Degenerate `for` step** (`code: for-step-zero`, `error`) flags a range `for` written with a literal `step 0` — it never advances the loop variable (an infinite loop), the case the parser's empty-range warning deliberately excludes (an empty-range check can't fire when the step is zero); points at the `step 0` expression. (`tests/cases/lint/dead-branch-if-false.vl`, `dead-branch-if-true-else.vl`, `dead-branch-while-false.vl`, `for-step-zero.vl`)
- **B17 lint: unused-function** — a non-exported top-level `function` that is never referenced anywhere in its file is dead code in a whole-program compile; flagged with a `warning` (`code: unused-function`, `source: vital`, `unnecessary` tag = grey-out) — `Unused function \`f\` (prefix with \`_\` to suppress, remove it, or \`export\` it)`. EXPORTED functions are NEVER flagged (public API — VL is multi-file, so an `export function` may be imported and called by another module). A `_`-prefixed name is the "intentionally unused" convention and downgrades to a `hint` (greyed, not a warning), mirroring the unused-variable rule. Reuses that rule's reference model (the symbol table's non-decl occurrences) and additionally consults an AST-level call/value-reference set so FORWARD/mutually-recursive calls (resolved against a hoisted signature before the real binding is declared) and UFCS/operator-method calls (`x.m(…)`, `a + b`, which the parser desugars to a named `FunctionCall`) count as uses — a function reachable from any call site is never falsely flagged. The LSP offers the `_`-prefix quick-fix (no multi-line removal). (`tests/cases/lint/unused-function.vl`, `exported-function-no-warn.vl`, `called-function-no-warn.vl`, `mutual-recursion-no-warn.vl`, `tests/lint_unused_function_test.ts`)
- **B17 fix: `run`/`build` suppress info/hint advisories** — `vl run` and `vl build` now apply a `warning` display floor (via the existing `meetsThreshold` helper): errors (still blocking) and warnings (dead code, empty intersections) print, but info/hint-level style lints (e.g. prefer-`const`) are suppressed — those are the job of `vl check` and the editor, not noise on every run. `vl check` is unchanged and still shows the full set.
- **B19 `return` / early returns** — early, from loops, fall-through; bare `return` yields null.
- **B-debug Name section + source maps + trap-to-source** — wasm name section + Source Map v3 (binaryen debug locations, survives `optimize()`); trap → precise VL `file:L:C` error message. (#76)
- **B6 Nullable-list narrow-then-use codegen fix** — a `T[] | null` narrowed to non-null (`if xs != null { … }`) then read into a list op (`xs[i]`, `xs[i]=v`, `xs + …`, `for…in`, `map`/`filter`) no longer crashes binaryen's `LocalSubtyping` (`isSubType` assertion): narrowing is type-level only, so the value keeps its nullable `(ref null $list)` slot, and stashing it in the op's non-null `(ref $list)` local was a subtype violation. Each such read now `ref.as_non_null`s the list (the narrowing guarantees non-null). Reproduces non-recursively with `i32[] | null`; found by the A11 array lane. (`tests/cases/types/nullable-list-index.vl`)
- **B-arrow-lambdas — arrow `(params) => body` is the SOLE anonymous-function syntax; `function(…)` expression form removed; lambdas debug-name from their binding** — an anonymous function is now written `(n: i32) => n * 2` (bare-expression body) or `(n) => { … }` (block body), and the old `function(n: i32) n * 2` EXPRESSION form is REJECTED — a `function` token in expression position reports `anonymous functions use arrow syntax \`(params) => body\`, not \`function(...)\`` (a named `function f(…)` DECLARATION is a statement, dispatched before expression parsing, so it is untouched; object method shorthand `{ m(a) {…} }` is untouched). The change is a pure SURFACE swap: an arrow lambda parses to the SAME nameless `FuncDecl` the old form produced, so the checker (un-annotated param inference from callback position, capture analysis) and the emitter (the fat-pointer closure value + `call_ref`) are byte-for-byte unchanged — only the front-door syntax moved. **Parser:** a `(` in expression position scans to its matching `)` and branches to a lambda iff `=>` immediately follows (a grouped expression's `)` never is), so `(a + b) * c` stays grouped and a function-typed param `(f: (i32) => i32) => f(3)` resolves the OUTER `)` past the nested arrow; the param list and bare/block/object body are shared with the `function`-keyword tail (factored into `parseParamList` + `parseFuncBodyAndBuild`). **Formatter:** anonymous functions now print as arrow — MANDATORY, since emitting `function(…)` would no longer re-parse; the 27 corpus fixtures + object method/field values were migrated via `vl fmt` and the result is idempotent. **Debug naming:** a directly-bound lambda `const foo = (n) => …` takes the binding name in the wasm name section, so a wasmtime trap backtrace reads `vl!foo` instead of `vl!__lambda_N` (an unbound `.map((n) => …)` callback keeps `__lambda_N`). The display name is DECOUPLED from resolution — a parallel `fnDispNames` array, populated at lift time, read ONLY by the name section, never entering `fnNameMap` (reusing `fnName` collided: the checker saw `redeclared foo`; and a `{[string]: string}` map mis-lowers with `?? ""`, so an array is used). Native fixpoint byte-identical, deno corpus 535, native sweep PASS=402. (`tests/cases/functions/arrow-lambda.vl`, `lambda.vl`, `arrays/map-filter-arrow.vl`)
- **B-closure-nonref-params — a function VALUE may take a function-typed / string / list / struct-list parameter** — the closure-call ABI's PARAMETER spine, previously limited to i32 / f64 / struct, now mirrors the already-broad RESULT spine. A lifted lambda used as a value (`const call3 = (g: (i32) => i32) => g(3)`) whose param is a closure (`(i32) => i32`), `string`, `i32[]` / `string[]` / `f64[]`, or a struct list (`P[]`) now lowers: its env-leading `$fnsig` encodes the param valtype via a new `cloParamTok`, so the call site `ref.cast`s the funcref to the RIGHT functype. Before, any non-i32/f64/struct param made `fnSigKeyOf`/`cloSigKeyExt` yield "", so no `$fnsig` was interned and the value call fell back to the all-i32 ARITY signature — casting e.g. a `(ref $cloStruct)`-param funcref to a `(…, i32) → i32` functype, which trapped wasm validation (`expected i32, found (ref …)`). The functype EMITTER already wrote `fbValtype(vtKindOfParam, …)` per param, so only the interning KEY needed widening; the annotation-string path (`annParamKind`, used to resolve a value call over a `g: (string) => i32` higher-order param) was widened in lockstep so both producers mint the identical key. **Soundness floor:** the kinds still outside the param ABI — an `i64`/`f32`, a nullable-ref (`T | null`), a union, or a map parameter (and an `f32` return) — keep `cloSigKeyExt` "" and are now REJECTED at the value site (`emitClosureValue`) with a clear message (`a function value's signature is not yet supported — …`) instead of mis-casting to the arity signature and emitting invalid wasm. (A named function with these types, called directly, is unaffected.) Native fixpoint byte-identical, deno corpus 536, native sweep PASS=402. (`tests/cases/functions/closure-value-nonref-params.vl`)
- **B-lambda-inferred-return — an anonymous lambda's inferred non-i32 return through a VARIABLE classifies correctly** — an arrow lambda with an un-annotated return whose tail is a plain `let`-bound variable of a non-i32 type (`const f = () => { const x: i64 = 42; return x }`, and the `f64` / `string` / `i32[]` / `string[]` counterparts) no longer emits invalid wasm (`expected i32, found i64`). The emitter's return classifier reads the checker's `A20` inferred-return table to type a return the expression-based fallback misses (a bare variable), but that table was keyed by function NAME — and a lambda is anonymous at check time, lifted to a `__lambda_N` name the checker never assigned, so `inferRetNameOf("__lambda_N")` missed and the return defaulted to i32 while the body produced the wider type. The checker now ALSO records an anonymous lambda's inferred return under a NODE-INDEX sentinel key (`#<nodeIx>`, read by `inferRetNameByNode`) — recorded in `checkFuncDeclNode` exactly where the named path patches the hoisted `TyFunc`, gated to the real (non-quiet) pass — and the emitter consults it (by `fnStmts[i]`) when the name lookup misses. The classifiable-name set is now a shared `isClassifiableRetName` helper so the named loop and the lambda recording stay in lockstep. A NAMED function with the same body always worked; this brings lambdas to parity. (The bug predates arrow lambdas — the old `function(…)` expression form had it too.) Native fixpoint byte-identical, deno corpus 537, native sweep PASS=404. (`tests/cases/functions/lambda-inferred-nonref-return.vl`)
- **B-arrow-return-annotation — an arrow lambda may carry a return-type annotation `(params): Ret => body`** — completing parity with the `function` form (which always allowed `: Ret`). `const inc = (n: i32): i32 => n + 1`, `(): i64 => { … }`, `(): string => …`, `(): i32[] => …` all parse; the annotation flows into the SAME `fnRet` the named form uses, so the checker and emitter are unchanged. **Parser:** `looksLikeArrowLambda` now commits to a lambda when the token after the matching `)` is a `:` (a return annotation) as well as `=>` — unambiguous because `vl` has no `?:` ternary, so a `(group):` never arises in expression position (the only other place `:` follows a parenthesised thing); `parseArrowLambda` consumes the optional `(":" type)` before `=>`. **Formatter:** `arrowHeader` now prints the `: Ret` verbatim — MANDATORY, since dropping it would change meaning (a load-bearing return type, e.g. one pinning the wider `i64`/`f32` result) and the round-trip would be lossy; idempotent. The closure-RETURN kinds still outside the value ABI (`: f32`, `: i32 | null`, a closure return) parse but hit the existing `emitClosureValue` soundness floor (a clean message, not invalid wasm). Native fixpoint byte-identical, deno corpus 538, native sweep PASS=404. (`tests/cases/functions/arrow-return-annotation.vl`)
- **B-bare-expr-return-coercion — a bare-expression body returning a narrower numeric literal coerces to the declared return type** — `function f(): i64 5`, `function f(): f32 1.5`, and the arrow-lambda equivalents (`(): i64 => 5`, `(): i64 => 10 + 5`) no longer emit invalid wasm (`expected i64, found i32`). The implicit-return tail (a bare value expression, vs an explicit `return e`) shares `emitReturnValue`, which promotes a narrower literal (`5` → i64, `1.5` → f32) to the declared float/i64 result — but the implicit path passed `widenNum = false`, deliberately SKIPPING that widening to avoid mis-widening an already-typed tail (a closure `call_ref` result the float-classifier once didn't recognise), so the literal emitted at its DEFAULT type (i32 / f64) and mismatched the result valtype. That skip is now obsolete: `exprIs{F64,F32,I64}` recognise a closure-call result (and a variable, field read, etc.), so `emitExprAs{I64,F32,F64}` is a no-op pass-through on an already-correct value — making the widening safe unconditionally. The `widenNum` parameter is removed; explicit and implicit returns now share one path. A general fix (it applies to NAMED bare-expression bodies too, not just lambdas). Native fixpoint byte-identical, deno corpus 539, native sweep PASS=405. (`tests/cases/functions/bare-expr-return-coercion.vl`)

- **Rep-bug burn-down, wave 1 (fuzzer-found)** — all ten confirmed bug families from the rep fuzzer's first sweeps fixed at their roots: map value kinds across the return boundary + atom-valued maps (#814); nullable/union rep seams — `f64|null` print import, nullable-scalar-element list constructs, variant scalar-list fields — + the boolean print classifier reading the checker's recorded type (#815); i64 widening seams — lambda contextual returns adopt the expected type, numeric prims invariant inside function types, union-box tags adopt the union's atom (#816); composite-global field-code drift — atom-array fields, union-with-closure-member fields (#817); scalar leaves in literal-inferred shapes (#818); parenthesized conditions narrow like bare ones — one peel at the `setNarrowFromCond` seam + checker exhaustiveness (#819), with fuzzgen paren coverage + baseline re-pin (#820). Fixed shapes graduated from `scripts/rep-fuzz-baseline.txt` into `tests/cases/`.
- **Rep-bug burn-down, wave 2 — zero unsound outputs (soundness milestone)** — every unsound class (INVALID-WASM, TRAP, MISMATCH) driven to **0** at the pinned CI seeds; the residual is 36 shapes, ALL fail-loud REJECT (coverage gaps refused cleanly, never silent miscompiles). Waves: structural heap-type dedup so structurally-identical declared/inline types share one WasmGC heap type (#833/#834/#835); value-union box read — narrowed member extracted into a typed local (#855); map-as-closure-return heap-type identity — the captured map's env field, the closure `$fnsig` result, and the returned map all dedup to one `$mapStruct` (#860); scalar-union-arm boxing in composite position (closure return + array element) with a function type promoted to a value-union REF atom (kind 11), which also closed the last union-closure-member-field xfail (#861). Remaining residual is coverage-only (union-with-map/array member, map reader path, niche nullable-scalar lists) — see `docs/internals/rep-fuzz-findings.md` + `ROADMAP.md`.
- **Union with an array member — real rep (#863)** — a union whose arm is an array (`S[] | {w:i32}`, `(() => f64)[] | i64`) now lowers end-to-end instead of rejecting: param acceptance for a ref-element array arm (`isVariantBoxUnion`), a deterministic additive tag band above the fixed value-atom kinds (`refArrSlotTag = uVariants.length + 12 + rlSlotByName(elem)` — zero blast radius on existing tags, fixpoint-stable), boxing the reflist wrapper into the union anyref (`emitUnionCoerce`), `is <ref-array>` tag compare, and a narrowed reflist read (`ref.cast` the payload to the wrapper). Struct-array / closure-array / scalar-array arms across param/local/return/global, read + construct. (One neighbour — an array whose ELEMENT is a paren union, `(C | D)[]` — stays a loud reject: `splitUnionAtoms` lacks paren-depth tracking; never unsound.)
- **Union with a map member — real rep (#865)** — a union whose arm is a map (`{[string]: string} | f64`, `{[string]: K} | i64`) now lowers instead of rejecting, mirroring the array-member feature (#863): `isVariantBoxUnion` accepts a map arm, an interleaved additive tag band (`mapSlotTag = uVariants.length + 15 + 2*slot` on ODD offsets, ref-arrays moved to EVEN `12 + 2*slot` so a `S[] | {[string]:i32}` union can't collide), `emitUnionCoerce` boxes the map struct ref into the union anyref, `emitIs` compares the map tag, and a narrowed read `ref.cast`s the payload to the map heap type (so `t["k"]` / `t["k"] ?? d` work); the checker's `floorMapUnion` guard is removed. Scoped to scalar/string/mono map VALUES: a ref-value map arm (struct/nested-map/union/closure value) would be a #860-style heap-type-identity hazard (silent invalid-wasm), so it stays a **loud registration reject** (pinned `error-map-member-refvalue.vl`), deferred to a follow-up.
- **Map-member union in a LOCAL binding + nullable-atom map values (map-union composition)** — two root fixes in the union-with-map / composite-map-value family the rep fuzzer flagged. (1) A local `const v: {[string]: i32} | boolean = h` (a map arm boxed into a union whose OTHER arm is a scalar/boolean — not the struct/map cases #865/#868 covered) emitted invalid wasm: the local-slot classifier (`letIsMap`) excluded the map-member-union ANNOTATION but fell through to `exprMap(init)` — and the init IS the bare map arm — so the cell was typed as the map struct while the RHS boxed into the union box (`struct.new $box` stored into a `(ref $map)` local). `letIsMap` now returns false for any registered `isUName` annotation (map-FIRST `{[..]}|X` and map-LAST `X|{[..]}`), so the cell rides its union box and the map arm narrows through the union. Graduates the 18 p0 (local) construct+read shapes — scalar/boolean/struct/nested-map value map-unions. (2) A map whose VALUE is a nullable-ATOM niche (`boolean | null` — 0/1 with the spare `2` = null) was mis-classified as a ref-VALUE union map (`mvValKindOfName` counted `boolean`+`null` > 1 and BOXED the values into a `(ref $box)` vals cell); it now reps as the MONO i32 map. `K0 | null` (a nullable LITUNION whose atom values are StrLit-syntax) rides the mono map too but hits the atom-map store guard and is now a clean LOUD REJECT (INVALID-WASM → REJECT) rather than plumbing nullable-atom-map store/read across every site. (`tests/cases/unions/map-member-local-narrow.vl`, `tests/cases/maps/map-nullable-atom-value.vl`)
- **Fresh-seed unsound triage (audit Phase 0.4) — compiler crash + 5 map-composition miscompiles fixed or loud-rejected** — every non-REJECT finding at the audit's three fresh fuzz seeds (55501/90210/314159) closed at the root: a union whose struct arm carries a `(...)`-grouped union-element list field (`{…, f: (boolean | string | null)[], …} | f64`) CRASHED the compiler (paren-blind arm interning left the field's ref-list slot unminted; `pushFieldStorage` indexed `rlWrapIdx` out of bounds) — arms now intern via an all-grouper-depth, arrow-aware split and a missing slot fails loudly; a rebind under a `!= null` narrow of a map-member union (`{[string]: V} | string | null`) mis-classified as a bare MONO map (`narrowedMapOf` gained the `nameIsMapMemberUnion` guard every sibling site carries); a map-FIELD read through a union's ref-array arm (`t[i].f[k] ?? d` after `is S[]`) never reserved the map scratch frame (`unionListElemMapFieldMember` pre-pass); a TYPED map value with no interned slot silently fell back to the mono map (`mvSlotOfMapValNameOrMono` now -3, atom-valued closure-call maps gated via the checker's litunion record); and two unrepresentable map VALUES became loud rejects — a union with a MAP member (`{[string]: {[string]: i32} | f64}`, unboxable at the store seam) and the `string | null` niche (`{[string]: string | null}`, whose box is never minted). Graduates `p2r {[string]: () => i32} | {w: i32} | null` from the baseline. (`tests/cases/unions/struct-arm-grouped-union-list-field.vl`, `map-member-null-narrow-rebind.vl`, `struct-list-arm-map-field-read.vl`, `map-member-closure-value-null-narrow.vl`, `tests/cases/maps/error-union-map-member-value.vl`, `error-nulstr-value.vl`)
- **Ref-list slot layer joins canonical structural dedup (repOf slot layer, ref-list table)** — the `repCanonKey`-keyed struct-twin dedup extends through the ref-list wrapper/backing slots and the inline-shape spelling bridge: a FIELD shape interned before its declared twin no longer mints a duplicate heap type (an `A` into a `{inner:{v:i32}}` field / an `A[]` into a `{items:{v:i32}[]}` field were INVALID WASM), and an inline-shape ref-list param (`sumA(bs: {v:i32}[])` given an `A[]`, was REJECT) resolves via the layout-guarded structural bridge — its slot twins with the declared one (one wrapper, one backing); `rlSlotByName` gains a nominal-then-canonical fallback (`repStructSlotsTwin`), and `structIndexOfTypeName` is tightened with the field-TYPE layout guard. - **Variant slot layer joins canonical structural dedup (repOf slot layer COMPLETE)** — layout-twin union variants share one variant-struct heap type (`buildVariantTwins` → `uVarTwin`/`uVarHeap`: canonical variant key + per-field storage guard, keys computed once per slot; the arithmetic `uVarIdx + vi` heap identity — one type per PUSH of a variant into any union — is retired and `uVarIdx` deleted). The SAME variant declared in two unions no longer emits twice, and a `Cat` boxed into `Kot | Bird` (structural twin arm) no longer TRAPS at the narrowed read — the field-name tag (`variantSig`) already matched, so the trap was one cast away from silent wrongness; with one shared heap type the tag compare and the payload cast agree. Completes the repOf slot layer: all four name-keyed tables (STRUCT, REF-LIST, MAP-VALUE, VARIANT) now dedup by canonical layout identity. (`tests/cases/unions/variant-twin-heap.vl`)
- **repOf hot path memoized (roadmap repOf item (c)) — self-compile ~26% faster, byte-identical** — `repCanonKey` gains a generation-stamped per-arena-index memo (consulted/written at TOP-LEVEL calls only: an interior de Bruijn back-edge fragment is context-dependent, so only a root's key is reusable verbatim), and `repSlotOfTy`'s per-query linear rescan of `sNames` (re-rendering every declared struct's key — 41.8% of a profiled self-compile) collapses into a stamped cache (nominal `di→slot` array + canonical-key→unique-twin maps; exact-match-wins order preserved). The stamps are two new checker generations: `tyMutEpoch` advances at EVERY in-place `Ty`-arena mutation (empty-collection pins, return-inference patches, 0a-placeholder fills, generic-alias instantiation fills, hole-shape field pushes) and `cUserTypesVer` at every `cUserTypes` write, so a mid-emit re-check can never serve a stale key. `removeAtomFrom` (25% of the same profile) becomes a pure-function memo (the dominant `removed == "null"` case keys on the set alone) over a slice-run rebuild (kept atoms are verbatim contiguous slices of the set, so the complement is ≤2 slices in the common case instead of two concats per atom — byte-identical by the `splitUnionAtoms` tiling invariant). Receipts: `repSlotOfTy` subtree 41.8% → 0.0%, `removeAtomFrom` 24.5% → 7.1% of guest samples (total −43%); `refresh-compiler.sh` 19.9s → 14.6s; `rep-fuzz-check.sh` 105.7s → 54.0s (identical failure set). Native fixpoint holds and the memoized compiler reproduces master's fixpoint artifact byte-for-byte from master's source. Also chartered: the fused `m[k] = (m[k] ?? 0) + 1` missing-key map-RMW miscompile the cache build tripped (ROADMAP B-bug-maprmw; comment-marked workaround at the `repSlotKeyN` build).
- **B-bug-maprmw — map SET evaluates receiver, key, and VALUE before the probe; fixes the fused missing-key RMW + the shared-scratch clobber family** — `m[k] = (m[k] ?? 0) + 1` on a MISSING key trapped (OOB array access — the append arm linked `index[slot]` and pushed the key BEFORE evaluating the RHS, so the RHS's probe of the same key hit the half-inserted entry and read `vals.backing[count]`) or, once the backing had grown, silently stored `0 + 1` and skipped the `??` default. Same root for every value shape (boolean/i64/f64/string/struct-field receiver). The same lowering also parked the receiver/key in the SHARED per-shape scratch locals across user code, so a same-shaped map op nested in the KEY or VALUE expr clobbered them: `b[a["x"] ?? "d"]` probed `a` (reads returned the default; a SET's write was silently lost), and `m["a"] = (n["x"] ?? 0) + 1` on a missing key appended into `n`. Fix: `emitMapRecvKey` leaves receiver + key on the OPERAND STACK (immune to nested ops) and `emitMapSetV` evaluates the value ONCE — before the probe touches anything — into a reserved stash (the mv slot's typed `valStash`; a new mono frame slot 14), which both arms consume; a value-expr CALL that mutates the map is now correctly ordered before the write too. #917's split-form workaround at the `repSlotKeyN` build stays ONE seed generation — the published seed's lowering predates this fix, so a fused spelling in compiler source traps when that seed code-gens it (the bootstrap ordering constraint); fuse it once the seed containing this fix publishes. (`tests/cases/maps/rmw-fused-missing-key.vl`, `rmw-fused-value-shapes.vl`, `rmw-cross-map-clobber.vl`)
- **Rep-rewrite Stage A — the RECURSIVE `Rep` tree + total `repTreeOfTy` + the differential shadow harness (audit Part III Phase 2 items 3–4, foundation; zero byte drift)** — `emit_rep.vl` grows the compositional successor of the flat `RepDesc`: an index-linked, hash-consed rep-tree arena (`Scalar|Bool|Str|Atom|Struct|List|Map|Box|Closure|Nullable(disc)|Unsupported(reason)`) built TOTALLY over the post-mono `Ty` arena by ONE constructor — every type gets a full tree or an explicit reason-coded policy node, cycle-safe via a build-before-recurse `Ty`-memo, generation-stamped on #917's epochs; plus a debug-only differential harness (`$VL_REP_SHADOW` → `setRepShadow`, the `setEmitNames` pattern) sweeping the final arena and asserting tree-vs-flat agreement on every `rdCovered` fact (top kind, null discipline, list-element vocabulary, `$fnsig` token, slot identity up to `repStructSlotsTwin`), with a coverage report (real-tree % + `unsup` buckets — Stage B's burn-down list). Sweeps: corpus (731) + self-compile + 16 pinned fuzz seeds + a branching/declared/multiobs survey — ZERO disagreements after three tree fixes the harness itself forced (`bool` leaf kept distinct from i32, variant-ness stripped at the single-member-union seam, litunion alias-copy discipline), and three latent FLAT-path irregularities reported for Stage B (single-member-union members classify `variant` at the TyObj arm vs `struct` at the union arm; the nullable-list arm covers ANY litunion element while the bare-array arm alias-gates the same element; litunion alias copies are index-invisible).
