- **B21 `match` (phase 1: litunion match) shipped** — exhaustive-by-default `match` over literal-union scrutinees: OR-patterns, `_` wildcard, redundant/invalid-pattern errors, cross-module rename support (`tests/cases/match/*`); payload-binding match over tagged unions is unshipped and stays on the roadmap.
- **B21 `match` (phase 2a: VALUE-union scrutinees) shipped** — `match` now dispatches over **every** union, not only literal ones: struct unions (`C | D`), scalar unions (`i32 | string`), mixed (`Box | i32 | string`), and both `| null` spellings (declared `TyUnion`, inline `TyNullable`). An arm's pattern is a TYPE (`C =>`, `i32 =>`, `{c: i32} =>`, `null =>`, or the OR-form `A | B =>`) and the parser mints it as a real `IsExpr` over the scrutinee, so the arm rides the EXISTING `x is T` machinery end to end — `collectThenNarrows`/`collectElseNarrows` narrowing, the `isVarTyIxOf`/`narrowTys` emit ABI, the module-merge rename, the lint type-name scan — and the desugar reuses the pattern node as the arm's condition. Every arm binds the narrowed member, the last one included: it lowers to the chain's bare `else`, whose union COMPLEMENT is that member. **Exhaustiveness is the point**: a missing member is a compile error naming it (`non-exhaustive match — missing {c: i32}`), where the `is`-chain this replaces has none. Still refused, each with its own reason instead of the old blanket "must be a literal union": a non-union scrutinee, a union with LITERAL members (an arm's `is 0` does not lower), and a pattern that resolves to a union (one `is` cannot test it). Also fixes a **compiler TRAP on master**: a zero-arm `match k {}` read `bodies[-1]` for the chain's bare `else` and died as a bare `wasm trap: out of bounds array access` with no diagnostic; it now reports its missing members. Corpus byte-, message- and run-identical (1,288 pre-existing files); fuzz A/B identical over 25,200 programs/side. (`tests/cases/match/value-union-*.vl`, `scrutinee-reject-messages.vl`, `zero-arm-error.vl`, `tests/cases/modules/match-type-pattern-cross-module/`)
- **B21 `match` (phase 2b: PAYLOAD BINDING) shipped** — a variant pattern may carry a punned field list, and the arm narrows AND binds in one form: `match cmd { Move{x, y} => f(x, y), Attack{target} => g(target) }` — the command-dispatch shape webcraft's order pipeline wants. Punning only (`{x, y}`); renaming (`{x: a}`) and nested destructuring stay deferred, with the one-branch cost of each recorded in `docs/internals/match-design.md`. **The lowering is the recorded one and nothing more**: the arm is already `if scrut is Move { <block> }`, so the desugar PREPENDS `const x = scrut.x` statements to that block — no new chain, no new narrowing, no new emitter path, and the exhaustive-last-arm bare `else` unchanged. Measured, not asserted: 18 grid cells (payload types i32/f64/string/struct/list/nullable x union shapes 2/3/5/aliased x punned/subset/empty/no-payload-arm/`_`-default x statement/expression) each compile BYTE-IDENTICAL to their hand-written if-chain twin, with two inverted controls reading DIFFER. The clause lives on a new `matchBinds` column PARALLEL TO `matchPats` (a `Block` of `LetDecl`s per pattern, or -1) rather than in the arm body, so `nodeTyIx` still covers every minted node (it is sized at `checkProgram` entry) and `vl fmt` still prints the arm the user wrote. Three walks had to be taught it: the FORMATTER renders the clause structurally (the pattern's source span stops at its type atom, so the verbatim slice phase 2a round-trips with would have silently DELETED every binding from a formatted file), the module MERGE shadows the bound names over the arm body (a module-level `const x` otherwise captured an arm binding `x`), and lint needs nothing because the splice has already run by lint time. Four rejects, each ONE error: a clause on an OR arm (forced — a multi-pattern arm gets no then-narrowing, so the field read cannot type), a duplicate binding, a body declaration that shadows a binding (both exist because the desugar SPLICES: post-splice the two share a scope the checker saw as two), and an unknown field. **Exhaustiveness is untouched**: coverage is decided from `matchPats` alone, so the same match with and without bindings produces the identical phase-1 `non-exhaustive match — missing …` error — pinned as one fixture and proved by sabotaging the coverage rule (both the new and phase 1's fixtures go green-when-they-should-be-red). Corpus six-channel A/B over 1,673 files: every pre-existing file identical on all six channels including BYTES; fuzz A/B identical over 14,400 programs/side. (`tests/cases/match/payload-binding-*.vl`, `tests/cases/modules/match-payload-shadows-global/`, `tests/vl_fmt_test.ts`)
- **B21 `match` — a binding arm can be a VALUE: the if-expression arm gained a PRELUDE (C6)** — `const r = match u { A{a} => a, B{b} => b }` reported `emitProgram: if-expression arm is not a single value`. The grid that localises it (binding/non-binding × statement/tail/value position, for `match` and for the hand-written `if` twin) reads 8 of 10 cells lowering on master, with both failures at binding × VALUE position — so the BINDING broke value position, not `match`-in-value-position, and not phase 2b: the desugar's output IS the `if` twin, and the twin failed identically. **An arm's value is now its LAST statement** (the rule `blockTailIsValue` already applies in tail position and `emitStmts` in statement position), and everything before it is the arm's PRELUDE — exactly what a payload clause produces. `emitIfArmOpen`/`emitIfArmClose` lower the prelude in the arm's own lexical frame; the five arm emitters (numeric join, ref join, union box, concrete variant, return sink) and the two binding-init sinks (nullable local, union-box pair) each still lower the VALUE in their own rep, so `match` and `if` alike now work in binding-init and `return` position across i32/f64/boolean/string/struct/list/nullable/`string | null`/value-union joins and `else if` chains. **The constraint is the local-slot PRE-ORDER**: wasm locals are function-scoped and `emitLetDeclStmt` claims them off a linear cursor, so a prelude may only be lowered where the collect pass allocated its locals in the same order — `collectIfExprLocals` walks the two statement positions whose order the emitter replays (a binding INITIALIZER, a `return` operand), and `armPreludeBlocks` records the arms it walked. `emitIfArmOpen` requires that membership, so the two unwalked positions — an if-expression buried deeper in an expression (`print(match u { A{a} => a … })`) and a TOP-LEVEL binding (a module global, whose initializer the start function's local collection never descends into) — are LOUD rejects naming the supported spelling. Both were compiler TRAPS (`out of bounds array access`) the moment the arm emitters accepted a multi-statement arm, so the mark is what converts a silent-or-crashing slot misalignment into a diagnostic. `armPreludeBlocks` holds arena NODE indices and so resets in `emitProgram`'s sidecar block with the other index columns — a stale index naming a node in the next program grants permission collect never gave, reachable only when one instance lowers several programs, which is why the corpus driver caught it and the CLI and the fixpoint ladder did not. Native fixpoint byte-identical; both seed-ladder legs green. - **The expression-statement DISCARD applies by node class, and the void-if-arm reject names its actual cause** — `emitStmt` implemented VL's "a bare value expression in statement position is evaluated and its value dropped" rule for a hand-listed few classes: a non-`=` `BinExpr` and a non-void `Call`. Every other value-shaped node reached `emitProgram: unsupported statement in body` with `vl check` rc 0. One cell per node class read **6 of 21** honouring the rule — `42`, `"s"`, `x`, `q.length`, `q[0]`, `-q`, `!q`, `{a: 1}`, `[1, 2]`, `(1 + 2)`, `q is i32`, `q as f64` all rejected. The rule was never in question: `tests/cases/statements/discarded-call-return.vl` pins it for a call, and `emitStmt`'s own `BinExpr` arm spells out evaluate-then-`drop`; only its coverage was. The discard now routes through **`stmtIsTailValue`** — the one classifier that already answers "this statement IS a value" — so it applies by MEMBERSHIP rather than by spelling, and a prefix `-q`/`!q` joins it (retiring `emitProgram: unsupported unary statement`). **This is also what a value-producing `if`/`match` in statement position needed**: such an `if` lowers as a VOID `if` whose arm blocks each end in a value, so the failure was INSIDE the arm on the arm's own last statement — which is why a hand-written `==` ladder reproduced it identically and why `match` needed nothing of its own (`desugarMatchAt` lowers it to the same chain before emit sees it). Measured on a 300-cell grid (node class × construct × position × arm types × value type × flag polarity): statement-position value-producing branches **5 → 51 of 51**, bare expression statements **6 → 22 of 23**, with **0 regressions** and **both silent classes 0 of 300 before and after** — the 84 cells where a VOID arm is the TAKEN one in a value-demanding position are loud in every case (57 emit-reject, 17 check-reject, 8 runtime trap on the emitter's `unreachable` poison, 2 invalid wasm), so nothing fabricates a value. The one class that still rejects is a bare `null` statement, correctly: it has no rep without a typed slot, and it says so. Separately, `emitProgram: if-expression arm is not a single value` **misnamed its own cause** — the common case is an arm ending in a VOID call, which IS a single expression and simply yields nothing. `ifArmNoValueFail` now distinguishes empty arm / void call / statement across all five arm emitters (plain, union, variant). **The layer that owns a void arm is the CHECKER**: VL types the arms and joins them, void included, and rejects `void` in a value slot on every ANNOTATED path (`return type mismatch: expected i32, got i32 | void`, `cannot bind the void result`, `argument 1: expected i32, got void`, `push: cannot add void`, `operator '+' is not defined for void and i32`). It applies that rule on annotated paths ONLY, so the emit reject is a BACKSTOP for an inference-path hole, pinned as two files that are one shape differing only by the annotation. That hole is `if`-independent and independently reachable — `function sv() { print(9) } print(sv())` is `vl check` rc 0 and invalid wasm — measured at **4 of 16** value-demanding positions uncovered (`print(<void>)`, `[<void>]`, an un-annotated `return <void>`, and a call to a void-tailed function). (`tests/cases/statements/discarded-if-expression-value.vl`, `discarded-expression-statement-classes.vl`, `error-if-arm-ends-in-void-call.vl`, `error-if-arm-ends-in-statement.vl`, `error-if-arm-is-empty.vl`, `error-void-if-arm-annotated-return.vl`, `error-discarded-bare-null.vl`)

Bare `__trap__()` is byte-identical to before; no new intrinsic name and no keyword (intrinsics stay dunder-only). The checker rejects a non-string arg or >1 arg (`__trap__ takes an optional string message`). `std:test` still uses the bare form (threading messages through it is a follow-up). - **Numeric-opcode intrinsics — the 44 operations that ARE one wasm instruction (webcraft P0.3+P0.4)** — the four IEEE bitcasts `f32bits`/`f32fromBits`/`f64bits`/`f64fromBits` (`*.reinterpret_*`, previously absent entirely, so a float's bits were unreachable — `as` converts), the f32/f64 `sqrt abs floor ceil trunc nearest min max copysign`, and the i32/i64 `clz ctz popcnt rotl rotr divU remU ltU leU gtU geU`. Free functions with the width taken from the operands under the binary operators' own rule (a bare float literal adapts down, a genuine f64 widens), so an intrinsic and an operator over the same operands compute at the same width; `clz` at i64 yields an i64 because `i64.clz` does. **Shadowable**: the checker's arm is skipped when the name is a declared function or an in-scope binding and the emitter's is reached only where the direct-call and closure-value lookups both failed, so a program's own `min`/`max` still wins. No import, no runtime, nothing for the linker — the host ABI is unchanged. Transcendentals are a deliberate non-ask (no opcode computes one; a std `sin` would be a determinism trap). Also fixes a latent import-scan hole this exposed: `scanPrintUse` now reads an intrinsic call's own recorded type, since an intrinsic RESULT scalar appears nowhere as an annotation (`print(f32fromBits(k))` alone emitted a call to a `__print_f32__` that was never imported). Corpus byte-, message- and run-identical over 1,342 pre-existing files; fuzz A/B identical over 25,200 programs/side; every opcode verified by `wasm-tools print`. (`docs/internals/numeric-intrinsics.md`, `tests/cases/numerics/bitcast-*.vl`, `float-opcodes-*.vl`, `int-*.vl`)
- **The linear-memory load matrix, `memory.grow`/`memory.size`, and the EXPORTED memory (webcraft P0.2 + the load half of P0.1)** — the seven missing load widths `__load_i8__`/`__load_u8__`/`__load_i16__`/`__load_u16__`/`__load_i64__`/`__load_f32__`/`__load_f64__` (`i32.load8_s`/`i32.load8_u`/`i32.load16_s`/`i32.load16_u`/`i64.load`/`f32.load`/`f64.load`, each one instruction at its natural alignment), plus `__memory_size__` and `__memory_grow__` (`memory.size`/`memory.grow`) — which were DECLARED and lowered by nothing, so a program could not address past the one hardcoded 64 KiB page and two 32 KiB buffers already trapped. `memory.grow` returns the PREVIOUS page count, or `-1` on failure, passed through unchanged. The narrow loads differ only in extension (`__load_i8__` of `0xFF` is `-1`; `__load_u8__` is `255`), the alignment immediate is a hint so every width reads correctly at an odd address, and a fresh page — including a newly grown one — is zero. **The module's linear memory is now exported as `memory`**, automatically, gated on the same `memUsed` flag as the memory section: a program that never touches linear memory is BYTE-IDENTICAL to before, while a memory-only module now emits an export section it previously skipped entirely. A host overlays `Float32Array`/`DataView` on `instance.exports.memory.buffer` and reads guest bytes in place — proved from the JS host and from a wasmtime 47 embedding, neither of which needed any change. A user `export function memory` in a memory-using program is a loud reject (export names must be unique); the same name without linear memory still compiles. **`memory.grow` DETACHES every host view** (`byteLength` 0, indexed read `undefined`, no throw), so the JS host's dead `imports.memory` and the two sinks that read it are deleted — censused dead across all 1,149 corpus modules that build — and the re-read-after-grow contract is asserted by test rather than described. NO `Buffer` type: O1/O5/O6 are unruled and the name is hard to change once shipped. Known limitation, censused across all ten memory intrinsics in four call positions: they work at top level and in a plain named function, and fail with `captured variable not found in enclosing frame` inside a lambda or in a named function in a module using a function value — so a `Buffer` METHOD surface is blocked until `isBuiltinFnName` is fixed. Also: `--enable-bulk-memory` added to `wasm-opt`/`wasm-dis` ahead of any `memory.copy`/`memory.fill` emission (binaryen 130 exits rc=1 with NO output without it); and the JS host no longer reports a linear-memory fault as "array index out of bounds". Every opcode verified by disassembly; suite 2,122/0/8. (`docs/internals/buffer-design.md` §H, `tests/cases/memory/`, `tests/vl_exported_memory_test.ts`)

- **A COMPILER CRASH NO LONGER WEARS THE PROGRAM'S ERROR — a banner and exit 70 (D1500).** The seed's own `wasm trap: out of bounds array access` over anonymous frames is byte-for-byte what a program indexing past the end of its own array gets, so the first external VL consumer read D1500 as their bug and spent a session inside their DEFLATE decoder. The host always knew which of the two modules trapped — one it loaded as the seed, one it instantiated from the compile result — and never said. It says now: two stderr lines naming the file, the vl version and the seed's byte count, ahead of the unchanged backtrace, plus **exit 70** (sysexits' `EX_SOFTWARE`), distinct from 1 (the program or its compilation failed), 2 (usage) and `fmt`'s 3. **Attribution is recorded at the CALL BOUNDARY, where the instance is known, never inferred from the message text** — `from_compiler` / `from_user` tag the failing wasm call, and both arms write, so a swallowed failure (`vl test` discards one per trapping test) cannot leave a stale attribution behind. A trap in the cause chain is required on top of the flag, so a link or I/O failure that never entered the compiler cannot be blamed on it. Every other output byte is unchanged: a program's own trap, a parse diagnostic and a trapping `vl test` case all keep today's stderr and exit code exactly, and the suite pins BOTH directions — a host that bannered every trap is the same defect with the blame reversed. The fixtures are tiny VL programs compiled by the real seed and handed back as `--compiler` (one trapping inside `compileSrc`, the D1500 rung; one in its own start function, the rung the command pump reaches), so the pin does not evaporate when the D1500 compiler bug is fixed. (`scripts/vl-host/src/main.rs`, `tests/vl_compiler_trap_banner_test.ts`, `docs/internals/cli-design.md`)
- **`check --fix` VERIFIES every edit before it ships, and the `redundant type annotation` hint stops comparing an annotation against a type the annotation produced (D1091, D1441, D1442).** Over a copy of `tests/cases` (2,804 files) the autofix rewrote **1,198 files and moved 159 of them `runs -> not-runs`** — 13.3% of everything it touched, and it shipped every one. The driver now COMPILES each candidate rewrite (emit + the engine's own validation, not just `check`) before it reaches the disk and drops an edit that stops a file building; generic, at the `--fix` driver, so it protects every autofix. `check` alone would wave through **87 of the 159**, because the annotation is load-bearing for the EMITTER far more often than for the checker. The ladder is all-edits-at-once (one compile, and it holds on 1,109 files), then — only on a failure — the ORIGINAL (a file that did not build before cannot have been broken by an edit), then greedy from the empty known-good set. **159 -> 2**, and both survivors are a module that VALIDATES and traps at RUN time, which nothing short of running the program can see. Cost: one extra compile per file with edits, `2.9s -> 49s` over the corpus. Two of the three mechanisms under it are closed rather than netted: the hint's comparison was CIRCULAR (`seedExpected` runs before `checkNode`, so `initTy` was computed WITH the annotation — the compiler's own comment claimed it was "the initializer's CONTEXT-FREE type"), gated now on a counter of contextual seeds a lambda actually consumed; and the return-annotation SPAN scanned forward for a depth-0 colon, which a type-parameter bound's colon is, so `--fix` wrote `function describe<T {`. Sites the fix must refuse: **269 -> 126**, and each is now REPORTED at its own line as an `info` rather than counted — 65 loud emit refusal, 34 check-clean invalid wasm, 6 checker cascade, 2 genuinely underdetermined. (203 stale `@hint` directives over 109 fixtures go with it; `cases_wasm_test.ts` adjudicates hints strictly both ways, so their absence is the pin.)
- **Colored `print` — serde-design Stage C0, host-side, and ANSI provably never leaks.** A program's own `print` of a rendered VALUE (i32/i64/f32/f64/boolean) is wrapped in ANSI when stdout is a terminal; a bare **string** is never colored. That is Node's split, and the palette is Node's too, **measured rather than chosen**: `util.inspect.styles` on node v24.11.1 gives `number`/`bigint`/`boolean` = `yellow` with `util.inspect.colors.yellow = [33, 39]` — the open/close PAIR, so a reset never cancels a bold the surrounding shell set — and on a pty `console.log(5)` emits `ESC[33m5ESC[39m` while `console.log("s")` emits `s`. **One correction to the ruling's own text**: Node renders `null` in **bold** (`[1,22]`) and `undefined` in grey, not dim/grey for null; nothing is colored for it yet because VL's import family has no null sink, and the measurement is recorded for C2. The escape is applied by the print IMPORT — the last point before stdout that still knows a value's type, and the only place a program's output can acquire one — so `toString`/template/serde output stays pure by construction rather than by a downstream strip. **Detection is REUSED, not rebuilt**: `color_ok` from the #2080 CLI overhaul (isatty AND `NO_COLOR` unset AND `TERM != dumb`), now behind a `ColorChoice` that folds in `--color=always|never|auto`. Probe table, every policy row: pipe **0** escapes (`xxd | grep -c 1b` = 0, and with `TERM=xterm-256color` set); pty **8** (4 values × 2); pty+`NO_COLOR=1` **0**; pty+`TERM=dumb` **0**; pipe+`--color=always` **8**; pty+`--color=never` **0**; `NO_COLOR=1` + `--color=always` **8** (an explicit flag overrides the variable, per the NO_COLOR spec's own carve-out); `print("42")` under `--color=always` **0**; `"n = " + toString(n)` under `--color=always` **0**; `--batch` `.out` **0**; `vl test`'s relayed program output **0** while its own report stays colored. Two fixes fell out. **`--color` is now an override on every subcommand**: the host appends its resolved answer AFTER user argv and the VL parser takes the last one it sees, so `vl check --color=always | less -R` resolved to `never` — accepted and then overruled; `cli_pump` folds the two before sending, and an unrecognized value is exit 2 rather than a silent "never". And **`vl test` relays a failing test's captured output plain**: that text is pushed character by character into a VL string for the reporter, so an escape in it would be an escape inside a VL string value — which the ruling forbids outright — as well as a double-wrap. The two TS print-sink twins are a documented deferral (neither has a stdout to test: `runWasm.ts` pushes into an array a test compares, `playground/runtime.ts` into the DOM, where an escape is literal garbage). (`docs/serde-design.md`, `scripts/vl-host/src/main.rs`, `tests/vl_print_color_test.ts`)

- **C3b `vl build -O3` — the RELEASE PROFILE (webcraft P1.3)** — runs `wasm-opt --closed-world -O3 --gufa -O3` plus the shared GC/reference-type/bulk-memory enables. `-O` is unchanged (one open-world `-O`), `-O3` wins when both are passed, and a missing `wasm-opt` stays a soft no-op — a note naming the flag, the unoptimized module on disk, exit 0 — exactly as `-O` already behaved. The box melts by closed-world type refinement + DCE. (2) *`--gufa` is measurably inert on VL output* — zero allocations and zero `ref.cast`s removed across all fixtures and on the 1.1 MB `vl-compiler.wasm` (4,503 casts either way); it is shipped because P1.3 names it, and the trailing second `-O3` is the member that earns its place (the only one moving the grown-list row 4→2). **What does NOT melt, pinned as a fixture at 4/4/4**: a union box whose narrowed value is READ. - **`vl check --codegen` now VALIDATES the module it emits — the check-clean-invalid-wasm class becomes loud at the gate that promises the program lowers** — `compileSrc()` returning 0 means "the emitter ran to completion", which is strictly weaker than "these bytes are a module", and the gap between the two claims is the class this codebase treats as its most serious: `vl check` and `vl check --codegen` both rc 0 over a program the engine will not load. `build` had closed it for its own artifact (`validate_written_module`) and `run` gets it free (`Module::new` validates before it translates); `check` could not, because its bytes never left the guest — the wasm validator lives in the engine and a VL program has none. **The bytes cross now, on the channel that already existed**: a new `CMD_VALIDATE` (10) hands the module off the driver's `rbyte*` readback buffer, exactly where `CMD_TEST_STASH` reads it, and the verdict returns through `cliValidateCommit(ok)` with the engine's own message on `cliResult*`. No new mechanism, no new export shape, ~40 lines of host and ~40 of `cli.vl`. The diagnostic is a **positionless `error` with the stable code `invalid-module`** — the validator names a wasm offset and no map from one back to a VL span exists — worded so the reader is not sent hunting in their own program (`the emitted module is not valid wasm (a compiler emit bug, not an error in this file): …`). `--no-validate` opts out, mirroring `vl build --no-validate`. **THE OVER-REJECTION QUESTION WAS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED, AND THE ANSWER IS EXACT**: swept over `tests/cases` (2,075 files) the gate flags **11**, and all 11 are precisely the files the corpus already marks `@no-instantiate` — no false positive, nothing missed. That set equality is now a TEST rather than a measurement (`tests/vl_check_codegen_test.ts`), verified red on both arms by sabotage: adding the directive to a clean file reports *marked but not flagged*, deleting it from a broken one reports *flagged but not marked*. So a defect that gets FIXED reddens the suite until its directive is deleted, and a newly-introduced shape reddens it immediately. Three open issues (#1792 union-of-litunions in return position, #1684 generic-application vs declared-struct layout twin, #1678 declared-union arm bound from a call) go from clean-at-the-gate to a loud error with this change and NO fix to their roots — that is the point of it. The three stale claims this retires are corrected where they were written (`tests/cases/soundness/README.vl`, `cases_wasm_test.ts`, `selfhost_native_align_test.ts` all said `vl check`, even `--codegen`, cannot see this class). The align suite's ACCEPT tier is unaffected because it checks WITHOUT `--codegen`; `mono-tyaram-grid.sh` buckets off `vl run`, so no cell moves and only its `check=` column reads 1 on a BAD cell. The host probes `cliValidateCommit` lazily, inside the arm, so a seed predating the command still runs. - **C5 Distribution via `deno compile`** — native `vl` binary (binaryen embedded); `deno task compile`/`smoke`; 11 smoke checks pass. → `DECISIONS.md`
- **C-redundant-type — lint + `--fix` for redundant explicit annotations (lean on inference).** VL's design hides types and surfaces them only where required, but hand-written annotations accrete; this is the first rule of a cleanup family. `vl check` now emits a `hint` for a `let`/`const` whose explicit annotation is EXACTLY what the initializer infers on its own (`let x: i32 = 5`, `const c: string = "hi"`), and `--fix` rewrites `let x: T = e` → `let x = e`. **Provably conservative — no functional change, never a false positive.** The check lives in the type checker (`compiler/typecheck.vl`, the `LetDecl` arm): the initializer is typed by `checkNode` BEFORE the annotation is consulted, so its context-free type is in hand; a finding is recorded only when that type RENDERS identically to the annotation. Widening / hole cases are excluded for free — `let x: i64 = 5` (the literal defaults to i32, the annotation widens), `: f64 = 5`, `: i32[] = []` and `: i32 | null = null` (the hole-bearing init type never renders equal to the concrete annotation), so the annotation is load-bearing and kept. The fix span runs from just after the name to the assignment `=` (found by a depth-aware token scan, so a multi-token or function-type `=>` annotation is handled), and the initializer — even `1 + 2` / `[1, 2, 3]` — is preserved byte-for-byte. cli.vl reads the finding stream (joined module, no marshalling) for both the report and `cliApplyFixes`. Gated to SINGLE-MODULE checks for now (a graph compile merges modules, so a dependency's findings would mis-attribute against the entry — per-module attribution à la inlay hints' `symOccModuleAt` is the follow-up, with the return-type and parameter rules). Validated: native fixpoint holds; corpus 468/0, LSP 36/0, native suite 513/0 (the finding stream is cli-only, never in the adjudicated diagnostic count); **0 false positives across 472 single-file corpus/std files** (already inference-first). (`tests/vl_check_redundant_type_test.ts`)
- **C-redundant-type: module-aware `--fix` + applied to the compiler (−150 annotations).** Drops the single-module gate. Two changes make the rule safe and reportable across a module graph: (1) **per-module attribution** — each finding records its name token; the driver's `redunModuleAt = modOfTok(redunTokAt(i))` (mirroring `inlayModuleAt`) resolves the owning module, and the cli keeps only the ENTRY's (module 0), de-mangling the merge's `$mN` suffix for the message + anchoring the fix span at the `:` token (robust to a mangled binding name). (2) **module-aware `--fix`** — the fix moves from a pre-fetch, entry-ALONE check (which gave unreliable types under unresolved imports — it once mangled `let x: i32[] = []` into `let x: []`) to AFTER the resolved module compile in `cliCheckCurFile`: the now-trustworthy redundant-annotation + lint streams drive the edits, the file is written, and a module-aware re-check produces the report (`cliComputeFixes` no longer re-checks; error diags are captured BEFORE the lint re-parse so module-compile errors aren't dropped). So an import-DEPENDENT redundancy (`let e: i32 = importedFn()`) is now removed too, while empty-collection holes stay correctly excluded. **Dogfooded:** `vl check --fix compiler/ std/` removed **150 redundant local-variable annotations** across 5 files, and the seed rebuilt from the cleaned source is **byte-identical** to before — proving every removal was semantics-neutral (the strongest possible check). Validated: native fixpoint holds; lint-self + fmt-check clean; native suite 518/0, corpus 468/0, full suite 612/0. Remaining follow-ups: the return-type and parameter rules (`docs/vl-tech-debt.md`). (`compiler/cli.vl`, `compiler/typecheck.vl`, `scripts/vl-compiler-driver.vl`)
- **C-redundant-type: redundant RETURN-type annotations + applied to the compiler (−1180 annotations).** Extends the family to `function f(): T { … }` whose body's inferred return is exactly `T`. A `retNatural` accumulator (the first non-void/non-error return, mirroring the inference's `noteInferredRet`) is gathered while checking an ANNOTATED function, and a finding is recorded when it renders identically to the declared return; `--fix` deletes the `: T` between the params `)` and the body `{` (span ends found by token-index scans — robust in a merged compile). Conservative exclusions: an annotation-influenced return (empty `[]`/`Map()`/`Set()`, `null`) is load-bearing and kept; and the rule is scoped to SCALAR/STRING returns of NON-generic functions — exactly the categories the emitter (default + `A20`) lowers for an un-annotated function. Object / array / union / nullable returns and `self`-generic functions keep their annotation (the emitter re-derives those from the return expression and can mis-lower; array support is a follow-up `A20` widening). This was the hard one: it needed `A18` (order-independent scope), `A19` (binding-group recursive inference) and `A20` (elaborate inferred returns for codegen) to land first — removing an annotation makes the function inferred, and earlier the inference (forward globals, recursive cycles) or codegen (string/variable returns) couldn't keep up. **Dogfooded:** `vl check --fix compiler/ std/` removed **1180 redundant return annotations**, the seed rebuilt from the cleaned source is **byte-identical**, and the native fixpoint holds — every removal provably semantics-neutral. Validated: lint-self + fmt-check clean; corpus 477/0; native suite 518/0. (`compiler/typecheck.vl`, `tests/vl_check_redundant_type_test.ts`)
- **C-redundant-type: classify inferred `i32[]` returns for codegen (`A20` widening).** Extends `A20` + the redundant-return rule from scalar/string to `i32[]` returns: the checker exports the inferred `i32[]` return name and the emitter maps it to `fRetArr` directly (no synthesized node — `fmt`-safe), so an un-annotated function returning a `let`-bound i32-array emits correctly when indexed, and the rule now flags such a return as redundant. The compiler-wide APPLY (removing the ~22 now-redundant `i32[]` annotations) is a SEPARATE follow-up — it must bootstrap on THIS seed, since the release seed can't compile a source with those annotations removed until the i32[] classification is itself in the seed (each seed self-compiles the next). `string[]` stays out — `string` is internally `{[i32]:i32}`, so `string[]` is a ref-list whose backing wasm type the bare `fRetStrArr` flag doesn't drive (the annotated path registers it via the real `TypeRef`); follow-up in `docs/vl-tech-debt.md`. (`tests/cases/functions/infer-i32-array-return-codegen.vl`)
- **C-redundant-type: applied `i32[]` return cleanup (−22).** The compiler-wide apply that rides on the previous entry's seed: `vl check --fix compiler/` removed **22** now-redundant `i32[]` return annotations (the big-int math, byte-buffer builders, etc., across `ast`/`parser`/`typecheck`/`wasmEmit`). Seed rebuilt from the cleaned source is **byte-identical** and the native fixpoint holds — every removal provably semantics-neutral. Split from the classification change because the release seed must carry the i32[] classification before it can compile a source with those annotations removed (each seed self-compiles the next). Validated: lint-self + fmt-check clean; corpus 478/0; native gated suite 519/0.
- **C-redundant-type: classify inferred `string[]` returns for codegen (`A20` widening).** Extends `A20` + the redundant-return rule from scalar/string/`i32[]` to `string[]` returns — the last array case the rule can lower safely. The earlier i32[] entry parked `string[]` on the theory that a `string` is internally `{[i32]:i32}` so its list needs a per-function ref-list slot the bare flag can't drive; in fact `string[]` lowers to the SAME module-global string-list wrapper (`mkListIdx`, valtype kind 7) the annotated path uses, so the only gap was the un-annotated **function-signature result valtype** — it handled `fRetStr/Arr/Uni/Ref/Nul/RArr` but not `fRetStrArr`, so an inferred `string[]` return fell back to an i32 result and a caller indexing it trapped (`index receiver is not an array or string`). The checker now exports the inferred `string[]` return name (same side table as scalar/string/`i32[]`), the emitter sets `fRetStrArr` directly from it (no synthesized node — `fmt`-safe), and the signature path maps that flag to kind 7. The rule now flags such a return as redundant. The compiler-wide APPLY (removing the 7 now-redundant `string[]` annotations) is a SEPARATE follow-up — it must bootstrap on THIS seed, since the release seed can't compile a source with those annotations removed until the classification is itself in the seed (each seed self-compiles the next). Remaining array/return kinds kept annotated: `f64[]`, ref-arrays (`T[]`), unions, nullable — `docs/vl-tech-debt.md`. (`tests/cases/functions/infer-string-array-return-codegen.vl`, `tests/vl_check_redundant_type_test.ts`)
- **C-redundant-type: applied `string[]` return cleanup (−7).** The compiler-wide apply that rides on the previous entry's seed: `vl check --fix compiler/` removed **7** now-redundant `string[]` return annotations — the line-splitters (`cliSplitLines`/`splitLines`), `cliPopLast`, the definite-assignment snapshot (`daSnapshot`), the `&`-type splitter (`splitTopAmp`), and the param/capture name lists (`fnParamNamesOf`/`captureNamesOf`), across `cli`/`format`/`typecheck`/`wasmEmit`. Seed rebuilt from the cleaned source is **byte-identical** and the native fixpoint holds — every removal provably semantics-neutral. Split from the classification change because the release seed must carry the `string[]` classification before it can compile a source with those annotations removed (each seed self-compiles the next). Validated: lint-self + fmt-check clean; corpus 479/0; redundant-type unit suite 6/0.

- **C6 `vl test` — the in-language test runner (webcraft P1.6).** `vl test [path]` walks for `*.test.vl`, compiles each module-aware (so `std:` and relative imports resolve), and runs them **one wasm instance per file across a host thread pool**. Measured 1.11 s serial → **0.31 s at `--jobs 4`** on four CPU-bound files (118% → 425% CPU). **All POLICY is VL** — discovery, compilation, the plan, `-t` filtering, the report and the exit code live in `compiler/cli.vl` as a third subcommand (`cliCmd == 2`) on the existing command-queue pump — and exactly three raw mechanisms cross to Rust (`CMD_TEST_STASH` keeps an emitted module, `CMD_TEST_COLLECT` instantiates + reads each registry, `CMD_TEST_RUN` runs the plan), because instances, threads and trap catching are the engine's and the engine is not reachable from a wasm program. This is the `CMD_RUN_WASM` capability `docs/internals/cli-design.md` reserved. **`std:test` grew its registration half**: `describe`/`it`/`itSkip`/`beforeEach`/`afterEach` register into module-level parallel arrays at instantiation (the start function IS the collect pass), and the `vlt*` protocol exports let the host drive one test per call — which is what buys per-test trap isolation, output attribution and single-pass filtering. **A test file writes no boilerplate**: the runner APPENDS the protocol re-export to the source before compiling (appended, never prepended, so every diagnostic position in the user's file is unchanged — asserted). **Trap isolation is real**: a failed expectation, a raw `__trap__()` and an out-of-bounds index each fail their own test and nothing else — the host catches the trap and re-instantiates, and the fixture proves a test declared after two traps still runs and passes. **Failure messages are structural, not scraped**: the matcher records `expected 7 to equal 8` in a module global and the host reads it back off the unwound instance (`vltFailLen`/`vltFailAt`); a trap carrying no message falls back to the engine's text. A test file that does **not compile** is one failing entry with the compiler's own positioned diagnostics and the run continues. Exit 0 green / 1 any failure / 2 usage. Known v1 gaps, all filed: void-return covariance on function values (a body ending in an ASSIGNMENT needs a trailing `done()` — VL types a function by its tail), f64 failure rendering (`<f64>` + the values printed into the captured output, until `std:fmt` grows f64→string), no per-test timings/timeouts, no `--no-capture`/`dot`/`json` reporters. Two ROADMAP premises were refuted on the way: `std:fs` was **not** the gate (the walk was already in `cli.vl`), and "the linker stays EMPTY" was already false (every printing program imports `__print_*__`). (`docs/internals/vl-test-design.md`, `tests/vl_test_runner_test.ts`, `tests/fixtures/vl-test*/`)
- **C-fmt: the trailing-lambda exception (`vl test`'s top follow-up).** `vl fmt` exploded `it("adds", () => { … })` into a six-line vertical argument list **structurally, not on width** — a 34-column call broke exactly as a 100-column one did, because the list rule is "an argument spans lines ⇒ break every argument" and a block-bodied lambda always spans lines. Now the call **hugs** when its FINAL argument is a block-bodied lambda, every preceding argument fits on one line, and the head line fits `fmtWidth`. The three deferred design questions get one guard set rather than three rules: an EARLIER lambda renders multi-line, so a two-lambda call fails the "preceding arguments fit" guard and breaks vertically; a lambda FOLLOWED by another argument fails "the last argument is a lambda"; both rulings are what the corpus already spells (of the 38 block-lambda call sites in the repo, **36 are trailing**, **2 are the `callIt(lambda, k)` shape and are already written broken**, and **0** pass two lambdas). Expression-bodied lambdas are untouched. Implementation discipline that is load-bearing: `hugTrailingLambda` **decides before it renders**, because a lambda body is rendered through the formatter's CONSUMING comment cursor and a speculative render thrown away would delete every comment inside it at rc 0. **Blast radius zero** — all 33 gated `.vl` files stay `fmt --check` clean, so nothing in `compiler/`/`std/`/`scripts/` is reformatted and the compiler's own bytes are the only delta. All **8** `tests/fixtures/vl-test*/` fixtures are now fmt-clean AS WRITTEN (their "deliberately not fmt-normalized" comments are gone, and `tests/vl_fmt_test.ts` pins that they stay clean). Validated: idempotence over 1,675 parseable corpus files (0 failures); round-trip over all 1,693 (`vl build` of the original and of the formatted text byte-identical, 0 differences); the formatter's reject set unchanged (26 = 26); 4 corpus files format better and none worse; two sabotages (hug-nothing → 3 fixtures red, hug-everything → 1). (`docs/internals/fmt-trailing-lambda-design.md`, `tests/vl_fmt_test.ts`)

## LSP / editor (Track D)

- **UFCS METHODS COMPLETE AFTER `.` AND WRITE THEIR OWN IMPORT, AND THE `no field` DIAGNOSTIC GETS A QUICK-FIX** — the tooling half of the owner's 2026-09-02 ruling *"UFCS is never implicit: the compiler resolves `x.f(…)` only against names IN SCOPE; the LSP surfaces the import"*. `expect(1 + 2).` now lists `toEqual` / `toBeTrue` / `not` from `std:test` with `std:test` on the row and an `additionalTextEdit` that merges the name into the existing `import { … } from "std:test"`; `"hi".` lists `trim` / `split` / `padStart` from `std:str`, a module the file never imported, and inserts the statement. On the `no field 'toEqual' on Expectation<i32>` diagnostic there is now `` Import `toEqual` from "std:test" ``, one action per candidate module. **The candidate set is the CHECKER's** — one new LSP query, `ufcsCandidatesAt`, asking `declFirstParamIsSelf` + `assignable` of every declared `self`-function, which is literally the pair `ufcsCallTy` applies to a written call, so `Expectation<i32>` fits `self: Expectation<T>` and the offered set cannot advertise a call the checker would refuse; no type matching moved into TypeScript. Three findings the build turned up. **A BARE `import "std:str"` MERGES NOTHING** (measured: it resolves the specifier and the scan comes back empty), so an un-imported module is reached by one ALIASED named specifier — a local name that cannot collide, over a declaration name the alias does not touch; eleven std modules cost ~20 ms. **A MODULE KEY IS NOT A SPECIFIER** — the checker reports `/proj/shapes.vl` and the statement spells `./shapes`, so writing the key would have been a WRONG edit rather than a missing one, and only the workspace-module test could see it (`std:` keys *are* their specifiers); `importSpecifierForKey` inverts `resolveImportSpecifier` and prefers a spelling the file already uses. And a dep module's PRIVATE `self`-function must not be offered — `std:str`'s `mapAsciiCase` fits `self: string` exactly like `trim` — so the scan carries the `export` keyword's presence, recovered from the token stream by `ast.declHasExportKw` (lifted out of `lint.vl`, which had the only copy). **Two capabilities fell out, neither asked for:** a CALL receiver completes at all — the field scan STRIPS the trailing `.` and re-resolves the receiver as a BINDING, which only works for a bare identifier, while the UFCS probe APPENDS a property and keeps a real member access — and the same trick lets the quick-fix ask about `expect(1 + 2).toEqual(3)` with no repair, since the diagnostic points AT the member and the receiver is that access's object. The quick-fix keys on the stable `ufcs-not-imported` code, with the current sentence as the fallback until vl-07 lands it. `tests/lsp_ufcs_import_test.ts` (23 cases, 6 seed-backed); 140 corpus programs compile byte-identically against master's seed.

- **`duplicate-import` — the same specifier written twice now warns, and the compiler's own source had 122 of them (#2393)** — the owner's 2026-09-02 ruling on the half D1120 deliberately leaves running: `import { area, box } from "./a"` followed by `import { area } from "./a"` binds one declaration twice, which is redundant rather than ambiguous, so it stays legal and gets a `warning` — `` Duplicate import `area` from "./a" (remove one) `` — at the SECOND occurrence's name token, the anchor `unused-import` uses, so the LSP remove-import quick-fix serves it with a one-line dispatch change (and it carries the `unnecessary` tag, so editors grey the dead specifier). The rule keys on all THREE parts of a specifier (source TEXT, imported name, local binding) where the ERROR keys on the resolved declaration: that is what keeps `import { area as a } from "./a"` + `import { box as a } from "./a"` in `modDiagDupImport`'s domain, and what makes a re-export chain landing on one declaration free to stay legal — `"./a"` is not `"./b"`, and `lint.vl` is per-file and parse-only, with no module graph to consult even if it wanted one. Measured over `compiler/` and `std/`: **122 hits, 0 in std**, every one inside a second whole `import { … } from "./ast"` statement the first already covered (`format.vl` 32, `lint.vl` 26, `typecheck.vl` 35, `wasmEmit.vl` 29) — four block deletions, and the tree is clean. One knock-on fixed rather than shipped: binding-keyed use tracking resolves to the INNERMOST binding, so a duplicated VALUE import made the FIRST specifier read `Unused import` on a line whose name is used two lines down; `unusedImports` now lets the LAST binding of a name own that verdict. Pinned as `tests/cases/lint/duplicate-import.vl` (+ a distinct-local near miss), `tests/cases/modules/duplicate-import-reexport-chain/` (runs, no error, no warning), and a module-graph row in `tests/vl_check_module_lint_test.ts` that also asserts two DIFFERENT sources still ERROR with no lint on top.
- **D9 slot 12: a test failure ANCHORS at the `expect` that failed — the real fix, and the queued heuristic was never built (#2235)** — the slot chartered a cheap half: when a test body holds exactly ONE `expect(...)`, put the failure `TestMessage` on that call instead of the `it(...)` line, with multiple expects keeping today's anchor. Track-caller shipped first, so the RUNNER now reports the position and the editor reads it: `testDiscovery.ts` parses `std:test`'s `  at <file>:<line>:<col>` line into a `FailureLocation`, `failureAnchor` resolves it against the cwd `vl test` was spawned in — the module key is spelled exactly as the target was, so both sides resolve the same way — and the extension turns it into `TestMessage.location`. **Two things the heuristic could not have done, both pinned**: a body with SEVERAL expects anchors at the one that actually failed, and a failure inside a HELPER anchors in the helper's own FILE, which no scan of the test body could ever have found. An unsaved buffer runs from a mirror beside the original, so the target's own path maps back to the DOCUMENT rather than to a dotfile the user never opened (`isTarget`). The `it`-line fallback is kept for the failures that carry no location by construction — `fail(msg)`, a raw trap, a `<compile>` error — so its absence is normal rather than a parse miss. **The parser matches the location ANCHORED, on its own line, and stops at the `--- captured output ---` sentinel**: the assertion sentence ends in a RENDERED OPERAND, which is arbitrary user text and can perfectly well read `at x.vl:1:1`, and a program under test can print anything at all. Graded end to end against the real runner's output (`tests/vl_test_runner_test.ts` — expected line and column read OUT of the fixture rather than written down, plus a temp-dir one-hop case proving the helper's failure lands in `helper.vl`), and 8 new pure cases in `tests/lsp_test_discovery_test.ts`. (`lsp/src/testDiscovery.ts`, `lsp/src/extension.ts`)
- **Two parallel-ladder drifts the editor was shipping, both closed with a guard the audit filed as "Guard: NONE"** (`docs/internals/ladder-audit-2026-09.md` A1 + A3). **(1) The module-arming gate had four implementations in three languages and the two TypeScript ones had never learned the `export { … } from "…"` arm #2182 gave the CLI and the Rust host** — measured on `export { helper } from "./nope"` + `print(1)`: the LSP reported **0 diagnostics** where `vl check` reported `Cannot resolve import "./nope"`, and the symptom of a gate that does not arm is SILENCE, not an error. The two TS copies are now ONE leaf module (`compiler/moduleGate.ts`, zero imports) that `lsp/src/wasmChecker.ts` (VS Code *and* the playground) and `tests/cases_wasm_test.ts` both import; the VL and Rust copies cannot import TypeScript, so they stay mirrored under a guard that **extracts each one's arm set from its own source** and compares — sabotage-tested, deleting either `export` arm reddens it by name. **(2) Five keyword vocabularies, three of them missing `match`** (`compiler/driver.vl` contained the string `"MATCH"` zero times), so `match` painted as nothing at all and — because `VL_HARD_KEYWORDS` feeds rename's new-name validation — **the LSP accepted renaming a binding to `match` and wrote a file that does not parse** (measured: `const foo = 1` → `const match = 1`, five parse errors). All five now reconcile against sets DERIVED from the compiler: 19 hard from `lexer.vl`'s `keywordKind`, 7 soft from `parser.vl`'s contextual text guards. **The audit's "TextMate over-claims `new`" did not survive its own witness**: `const new = 1` runs (so `new` is not reserved) *and* `type Id = new i32` runs (so it IS syntax) — `new` is a contextual keyword, as is `flat` (`flat type R = { … }`), and neither was in any list; the two genuine inventions were Monarch's `fn` and `elseif`, which are not VL syntax at any position. Guards: `tests/module_gate_agreement_test.ts` + `tests/keyword_vocabulary_test.ts` (pure, in the `ci` job, with a loud floor so a stale extraction can never pass as "no drift"), `tests/vl_module_gate_test.ts` re-running the shared case table through the native `vl`, plus behavioural rows in the LSP checker and rename suites. Every extraction sabotage-tested one list at a time: 4 of 4 keyword lists and 3 of 3 gate copies redden, each with the failing entry named. (#2219)

- **D9 slot 10: signature help** — `textDocument/signatureHelp` on `(` and `,` (retrigger `)`): the callee's parameters with the one you are typing highlighted, in VS Code and the playground. The survey planned two grades and the CLEAN one turned out cheaper, so the bridge's rendered-string re-parse was never written: a new native export family (`sigAt` → param count, `sigParamName*`/`sigParamType*`/`sigRet*`) returns the callee's parameters AS DATA — the same decl-names-zipped-onto-`TyFunc.fnParamTypes` walk `fnSigStr` renders for hover (#2105), kept in columns instead of concatenated. A host re-parse would have had to parse VL's type grammar to know the comma in `(cmp: (i32, i32) => i32, xs: i32[])` is not a separator. A pure query — it reads `symOcc*`/`symBind*`/`symMem*` and records nothing; corpus movement zero. **UFCS drops `self` in the CHECKER**, not the host, so argument N is parameter N at both spellings (`shout("x", 2)` highlights `self`, `"x".shout(2)` highlights `n`) and no caller applies an offset. Also served: imported functions under their source parameter names, a struct field holding a function (`o.cb(…)`), a function-typed value (types, no names — `TyFunc` carries none by design), and a zero-parameter signature (0 rows; −1 is the refusal, and conflating them would make every `nil()` look unknown). A generic shows its DECLARED form, measured not chosen — the checker retains no per-call instantiation, and hover says the same thing at the same position. The host half is the lexical one only (`lsp/src/signatureHelp.ts`, third consumer of `vlLex.ts`): which call, which argument — a comma inside a string, a char literal, an array/object literal or a nested call is not a separator, and a template HOLE is re-entered as expression source (`f(\`v=${g(1, |2)}\`)` answers about `g`) while template TEXT is not. Mid-edit: every BALANCED shape already worked (empty argument list, trailing comma, wrong arity — a check error does not stop the symbol pass); an unclosed `(`, which the counter reads fine but the parser cannot, gets its closers appended and re-asked (`repairedSource`), tried only after the buffer as written comes back empty. Known gap, named: a BUILTIN callee (`print`, `xs.push`, `s.slice`) has no parameter table — the same absence that leaves member hover dark on them. 8 pure + 11 seed-backed tests. (#2199)

- **D9 slot 9: folding ranges + language-config indentation/on-enter rules** — `textDocument/foldingRange` over bracketed blocks, multi-line paren/bracket groups, `//` comment runs (kind `comment`) and the leading import block (kind `imports`), plus the `indentationRules`/`onEnterRules` the manifest never had. Regions come from the TOKEN stream, so `const open = "{"` opens nothing and `// }` closes nothing; a block ends one line above its closer so the `}` stays on screen. Mid-edit buffers are the normal case, so an unclosed opener yields no range (never a fold to EOF), a stray closer is ignored, and a mismatched one closes the opener below it. The survey planned this on `lexicalTokensAt`; comments turned out to be purely lexical, so the whole feature is **seed-free** — the one handler that still works when no compiler seed loads. The tokenizer `testDiscovery.ts` carried inline is now `lsp/src/vlLex.ts`, shared rather than rewritten (its 29 tests unchanged). Language config: increase indent on a trailing unclosed `{`/`(`/`[` that is neither inside a string nor after a `//`, decrease on a leading closer; `//` and `///` blocks continue on Enter and an EMPTY comment line ends the run — and no block-comment rule, because VL has none. 32 pure tests. (#2170)

- **D9 slot 8: per-test click-to-run (VS Code Testing API)** — Test Explorer + gutter arrows over `vl test <file> -t <substring>`, zero CLI/server/compiler changes. Discovery is a tokenizer over VL's real grammar (paren-depth nesting; `xs[it]("x")`, member calls, dynamic names, brace-holding names all ignored correctly — each a test); `-t`'s substring semantics are measured per request (describe runs under the strictly-longer `"<path> > "`, a contained `it` name surfaces its extra matches onto their own items with a note); the output parser pins the runner's column contract so a program printing `  ok fake` cannot forge a result; dirty buffers mirror beside the file (dotfile, cleaned in `finally`) so relative imports resolve. 29 pure tests + an end-to-end smoke against the real bundle and real `vl` binary. (#2112)

- **D0 Diagnostics on change.**
- **D1 Hover types** — `onHover` resolves cursor via D2 symbol table + `receiver.member` (object fields, array/list/string members via `typeFromExpression`/`listMemberType`/field); rendered via `stringifyType`.
- **D2 Go-to-definition / find-references** — symbol/binding table (`compiler/symbols.ts`); `textDocument/definition` + `textDocument/references`; locals, params, function decls, type aliases, single-document. → `DECISIONS.md`
- **D3 Autocomplete (core)** — scope-aware identifier completion + structural member completion (`lsp/src/typeFeatures.ts`); tested (`tests/lsp_completion_test.ts`).
- **D4 Formatter (core)** — AST-driven source formatter (`compiler/format.vl` via the seed, `vl fmt`, LSP `textDocument/formatting`); idempotent, round-trip-AST-equivalent, comment-preserving, 80-col reflow.
- **D5 Semantic tokens** — `textDocument/semanticTokens/full`: identifiers via D2 table, literals/keywords/operators via lexer, comments by source scan, `receiver.member` names (→ `property`/`method`).
- **D6 Inlay hints** — inline `: <type>` at unannotated `let`/`const`/params and omitted returns; annotated positions and unresolved holes suppressed.
- **D6 fix: an inferred array displays as `T[]`, not `{i32: T}`** — an array is internally an `{[i32]: T}` index-signature object; an array LITERAL (`[1, 2]`) and an `A-infer-empty` empty `[]` were keyed by the integer type `i32` and so fell through to the generic object render `{i32: i32}` in hover / inlay / error messages, while a `T[]` annotation already printed `i32[]`. Array construction now CANONICALIZES on a single `number`-keyed index signature (`number` = the i32-width array-index alias) across all three paths — the `T[]` annotation suffix (`parseArrayType`), the array literal (`ArrayLiteral`), and the intrinsic `listOf` (`.push`/`.map`/`.values()` results) — so a literal, an annotation, and an inferred-empty `[]; .push(1)` yield the SAME type shape and all render `i32[]` (`["a"]` → `string[]`, `[1.0]` → `f64[]`, `[[1]]` → `i32[][]`). `arrayElementType` / `isListType` / `getConcreteType` / `ensureType` treat the `number` key as the i32-width index (resolving to `i32`), so element inference, indexing, `.push`/`.length`, assignability, and codegen are unchanged; an explicit `{[i32]: V}` index-signature annotation keeps its `i32` key (still a native array, rendered `{i32: V}`), and a `string`-keyed map (`{[string]: V}`) stays a distinct map. (`tests/cases/arrays/render-i32-array.vl`, `tests/lsp_inlay_hint_test.ts`)
- **D3 Keyword + snippet completions** — 26 keywords + 10 snippet skeletons with tab-stops; after-dot completions suppress keywords/snippets; trigger-character tuning. (#143)
- **D4 Formatter: collapse short if/if-else** — a single-conditional `if { stmt }` or `if { a } else { b }` that fits 80 cols folds to one line; comments/multi-statement bodies stay block. (#138)
- **D4 Formatter: trailing comment on `type` alias** — a trailing comment on a `type X = …` line now stays on that line instead of being displaced. (#146)
- **D4 Formatter: verbatim-fallback for fn with commented expression body** — a function whose body is a single expression spanning multiple lines with an own-line comment is reproduced verbatim, preventing the comment from being displaced after the closing brace.
- **D4 Formatter: trailing comment on bare-body loop header** — a trailing comment on a `while`, `for`, or `for-in` header with a bare (brace-less) body (e.g. `while r < 10 // cond`) now stays on the header line instead of being displaced outside the enclosing function.
- **D4 Formatter: trailing comment on block closing brace** — a trailing comment written on the same source line as a closing `}` (e.g. `} // done`, `} // end of f`) now stays on that line for `if`, `while`, `for`, `for-in`, function, and free-standing blocks instead of being displaced to an own line before the next statement; the `if`-block case was also not idempotent (second pass re-moved the comment).
- **D4 Formatter: trailing comment on verbatim-fallback function last line** — a trailing comment on the last source line of an operator-named (`function +(self,b){…}`) or method-shorthand-body function (reproduced verbatim because the AST discards the surface syntax) now stays attached to that line instead of being displaced as an own-line comment before the next statement.
- **D7 Doc-comment cross-references (single-file)** — `` [`Name`] `` / `[Name]` rustdoc-style intra-doc links in `///` comments resolve via D2's symbol table and render as clickable markdown links in hover and completion `documentation`; unresolved names left verbatim; cross-import resolution deferred (needs H0 phase 3 module graph).
- **Module-aware diagnostics (H0 phase 3)** — the open file is analyzed as the entry module through a workspace `ModuleReader` (open buffers + disk, `lsp/src/moduleGraph.ts`): `import`ed names resolve to their real types instead of flagging "undeclared", and genuine import errors (bad path / not-exported / cycle) surface on the import line; hover/completion seed the same imported-name types; no-import files unchanged.
- **Cross-file navigation (H0 phase 3)** — go-to-definition and doc-comment `` [`Name`] `` xrefs on an imported name jump to the EXPORTING sibling module's declaration (`lsp/src/moduleGraph.ts` resolves an imported local name → exporting module + the export's decl span via the symbol table); find-references gathers a symbol's occurrences across the current file + other OPEN documents (graph-seeded so importer uses are recorded); single-file go-to-def/refs/doc-xref unchanged; refs over unopened on-disk siblings deferred.
- **Find-references: unopened on-disk sibling modules (H0 phase 3)** — find-references now crawls `.vl` files on disk that are not open in the editor: project root is detected from the LSP workspace folder or by walking up to the nearest `deno.json`/`package.json`/`.git` ancestor (max 6 levels); `.git`, `node_modules`, `dist`, `.claude`, `reference` dirs are skipped; at most 500 files per request; open-buffer text wins over disk; on-disk results are deduplicated against already-found open-doc refs by URI.
- **D8 (partial) Type-alias name preservation** — hover/inlay render the alias name (`Point`/`I32`) not its expanded body; `Type` node carries the source alias name (`aliasSymbol`-style), `stringifyType` `maxDepth=0` default preserves all names. (Verbosity step-expansion still ahead — needs proposed LSP 3.18.)
- **D — Project-wide unused-export hints (two signals)** — a debounced workspace pass (triggered on document save and after a 3-second idle) builds a global use-map over up to 500 `.vl` files and publishes `hint`/`unnecessary`-tagged diagnostics for two export conditions: (1) **fully dead** (`code: "unused-export"`) — exported symbol with zero references anywhere (not imported by any other module AND not used within its own file) — greys the export **name**; (2) **redundant export** (`code: "redundant-export"`) — exported symbol used only within its own module (e.g. a recursive function or a locally-consumed value) but never imported by any other module — greys the **`export` keyword** itself with message `` `export` is redundant — `foo` is only used within this module, never imported ``; the `export` keyword span is captured in `Binding.exportKeywordSpan` (stamped in `compiler/parser.ts` alongside `binding.exported = true`); the use-map tracks cross-module imports and same-file local uses separately (`ExportRefCounts { cross, local }`); struct fields are out of scope (structural typing makes field-level analysis fuzzy); merged with regular lint/type diagnostics; tests in `tests/lsp_unused_export_test.ts`.
- **kill-TS: semantic tokens off the self-hosted checker (lexical slice)** — the last TS dependency in the wasm semantic-tokens path is gone: new driver exports (`lexScan`/`lexClassAt`/`lexLineAt`/`lexColAt`/`lexLenAt` in `scripts/vl-compiler-driver.vl`) tokenize the staged source and classify each COLOURED token (keyword / operator / numeric+boolean literal / comment) natively — the counterpart of the host's TS `tokenize` + `lexicalTokenType` + comment scan. `wasmChecker.lexicalTokensAt` wraps them (`WasmLexicalToken`); `semanticTokensDataFromWasm` (typeFeatures) assembles a whole document from the wasm identifier + lexical + member slices with NO `tokenize`/`checkOnly`/AST, and the `"wasm"`-mode `textDocument/semanticTokens` handler now takes that path (TS only in `"ts"`/`"both"`/no-seed fallback). Incidentally fixes an operator-classification drift: the TS `lexicalTokenType` matched stale kind tags (`DIV`/`MOD`/`EXCLAMATION`/`EQUAL_TO`/…) the lexer never emits, so `/`, `%`, `!`, `==`, `!=`, `<`/`>`/`<=`/`>=`, `<<`/`>>`/`>>>`, and the compound-assigns went uncoloured; the native classifier keys off the real lexer kinds, so every operator now gets a token. (`tests/lsp_semantic_tokens_test.ts` — `wasm-lexical: …`)

The native parser isn't error-tolerant for the incomplete `receiver.`, so `server.ts` strips the trailing `.` (a `removeCharAt` repair) and resolves the receiver as a bare expression at its own position; the `"wasm"`-mode `onCompletion` `.`-branch takes this path, falling back to the TS `receiverObjectType` + `memberCompletions` only when wasm yields nothing (no regression). (`tests/lsp_member_completion_wasm_test.ts`)

The new `typeAliasAt` export (driver) + `symTypeAliasAt` (typecheck) close the type-alias-hover gap by scanning the token stream for the identifier under the cursor and resolving it through the checker's declared-types map (`cUserTypes`) — no new occurrence table; builtin hover reuses the PR-4a `builtinCompletions` list. No `checkOnly`/`parseSymbolsSeeded`/`importedScopeFor` on the wasm hover path (TS retained for `"ts"`/`"both"`/older-seed). Source `///` docs remain absent on wasm-mode hover (a pre-existing limitation now tracked in `docs/vl-tech-debt.md`). (`tests/lsp_wasm_checker_test.ts` — `wasm-symbols: typeAliasAt …`)
- **kill-TS: inlay hints off the self-hosted checker (+ inferred-return retention fix)** — `inlayHint` in `"wasm"` mode now sources the inferred types + declaration positions from the native checker (`inlayScan` export over `symInlayScan`, wrapped by `wasmChecker.inlayHintsAt`); the source-scan filters (skip an annotation the user wrote, place a function's hint after its `)`, honor the request range) stay host-side in `inlayHintsFromWasm` (typeFeatures), reusing the same helpers as the TS `deriveInlayHints`. No `parseSymbols` on the wasm inlay path. **Checker fix:** an unannotated function's demand-inferred return is now written BACK into its retained symbol-table type (`checkFuncDeclNode` re-retains after inference) — previously the retained `fnRet` kept the `-2` infer-later sentinel, so hover rendered `(i32, i32) -> <none>` and a function-return inlay hint couldn't be produced; both now show the inferred `-> i32`. Pure type relocation — no behaviour change.

The `vital.checker` `"ts"`/`"both"` modes and their live parity instruments (`diffDiagnostics`/`diffHoverType`/`diffSemanticTokens`/`diffDefinition`/`diffReferences`) are gone, along with every TS fallback path (`checkDocument`/`checkOnly`/`parseSymbols`/`parseProgram`/`tokenize`/`defaultScope`) and the helpers that fed them (`importedScopeFor`/`parseSymbolsSeeded`/`buildDocRefResolver`/`ctxToRange`). Each handler now runs the native path and degrades to an empty/no-op result when no seed is loaded (rather than a TS fallback). `server.ts` imports NOTHING from the compiler core — only the diagnostic types (the leaf) and `format` (the formatter fallback, its finale separately gated on the playground migration). The surviving cross-file functions (`crossFileReferences`, `canonicalExportOf`, `buildUnusedExportUseMap`, `unusedExportHints`) are wasm-backed. `moduleGraph.ts` now imports only the `ModuleReader` glue type + the diagnostic leaf — nothing from the compiler core (lexer/parser/typecheck/compile/defaultScope/lint/ast). - **kill-TS: the wasm checker is now environment-agnostic** — `wasmChecker.ts` no longer touches `node:fs`: its loader splits into `createWasmChecker(instantiate, wrapReader?)` (the env-agnostic driver protocol — types, the symbol/token/scope/member/inlay + format/lint query families, the diff helpers) and a new `wasmCheckerNode.ts` that owns the `node:fs` seed load (path → bytes, mtime-reload) + the `withStd` reader wrapper and delegates to the core. Node consumers (`server.ts`, the wasm-checker tests, `checker-parity-sweep.ts`) import `loadWasmChecker` from `wasmCheckerNode.ts` (which re-exports the whole core surface); the std overlay is now an injected `wrapReader` rather than a hard `withStd` import, so the core has no `node:fs`/DOM coupling. This unblocks the browser playground driving the SAME self-hosted checker (fetched seed + embedded-std reader) — the keystone for retiring the playground's TS LSP transforms. Pure refactor — no behaviour change. (existing `tests/lsp_*wasm*`/`lsp_wasm_checker_test.ts` cover it via the relocated import.)
