Those types move to a new dependency-free leaf `compiler/coreTypes.ts` (mirroring the `diagnostics.ts` precedent); the original homes re-export them so the compiler's internal imports are unchanged, and the editor layer imports them from the leaf. `lsp/src` now references only the two neutral leaves (`diagnostics.ts`, `coreTypes.ts`); the sole remaining `compiler/*.ts` runtime importer outside the core is `tests/std_resolution_test.ts` (the TS module-loader test). Also deletes the fully-orphaned `compiler/wasmDebug.ts` (zero importers). Pure type relocation — no behaviour change; `deno check`/`deno lint`/LSP+playground builds clean.
- **D9: flow-narrowed types in hover AND member completion** — inside `if r is string { … }` hover shows `string` and `r.` in an `is IoError` arm offers its fields (both previously showed/offered the declared union or nothing). One `symOccTy` column retains the checker's OWN narrowed type per occurrence (gated on the live narrowing shadow; nothing re-derived); one shared `symOccQueryTy` feeds both surfaces so they cannot disagree. Negative `else` arms, `!= null`, assignment narrowing, `else if`, and `while` guards all narrow; declarations, guard operands, and re-widened positions correctly don't; property-path narrowing (a different overlay) flagged as follow-up. (#2108)
- **D9: hover polish — one demangling render pathway + named function signatures** — `tyToStrUser` (demangle∘render, the single user-facing pathway) cleans all eight audited query exits (hover/member/alias/inlay/completion details/redun/rcoal messages); `tyToStr` stays raw (its spellings are canon/interner keys). The audit found and fixed two live defects: type-alias hover was completely DARK in multi-module programs, and the entry module's own `$m0` mangle leaked with zero imports. Function hovers now zip decl parameter names with the type: `it: (name: string, body: () => void) => void`, defensive bare-type fallbacks, slot-10's read point noted. (#2105)
- **D9: rename symbol (+prepare)** — alias-aware rename over the references machinery: exported names rename everywhere including import specifiers; an `x as y` alias renames only locally; std-declared bindings, the mixed plain+alias import, and keyword/invalid new names are REFUSED with visible reasons (refuse-rather-than-guess, each case measured). Found en route: `referencesAt` reports an imported decl at the dependency's own coordinates — rename routes around it; the pre-existing raw consumers are noted for follow-up. (#2103)
- **D9: `source.organizeImports`** — VS Code's Organize Imports command, palette entry, and on-save integration light up from the well-known code-action kind, zero client-side code. fmt-canon semantics: per-statement rewrite (unused specifiers from the lint tier at request time; survivors spelled by the seed's `formatSrc`; zero survivors deletes the line; statements never merged/reordered), idempotent, no-op-silent on clean files. `onCodeAction` now honors `context.only` for QuickFix too. (#2097)
- **D9 batch 1: document highlights, seed status-bar, flat outline, export ref-count code lenses** — four editor-surface-queue features off the existing checker surface: highlights pair `referencesAt` with one `definitionAt` for Read/Write kinds; the status bar shows which seed-ladder rung won (`vital/seedOrigin` notification, warning state when NO seed loaded — the previously invisible degraded state); document symbols give a flat Outline/breadcrumbs (functions, module-level bindings, type aliases, export-flagged); code lenses show `N refs` per export from the save pass's existing use-map with lazy click-through to the references peek. 21 tests across four suites, wired into ci-native; playground parity gaps documented as knownGap rows. (#2088)
- **Four diagnostics from live editor use: the span, the sentence, and one import that STOLE a string from further down the file** — (1) a deferred operator refusal now names the ARGUMENT and anchors at it: `double({foo: "bar"})` on `(a) => a + a` said `… for {foo: string} and {foo: string} (the call's argument types)` with the caret on the call's `)`, reading as two arguments for a one-argument call, and now says `argument 1: … (the body of \`double\` uses it on both sides of '+')` spanning the argument; two distinct arguments get `applies '+' to arguments 1 and 2` (no head, since a head would blame one of them), and a SHARED type variable (`g<T>(a: T, b: T)`, where `T ^ T` is what both `a ^ b` and `a ^ a` record) keeps the old sentence unchanged and takes only the better anchor — which is why the corpus moved **no cell and no message**. (2) Char-literal length errors span the whole literal: a TOKENLESS diagnostic has no anchor token for `diagEndCol` to size, so every lex and module-resolution report was a one-column caret however much source it was about; `Diag`/`vcDg*`/`modDiag` carry their own exclusive end now, and `'xy'` gets `^~~~` instead of a caret on the quote. (3) **A char-quoted import specifier made the import adopt the next string literal ANYWHERE in the file** — `modScan`'s walk to the path STRING skipped every non-STRING token, past the statement and past the line, so `from 'std:fs'` (a CHAR token) reported `Unsupported import specifier "passes"` against an `it("passes", …)` further down. The parser had grown exactly this bound already and the second scanner never did: `isStmtKeyword` is now imported from the parser so the two cannot drift, and a char literal in the specifier slot gets its own sentence (`importSpecCharMsg`, shared by both scanners) spanning the literal — one error, no cascade, the bait string in no message. (4) A char literal landing in a `string` explains itself: `cannot assign i32 to 's' of type string — a char literal is its i32 code point; use double quotes for a string: "x"`, keyed on the SOURCE FORM (a `CharLit` node) so a plain i32 keeps the plain sentence, at all four positions that can carry it (declaration, argument, return, write). All eleven gates; corpus **no cell changed class**, `runs` 4,620 / 7,564 unchanged; filed witnesses 341/341 `--strict`. (#2182)
- **Diagnostics anchor at the OFFENDING token; fmt guarantees a blank line after imports** — `argument N` mismatches anchor at the argument (single-token literals get a real `^~~` span; a function-literal argument whose provable offence is its RETURN anchors at the return site — `return 7` puts the caret on the `7`); char-literal length errors anchor at the opening quote; fmt forces exactly one blank line between the import block and the first statement (idempotent, four tree files moved one line each), with the LSP auto-import insertion carrying the blank so accepted completions stay fmt-stable. Corpus: no cell changed class. (#2083)
- **D4 Formatter (self-hosted) quality pass** — `format.vl` gains first-line-only indent on wrapped object literals, trailing-comment alignment within a block (opt-in when any comment in the block sits >1 space off its token), forced-paren wrapping for over-wide `if`/`while` conditions, per-clause `if`/`else if` chain reflow, parameter-list wrapping, and inline-collapse refinements. (#445, #447–#452)
- **`vl fmt` is ~linear** — fixed O(n²) hotspots (the `joinOut`/`joinLines`/`normalizeProgram` string accumulators and the `lineOf`/`exportPrefix` per-node scans) that crashed (`allocation size too large`) or hung on large files; now divide-and-conquer joins + binary-search lookups. (#455)
- **Parser: newline after `(` / before `)`** — `parsePrimary` skips newlines around a parenthesized expression (porting the host's behavior), so `vl fmt`'s forced-paren condition output re-parses. (#454)
- **`vl fmt --check` gate** — the whole `compiler/`, `std/`, `scripts/` tree is `vl fmt`-clean, enforced in `scripts/lint-self.sh` + CI (tests/ excluded by construction); landed via a one-time tree reformat. (#456)
- **cleanup: `0 - N` literal idiom → unary `-N`** — ~915 operand-position numeric-literal sites in the compiler source; semantically identical (unary `-` lowers to the same `push 0; <x>; i32.sub`, so the self-compiled seed is byte-identical). (#457)
- **kill-TS: retire the TS formatter (`compiler/format.ts`)** — the self-hosted `format.vl` (via the seed) is the sole formatter for `vl fmt`, the LSP, and the playground; `format.ts` had no remaining importers and is deleted. `lsp/src` and `compiler/cli.ts` reference no TS formatter.
- **Editor-surface survey (`docs/internals/editor-surface-survey.md`) + two fixes it found** — the full LSP 3.17 + VS Code API surface graded against the shipped extension and the WasmChecker's actual capabilities, with a prioritized shortlist (Testing API per-test runs first; `vl test -t` already suffices). Fixed: `vital.compilerPath` never reached the server's seed ladder (initializationOptions carried only compilerWasm), and a dead `registerProposedFeatures()` after `client.start()`. (#2079)
- **Run Current File: workspace-anchored terminal; `*.test.vl` routes through `vl test`** — the run terminal's cwd fallback ended at the extension install path (under a symlinked install: `~/.vscode-server/extensions`); now `deno.json` root → workspace folder → file's dir → `$HOME`. A test file runs via `vl test` instead of `vl run` (which executes only the registration pass), with the dirty-buffer mirror keeping the `.test.vl` suffix. (#2078)
- **Seed ladder: the bundled seed outranks `vl seed`; auto-import items no longer lose the accept race** — an installed CLI's embedded seed was ABI-compatible but BEHAVIORALLY stale (pre-scopeAt-filter): `speaksAbi` accepted it and completion silently regressed in every non-checkout workspace, so the seed PAIRED with the server binary now wins (the failure modes are asymmetric — `vl seed`-first fails silently, bundled-first fails visibly; a build-identity stamp is the real resolution, noted in the ladder doc). Also dropped the auto-import `sortText` demotion: demoted below the editor's word-based suggestion, Tab accepted the word (no import rewrite) whenever the completed name already appeared in the buffer. (#2077)
- **D3 Auto-import completions for std exports; `scopeAt` stops leaking dep-module internals** — completion offers std exports NOT in scope (labeled with their module), and accepting one rewrites the import statement via `additionalTextEdits`, spelled by the seed's own `formatSrc` so `vl fmt` never rearranges it (fmt sorts specifiers; new-module imports land after the last import). Natively, the driver's `scopeAt` now filters the merged program's visibility rows to the entry module + its actual imports (exact merged-name match via `modMergedTargetOf`) — previously every dep binding leaked into entry completions (std internals, un-imported exports, mangled type details like `Expectation$m1`; types now pass `demangleMsg`). Also `bundle-seed.ts` prefers the checkout's `../build` seed over `vl seed` (the bundle must carry this tree's compiler). (#2074)
- **Go-to-def on a std export opens the std source (`vl-std:` scheme)** — a std import's module key (`std:test`) is not a path, but `toCrossFileSource` piped every key through `pathToUri`, so jumping to any std export errored on `file://std%3Atest`. `crossFileUriOf` now mirrors `withStd`'s read precedence: the workspace's own `std/NAME.vl` when it exists (dogfooding → the real file), else `vl-std:/NAME.vl`, served read-only from the embedded map by a `TextDocumentContentProvider` in the extension — same generated map the checker reads, so ranges can't drift. (#2072)

## Browser playground (Track E)

- **E1 Browser bundle** — esbuild + `esbuild-deno-loader`; binaryen@130 runs client-side ESM; `deno task playground`.
- **E2 Playground UI (core)** — `<textarea>` + Run + diagnostics/log/WAT panes + sample picker (`playground/`).
- **E2 Playground redesign** — branded light/dark theme pair (system-default with revert-to-system toggle, lock-step Monaco theme), results-as-tabs (Output/WAT/Diagnostics + size/count badges), multi-file projects (per-file diagnostics, whole-program `compileProgram` run/WAT), opt-in auto-run (always-on debounced analysis), full-width status bar, real Share + Format wiring.
- **E4 Shareable links** — source encoded in URL hash (#94).
- **Playground↔LSP parity test** — `tests/playground_lsp_parity_test.ts` enumerates the language features `lsp/src/server.ts` exposes (handlers self-validated against the live source) and asserts, per feature, that `playground/src/lspAdapter.ts` exports the pure binding AND `playground/src/main.ts` wires the matching Monaco provider — so an LSP feature can't be added without wiring the playground (the gap that left "Auto Fix" silently missing). Three current gaps are documented as asserted known-TODOs: code actions (`registerCodeActionProvider` unwired in `main.ts` though the `codeActions` adapter binding exists), find-references, and completion.
- **kill-TS: the playground's LSP runs on the self-hosted seed** — the playground's language features (semantic tokens, hover, inlay hints, go-to-definition, completion, format) no longer run the TS `typeFeatures` transforms / symbol table; they drive the SAME `build/vl-compiler.wasm` seed the Node LSP and `vl check` run, through the environment-agnostic `createWasmChecker` core. New `playground/src/wasmCheckerBrowser.ts` fetches the seed (`new URL("vl-compiler.wasm", import.meta.url)` — copied next to the bundle by `build.ts`) and instantiates it with an embedded-std reader (the `std:` half of `withStd`, no workspace dir in a browser); `lspAdapter.ts` is rewired to drive it (mirroring `server.ts`'s wasm-mode handlers) + the kept `*FromWasm` assembly helpers, with `main.ts`'s providers now awaiting the async results. The features degrade to empty (format to a no-op) until the seed loads, and stay disabled if it can't be fetched — Run is unaffected (it still uses the TS compiler + binaryen, pending the codegen-export migration). Diagnostics stay on the TS `checkOnly`; quick-fixes stay pure string surgery. The GitHub Pages deploy (`pages.yml`) fetches the seed (`fetch-seed.sh`) and ships it in the artifact so the live site keeps these features. `playground/verify.ts` exercises the full bundled path; `tests/playground_lsp_wasm_test.ts` pins it in CI (and `playground_completion_test.ts` moved to the seed-backed path). This makes `playground/src/lspAdapter.ts` the last consumer of the TS `typeFeatures` transforms to migrate — clearing the way to delete them.

- **kill-TS full-delete P3 (step 1+2): `vl fmt` + the compiler CLI off the deno tasks** — the native `vl` binary (`scripts/vl-host`) gains a `fmt` subcommand driving the seed's `formatSrc` (the formatting logic lives in `format.vl`; the Rust host is just I/O), matching the TS CLI's surface: `vl fmt <file>` → stdout, `-w/--write` → rewrite in place when changed, `--check` → non-zero exit on drift, `<dir>` → recurse `*.vl` (skip-list: `node_modules`/`.git`/`dist`/`reference`), stdin → stdout; a parse error leaves the source unchanged. Like `-O`, it's an OPTIONAL external tool resolved `$VL_WASM_DIS` → PATH (a shared `binaryen_tool` helper now backs both `wasm-opt` and `wasm-dis`), enables exactly the GC + reference-type features WasmGC output needs (not `-all`, which wasmtime would reject), and is a soft no-op when absent. The "binaryen missing" note is unified into one `cfg!`-tailored helper: the macOS build suggests `brew install binaryen`, other platforms point at the package manager / prebuilt releases — so it never suggests `brew` on Linux. README/AGENTS document the binaryen dependency for `-O`/`--wat`.
- **kill-TS full-delete P3 (step 3b): `vl run` from `-e`/stdin** — `vl run` reaches TS-CLI parity for its input sources: `-e "<snippet>"` (inline source), stdin when piped (`… | vl run`), a file, or a prebuilt `.wasm` (magic-byte detection — runs straight through wasmtime). Like `fmt`, `run` is dispatched ahead of the positional `<cmd> <input>` parsing (its arg shape has no file with `-e`/stdin). An interactive TTY with no input shows usage instead of blocking on stdin forever; an empty snippet/stream is a clean usage exit (2). The compile+run tail is factored into a shared `compile_and_run` (seed compile with the `name` section for legible traps → DRC-engine run).
- **kill-TS full-delete P3 (step 3c): `vl check` reports lint + severity, pretty output** — `vl check` moves from type-errors-only toward TS-CLI parity. It now MERGES the error tier (`checkSrc`) with the lint tier (`lintSrc` — `unused-variable`/`prefer-const` warnings, intentionally-unused hints), the same diagnostics the editor shows (the `cargo check`-shows-warnings model; a heavier `vl lint` can come later). `--severity <hint|info|warning|error>` (and the `--severity=` form) does double duty — it gates the exit code (default `error`: only errors fail) AND raises the display floor (default: show everything); an unknown level is a clean exit 2. Output is rustc/Deno-style PRETTY by default (`[SEVERITY]: msg` + source line + caret, ANSI color auto-gated on a TTY and `NO_COLOR`), with `--concise` for the grep-friendly `file: severity [L:C] msg` one-liner. `--codegen` runs the full `compileSrc` so emit-tier errors surface. On a rejection the summary NAMES the failing stage — `Found N errors. (parse|type|emit error)` — so tooling (the native-align reject suite) can classify WHERE the front end rejected. The seed staging (module-fetch loop + `srcReset`/`srcPush`) is factored out of `compile_vl` into a shared `stage_program`, reused by the new check path. (Single-file for now; a directory walk + `--exclude`/`--ignore` is the next slice. The TS `cli_codegen` test's binaryen-specific `recursion limit exceeded` message is a TS-path artifact the self-hosted emitter won't reproduce — it'll be retired with `cli.ts`, not ported.)
- **playground fix: cross-file LSP (imported names + dependent locals)** — the playground's editor features ran single-file (no sibling reader), so in a multi-file project hovering an imported name (`add`, `square`) or anything whose inferred type depended on one (`let r = add(square(3), 4)`) showed no tooltip — only builtins like `print` resolved (VS Code, with its workspace reader, was unaffected). `lspAdapter` now takes the active file's KEY + a workspace reader over the live project buffers (wired by `main.ts` via `setWorkspace(projectFiles)`), the browser counterpart of the Node LSP's `workspaceReader`, so an importer's graph resolves: `add` → `(i32, i32) -> i32`, `r` → `i32`. Every feature (hover/semantic tokens/inlay/definition/completion) threads the entry key; single-file queries (and the unit tests) default to `main.vl` with an empty reader. (`tests/playground_lsp_wasm_test.ts` — cross-file hover case.)
- **playground: code-split binaryen off the initial load** — with codegen on the seed, binaryen (~13 MB) is reached ONLY via the lazy `import("binaryen")`/`import("./toWasm.ts")` behind `wasmToWat` (the WAT renderer). `build.ts` now enables esbuild `splitting` (`outdir` + object-form `entryPoints` → `playground.js`), so binaryen lands in its own `chunk-*.js` fetched on demand when the WAT pane is first shown — not on page load. The entry `playground.js` drops from ~22 MB to ~2 MB (the rest is lazy chunks: Monaco's on-demand features + the binaryen WAT chunk). `pages.yml` ships the chunks (`dist/*.js`); `index.html` still loads only `playground.js` + `playground.css`. WAT stays a feature (binaryen disassembling the seed's bytes), just off the critical path.

## Infrastructure (Track F)

- **THE `??`-MERGE FAMILY IS AN INDEX, NOT TWENTY-FIVE ARENA SCANS — a four-line program that imports two std modules builds in 22 ms where it took 5,006 ms (D1514)** — `vl check` of `tests/cases/literal-unions/litunion-order-cross-module-alias.vl` is 0.08 s and `vl build` of the same 38 lines was 7.0 s. **The second instance of #2419's class, one rung deeper and three levels nested**: `anonLeafCloSlotMark` asks `anonLeafParamFnTarget` per callback-typed parameter, that asks `anonLeafParamFnTargetAt` per `Param` of the name, and that scanned every `Call` calling `anonLeafCallMayTarget`, which asks `anonLeafOneDeclNamed` — itself a whole-arena scan — per candidate. Cubic in the MERGED module's node count, so a program's own length says nothing about what it pays. Guest profile of the emitter before: `anonLeafOneDeclNamed` **59.2% self**, `__str_eq__` 17.3%, `anonLeafFnValueNames` 11.4%, `anonLeafFnValueTargetGo` 10.5%, `anonLeafParamFnNamesAt` **97% inclusive**; after, no `anonLeaf*` function appears in the top ten of either the self-compile or a 300-callback program. **The fix is a REBUILT index, not a prefix memo, and the distinction is the point**: `moduleHasUnionAs` resumes because its answer only grows, while "is this call wild" and "is this name used as a value" are whole-arena facts a suffix can change — so `anonLeafIxBuild` runs once per program before the first mark pass and hands every reader the same nodes in the same ARENA ORDER (order is load-bearing: `anonLeafParamFnNamesAt` appends to its caller's set and `anonLeafCloSlotMark` takes the FIRST member). D1100's own two-column declaration index answered two of these questions by linear scan and is folded in and deleted. **Two prunes make the call-site lists small and both are exact**: a call whose callee is declared exactly once can only target THAT name, and a wild call can only reach a name some `Ident` spells outside callee position, because every non-empty answer the delivery resolvers give comes from a write, an argument or a return expression. The second is load-bearing, measured by removing it: 300 callback slots go from 5.5 s to not finishing in 200 s. **Byte-identical, on the largest program available**: the candidate compiling master's own 100k-line compiler source gives the same 2,046,160 bytes master's compiler does, and `refresh-compiler.sh --prove-fixpoint` holds. Measured at load ~32, `vl build` before → after: the witness **7027 → 31 ms**, `std/array-sorted.vl` **4847 → 35 ms**, `generics/mono-callback-bound-arm-beside-layout-twin.vl` **5694 → 39 ms**; the corpus oracle (`deno test -A --parallel tests/cases_wasm_{0..3}_test.ts`, 2,710 cases) **14.5 s → 2.3 s**; `scripts/scan-budget.py` **132 → 107** scans outside a pass, 53 → 28 in `emit_collect.vl`. **The guard this owes is a new scaling-shape axis**, `callback slots` — N higher-order functions each taking a callback against N/K taking the same N callbacks over K call sites — which reads 1.92 on the fix and does not finish in 200 s on master at a SEVENTH of N. Neither existing guard could have fired: the compiler's own source declares no callback-typed parameter, so `self-compile-time.sh` never paid it, and none of the seven shape pairs varied that entity. (`docs/internals/profiling-the-compiler.md` §"Measured 2026-09-03")

- **A std COMMENT IS API SURFACE — every `std/*.vl` comment rewritten for a CONSUMER, 1,919 comment lines to 689, and `std-comment-audience` keeps them that way** — the comment BUDGET capped LENGTH (12-line blocks, 40-line headers) and said nothing about AUDIENCE, so every std header sat at its cap reading as internal commentary: defect ids, PR numbers, dates, mechanism, arguments with earlier versions of the file. That is the wrong audience for the one file a caller actually reads (owner CODE YELLOW). **The rule**, written into `docs/internals/std-api-review.md` §4 and CLAUDE.md: a header of at most **10 lines** (what the module is for, how to import it, what it deliberately does NOT do); **1–4 lines** directly above every `export` (what it does, what its arguments mean, what it returns, and the edge case a caller must know); **0 or 1** for a private helper; and everything true about the COMPILER rather than the API out of std entirely, into the new `docs/internals/std-notes.md` — **which std does not link to**, so a caller never lands in the internals. Headers went 38/40/40/36/40/40/40/40/40/38 lines to 7–10; the 45 comment lines citing a row id, a PR number or a date went to **0**. **NOT ONE non-comment byte changed**, proved three ways: the filtered diff is empty; a self-compile off the same fixpoint seed with master's `std/` and with the new one is byte-identical (`cmp` clean — the compiler graph does not include `std/`); and because a std trim is NOT byte-identical downstream for user programs (trap messages embed `line:col`), all **67** of `tests/cases/std` were built and run on both arms and compared on build rc, run rc and stdout — **67/67 identical**. **The gate**: `std-comment-audience` in `compiler/lint.vl`, module-scoped by a module path the driver and CLI now set beside the source — the `std:` KEY the graph walk hands over, or a target rooted at `std/`, which is the shape `lint-self.sh`'s `vl check std/` produces; a bare `/std/` ANYWHERE was tried and dropped, because it would hold someone else's `src/std/` to VL's own rubric — tier `warning`, **no baseline** — it lands and stays at zero, so `lint-self.sh` reds on a regression rather than ratcheting one in. It flags a header over 10 lines, an export doc comment over 4, and any std comment line citing `D\d{2,4}`, `#\d{3,4}`, a `2026-` date, `DECISIONS`, `inventory`, `emitter`, `rep` or `arena`. A rule that lands at zero has no tree evidence that it still FIRES, so `tests/vl_std_comment_audience_test.ts` plants each violation and demands the finding at its exact line, with the same file under a non-`std/` directory as the CONTROL — a scoping bug would otherwise surface as noise in every other tree instead of as a red here — and pins the two shapes that must stay quiet (a 5-line block on a private helper; a 5-line section banner separated from the doc comment it precedes by a blank line). **FIVE stale claims fell out on the way, and that is the lesson rather than a footnote**: a comment lifted verbatim out of std into `std-notes.md` is a measurement with its date stripped off, and re-running the witnesses refuted four of the paragraphs on the day the file was created — `scripts/capability-probes/i64-list-pop.vl` RUNS (so `bnLen` and the untrimmed limbs are now removable by the note's own instruction), the Rust host's decimal-tie divergence closed with D1011 (that suite's test is now named *"print(x) and toString(x) agree at every vector"*), D1030 closed 2026-09-02 so `toJson(r)`, `r.toJson()` and `const v: Json = r` all run, and D947's non-atom union `toEqual` passes at both an `i32` and a struct payload. The fifth was in std itself: `std:array`'s `concat` comment said `+` over two lists is narrower than `concat` and cited D102's `type F = 1.5 | 2.5`; `+` RUNS at all five spellings that comment listed. Each is now recorded as history with its re-measurement, and `parseJson`'s doc — which told callers to work around D1030 with the row id stripped out, making it ungradeable — was deleted outright. **The `std-api-reviewer` graded the change INCONSISTENT on exactly this class** and on two rubric rows the rewrite itself made stale (§1 cited a `fmt.vl` sentence the rewrite deleted; §2's "the header names the constraint" test was one no module could pass after §4.4 moved that material out) — all six blocking findings are fixed here, including the §2 reconciliation that now decides WHERE a deviation's reason lives: the header when a caller can see it, `std-notes.md` when only a maintainer can.
- **THE SEED'S SIZE IS NOW A GATED PER-LANDING NUMBER — `scripts/seed-size.py`, a committed one-line baseline, and a +3% bar** — `build/vl-compiler.wasm` is the compiler's codegen of its own source, so it prices every emitter change in bytes, and it was read only when somebody went looking: a reported **1,834,521 → 1,996,118 (+8.8%)** across four landings on 2026-09-03 (#2448, #2449, #2450, #2452), noticed because a peer asked. Same ratchet shape as `comment-budget.py`: `--check` in `scripts/gate.sh` (a milliseconds-long row) and in ci-native right after the fixpoint step, `--write-baseline` in the SAME PR as the growth it records. It reds **only above +3%** — shrinkage and small growth print and pass, because the event this owes an alarm for is unexplained growth, not a byte target; and because the baseline moves only when a human rewrites it, an unattended series of landings faces 3% TOTAL rather than 3% each. **The deciding reading is the FIXPOINT's, and that is a measured distinction, not a caution**: at `ff4b5f04` one `refresh-compiler.sh` rung gave **1,842,901** bytes against a fixpoint of **1,996,118** — 8.3% apart at one commit, larger than the bar — because one rung off a stale seed is the PREVIOUS compiler's codegen of current source. ci-native therefore takes the reading immediately after `--prove-fixpoint`. `tests/vl_seed_size_test.ts` grades the bar at the boundary from both sides (exactly at it passes, one byte past fails) on a fake baseline/size pair in milliseconds, with no seed and no `vl` binary, and pins the two behaviours the gate leans on (shrinkage passes; an absent seed exits 0 saying so, since the `ci` job builds none) plus the baseline's one-line shape and both runners still invoking it. Validated against a control: widening the constant to 5.0 reds the boundary case. Baseline written at `ff4b5f04`: **1,996,118 bytes**. Rationale: DECISIONS.md §"The seed's size is a per-landing number".
- **ci-native's four quick wins — a sharded corpus oracle, two split suites, both sidecar tags warmed, and a content-keyed sidecar** — the `ci-native` job went 53 s (2026-07-30) to 250 s on ~2x the inputs, and `docs/internals/perf-opportunities-2026-09.md` ranked why. **(1)** The corpus oracle was ONE file, so `deno test` ran all 2,786 cases on ONE core; it is now `tests/support/casesWasmOracle.ts` plus four `tests/cases_wasm_<k>_test.ts` shards, and `--parallel` gives each its own worker — three alternating pairs, median **25.7 s -> 11.2 s wall**, identical `2688 passed / 0 failed / 9 ignored` on both arms — and the +25% user the survey predicted for four seed loads does not appear at low load (25.7 -> 25.1 s). A shard is a CONTIGUOUS block of the sorted case list, not `i % n`: the cases share one `WebAssembly.Instance` by design, and round-robin reordering turned `unions/paren-narrowed-receiver-read.vl` red behind `unions/nullable-variant-positions.vl` — **a real per-instance emitter state leak the corpus order was masking**, filed in §F5, not fixed here. **(2)** `selfhost_native_release_test.ts` (36 tests, one worker) split into four files, **64.7 s -> 20.9 s wall**; `vl_buffer_view_bounds_shape_test.ts` into two, **18.8 s -> 14.0 s**; both with the test bodies moved verbatim and the count asserted equal (36 = 36, 19 = 19). `vl_check_codegen_test.ts` is deliberately NOT split — measured, 19.00 of its 19.08 s is ONE test, whose cost is `vl check --codegen` re-checking the std graph once per file in `tests/cases/std` (45.9 s against `soundness/`'s 0.79 s), so neither a file split nor concurrent directories moves it. **(3)** `refresh-compiler.sh` carried forward only the `.cwasm` sidecar its own sanity `vl run` made, leaving the `vl check`/`fmt`/`test` engine tag COLD at the start of every native step — so every worker that started before the first JIT published re-compiled the 1.8 MB seed itself. It now warms both tags concurrently and prints the count: alternating A/B of the whole step, **681 -> 351 s of user CPU, -48%**. **(4)** The on-disk sidecar is keyed by the seed's CONTENT (`<seed>.<seed key>.<engine tag>.cwasm`), as the embedded path already was, instead of by mtime — a byte-identical rewrite (`touch`, a `cp` between worktrees, a cache restore) went from a **4.43 s** re-JIT to **0.02 s**, and a different seed at the same path retires the old key's files so `build/` stays at two. Priced rather than assumed: the key is hashed on every invocation, byte-at-a-time FNV-1a cost +2 ms of `load_compiler` (6 -> 8 ms), so it is four-lane word FNV at **+0.85 ms**. Graded against a pristine `origin/master` tree beside this one: `scripts/gate.sh`'s slowest row **149.9 s -> 88.8 s**, with `deno task test` **3181 passed / 0 failed / 2977 ignored** and `ci-native` **3059 / 0 / 3** IDENTICAL on both arms — the test-count equality proof at gate scale. Every number, its load and its script are in `docs/internals/perf-opportunities-2026-09.md` §F — including the RUNNER, which the survey could not measure and this PR's own job now does (§F7): the corpus-oracle step is **40.5 s -> 24 s** by median there (3 runs against 6 on master), and item 3's estimated −10 s **does not reproduce — on four cores it is net negative** (the native step stays inside master's own 121–147 s spread while the refresh grows 12 -> 39 s paying the JIT up front — on four cores the storm is four workers deep, so the -330 s of CPU is a 24-worker effect and the CI ledger is a wash). (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `scripts/refresh-compiler.sh`, `scripts/vl-host/src/main.rs`, `tests/ci_seed_coverage_test.ts`)

- **A KIND LADDER WITH A HOLE IS A LINT — `kind-ladder-incomplete` + `kind-ladder-split`, ratcheted like the comment budget** — four instances in one week and one rule covers all four: `eqConcreteVariantRow`'s missing `nulvariant` rung (#2400), `modRwExpr`'s missing `IfStmt` arm (D981), `tpMemberFloorMsg`'s wordless unbounded-`TyVar` default (D1004/D1221) and `captureValKind`'s i32 fallback for a module-block capture (D1370). **The rule**: a run of `if` / `else if` arms, inside ONE function, testing the SAME subject against members of ONE closed set must be exhaustive over that set, or end in a DEFAULT THAT NAMES what it excludes — an `emitFail`, a sentence of twelve characters or more, or a delegation to the ladder that owns the rest; a bare fall-through to `-1` / `""` / `false` / `0` names nothing, which is exactly how `memberFloorMsg` came to format an empty string. **The closed sets are read from the tree, not copied into it**: twelve of them (`Node` 37, `TokKind` 72, `VKind` 30, `EqCmpKind` 17, `RtKind` 15, `Ty` 11, `PrimName` 10, `MfKind`/`PushKind` 7, `AsMode`/`BtKind`/`LitKind` 3), and `scripts/ladder-budget.py` re-derives every one from the `export type` that declares it, comparing members AND order against `compiler/lint.vl`'s copy and refusing to run on any drift — validated against a control (one member deleted from `klBtKind` fails the gate and names the set). **The floor is two arms and it is MEASURED**: at one arm the `const n = P.nodes[ix]; if n is X { … }` guard idiom floods (1,901 silent ladders), at two it is 440 and at three 248 — and D1370's ladder has exactly two, so three cannot see it. **`kind-ladder-split`** is the D981 shape the first code provably cannot catch: one walk over one enum SPLIT by syntactic position into two ladders where the first's default hands the rest to the second, the second hands none back, and the second drops a kind the first tests. It fires on `modRwStmt`/`modRwExpr` on both sides of #2447 — 12 dropped kinds before, `IfStmt` among them, 11 after — and the CONTROL, `urcExprClean`/`urcStmtFlags` in `lint.vl` itself, which hand back BOTH ways, stays silent; the union-gap clause was measured and dropped, because it fires on that control too. **440 + 9 hits**, ratcheted per file by `scripts/ladder-budget.py --check` (its own `gate.sh` row, the `--exempt-codes` hand-off to `lint-self.sh` that deletes itself at zero, sibling of `comment-budget.py` and `scan-budget.py`). Python and lint agree **file for file on all 440 and site for site on all 9** — the one divergence found on the way was the naming tell reading a COMMENT's quoted string, which graded a silent default as named. **`scripts/ladder-census.py` is the discovery half**: `--sets`, the ladder table with a widest-first ranking (`checkNodeReal` 35/37, `nodeChildren` 25/37, `jwKids` 22/37, `repSigTokOfKind` 21/30, `monoWalk`/`drwWalk`/`cboxWalk` at 18–20), `--split`, and `--pred` for the form with NO kind literal in it at all — a chain of rungs calling helpers named after storage classes, which is where #2400's hole lives and where nothing that greps for `== "<kind>"` can see it (pre-fix `eqConcreteVariantRow` grades `variant struct`, missing `nulvariant`; post-fix all three). Byte-identical: master's source compiled by the seed carrying the lint is the same bytes as master's own fixpoint (1,997,222 at `c8379662`, self-reproducing in one step). (`tests/vl_kind_ladder_test.ts` — four fixtures pinning the false positives: a delegating default, a membership test written as one `||` expression, a refusal default, a single-arm guard, and a pair that partitions a set and hands back both ways; CLAUDE.md §"A LADDER OVER A CLOSED KIND SET", `docs/internals/registry-by-type-id.md` §6)

- **THE INDENTED-FALLBACK WITNESS RULE IS RETIRED BY CONSTRUCTION — every row carries a `Repro:` label, so no row can be graded on prose** — #2445 made a `Repro` lead-in WIN over an earlier indented block but had to keep the fallback, because rows existed that carried no label at all and would have gone ungradeable. This closes that: the rule that could reach an English paragraph is gone, not merely outranked. **The population was measured by instrumenting the grader's own parse, not read off the brief: 25 rows, not the 17 expected** — `D964`, `D982`–`D987`, `D989`, `D1009-N` in `docs/internals/inventory/`, and 16 of `inventory-2`'s 17 (`D988` and inventory-2's `D14` already had labels). Every one of the 25 blocks was confirmed to be the row's REAL witness before it was labelled — each parses, and each produced its row's declared outcome on the day's seed — and each row's `**Control**` programs sit below the defect program, so the fallback had never taken the wrong block on a row that still relied on it. **The edit is a label and nothing else, and that is proved rather than asserted**: snapshotting all 527 rows' extracted program through the grader's own parser before and after gives **527 of 527 byte-identical**, with 25 rows moving `indented fallback` → `Repro block` and no row moving the other way; the whole `--strict` run is byte-identical too, **527 graded · 527 as filed · 0 MOVED · 0 not graded · 0 UNPARSED** on both sides. `tests/vl_inventory_rows_test.ts` loses the `VL_LINE` "looks like VL" predicate it needed to tell prose from a program — with no unlabelled block accepted there is nothing to tell apart — and gains a faithful mirror of the grader's `block_at` scan window, so a row it calls gradeable is one the grader reports the same way. **Validated against a PLANTED row** carrying a perfect `print(6 * 7)` and no label: green on both pre-change instruments (grader rc 0, the planted row graded `runs / runs / as filed`; rows test 2 passed), red on both after (grader rc 1 `not graded (no Repro block)`; rows test naming the retired fallback in its `got:` line). Deleting it again is itself checked — `tests/vl_inventory_refs_test.ts` reds on the control's id surviving in this very entry, which is how the number above is spelled out rather than cited. **And the control found a hole in the instrument doing the enforcing**: #2445 widened the PYTHON's `SEC` to admit a hyphenated suffix and left the test's copy narrow, so `D1009-N` was a row the rows test could not see — it would have accepted that row with no `Repro:` label at all, and a second plant confirms it (a hyphen-suffixed id, unlabelled: old test 2 passed, new test reds). Widened to match, and the widening is not the fix — the test now counts the POPULATION of `### D…` headings against what `SEC` parsed, the same `ROWHEAD` audit the python grew for exactly this, so the next id shape nobody anticipated reds instead of vanishing.

- **A WITNESS THAT DOES NOT PARSE IS ITS OWN GRADED OUTCOME — `--strict` was passing on PROSE, and D957 was the row** — the grader's fallback rule ("the first indented block after the status line", which 28 of 527 rows genuinely depend on) took D957's numbered-list continuation lines — five spaces in, correct Markdown, English — ahead of the `Repro:` block further down. `vl check` answers `(parse error)`, that mapped to `check_reject`, the row's declared status matched, and the row graded `as filed` while it had already been CLOSED by #2381. Two fixes, both general: a `Repro` lead-in now WINS over an earlier indented block, and a check refusal whose summary names the PARSE stage grades **`witness_unparsed`** — the fourth column, failing `--strict` — unless the status explicitly files a parse error as the outcome. **Measured before touching anything**, per row, which rule supplied the repro and whether the program parsed: **527 rows · 499 `Repro:` block / 28 fallback · 4 repros that do not parse**. Three of the four (D46, D444, D471) file a parse-stage refusal deliberately and now SAY so in their status lines; the fourth was D957. `tests/vl_inventory_rows_test.ts` gets the structural half — it runs no program, so it decides by SHAPE: a block counts only if its first non-blank line opens like VL (a keyword, a comment, a directive, or an identifier VL punctuation follows), which **522 of 523 rows passed on the day it was written and the one failure was exactly the paragraph**. Both instruments were validated against PLANTED prose, with and without a `Repro:` label — grader `not graded (… block came from the indented fallback / Repro block)` rc 1, rows test `an indented block that does not open like VL` — and the shape rule keeps an in-process specimen table so a predicate that accepted everything could not look identical. **D957 gets its real witness back and it RUNS**: the filed program prints `2` un-annotated, and a two-face grid over `i64` / `f64` / `f32` / `string` / `i32` / `boolean` is **12 of 12 at rc 0** — including the i32-backed leaf whose missing fifth site sank the fix the row itself describes, because #2381 (D1062) closed it by pinning the annotation rather than by typing a new un-annotated seed. Whole-tree grade unchanged either way: **527 graded · 527 as filed · 0 MOVED · 0 not graded · 0 UNPARSED**.

- **`KNOWN_UNFILED` RETIRES TO THE THREE NUMBERS THAT WERE NEVER ROW IDS — the six ids shipped work cited with no row are settled, four by FILING and two by naming the PR instead** — the reference-integrity test landed holding nine exemptions, and the six real ids were the debt. **Four are real defects, filed under their ORIGINAL ids with witnesses re-measured on today's seed rather than copied from the citation**: `D973` and `D974` (struct-union `==`, and its nested-shape field) close as `runs`; `D949` (a generic application losing its NAME across `substTyDeep`) is `now a loud check reject` whose MESSAGE is the discriminator, measured on both compilers — `cannot assign {v: i32} to 'bad'` on a control self-compiled from `fef77fc1`, `cannot assign Box<i32> to 'bad'` today; and **`D705` is OPEN, `check-clean invalid wasm`** — a module-scope `string` shadowed by an i32 function-local, where the disassembly shows the emitter choosing `print`'s STRING arm from the module table and writing the i32 into it. **The citation that sent us there was wrong twice**: `tests/cases/generics/error-pin-global-shadowed-by-local.vl` said the row was FILED (it was not), and said a STRUCT global fails the same way (it RUNS) — and the GENERIC in its own spelling is not an ingredient at all, so the defect is not mid-mono. The other two were WORK LABELS a row would have fictionalised, and their citations now name the PR that did the work: the scoreboard concedes-phrase audit is **#2122** (7 sites, `CLAUDE.md` included), the `is <literal>` hint is **#2404** (3 sites). What remains exempt is only `D800` / `D1000` / `D174` — a UTF-16 code point and two reservation-range closing endpoints — each with its reason in the list, and a code rule to skip them was considered and rejected as the worse option. Grader: **510 graded · 510 as filed · 0 MOVED · 0 not graded**.

- **Three guards so the #2419 class of compile-time regression cannot come back — scaling-SHAPE pairs, an arena-scan lint with a ratchet, and an L2 time tripwire** — #2419 lost 59% of a self-compile to two module-wide predicates re-derived once per emitted FUNCTION, and nothing in the tree could have caught it: the source reads identically either way, and a wall-clock budget has to be loose enough for the slowest box that runs it. One guard per moment. **Review time — `arena-scan-outside-pass`** (`compiler/lint.vl`, `warning`): a `while` bounded by a whole-program table (`P.nodes`, `fnStmts`, `sNames`, `unNames`, `uVariants`, `globalStmts`) inside a function that is neither a row of `emit_sections.vl`'s pass table nor one of seven allow-listed once-per-module scanners, each carrying its caller count as its reason. **A scan resuming from a memo is exempt** — the loop variable must be a `let x = 0` in the same body — because `let i = modUnionAsSeen` IS the #2419 fix and flagging it would ask for the repair twice; `moduleHasUnionAs`, `moduleHasNumCast` and `nameNamesFunction` are all correctly silent while `fieldClosureFeOfRecv`, which got a gate rather than a memo, is still named. **132 hits**, ratcheted per file by `scripts/scan-budget.py --check` (sibling of `comment-budget.py`, same `--check`/`--write-baseline`/`--exempt-codes` shape, its own `gate.sh` row); the script re-derives the pass list from `runEmitPass` and **fails when the lint's copy disagrees**, and reads the tables and the allow-list out of `lint.vl` itself, so there is one source of truth. Python and lint agree **line for line on all 132 sites**. Byte-identical: master's source compiled by the seed carrying the lint is the same 1,818,040 bytes as master's own fixpoint. **Merge time — `tests/vl_scaling_shape_test.ts`**: seven pairs of the same work reshaped along ONE axis — functions, types, unions, call sites, closures, modules, generic pins — graded on the TIME RATIO, because machine speed, JIT warm-up and box load multiply both arms and cancel. Across box loads of 3 to 101 absolute times moved 3× while the four linear axes' ratios moved under 0.12; the three super-linear ones move up to 0.76, which is the other reason their bars sit clear of the measurement. 16–25 s for the family, its own `gate.sh` row, and **validated against the pre-#2419 compiler, which reds the `functions` pair at 5.81× (bar 2.5) and the `closures` pair at 6.95× (bar 3.2)**. **Three axes are already super-linear and carry a bar just above their measurement rather than the default 2.5**, each naming the function so the bar is recorded debt and not tolerance — and all three are name-keyed registries answering a lookup by linear scan, which is the `__str_eq__` track #2419 left open: **closures 2.22×** (`fnStmtsPosOf`, 21.2% self on the many arm and absent from the one arm, a scan of `fnStmts` per closure), **modules 2.47×** (`modIndexOfKey` 47% and `capHas` 35% inclusive, `__str_eq__` 73% self; 800 modules against 400 is 4.45×) and **generic pins 4.37×** (`collectA` 68% inclusive against nothing on the one arm, interning each pin through `tyTopIndexOf`; 0.23 s at 200 pins, 0.84 s at 400, 3.23 s at 800). **Bootstrap — `scripts/self-compile-time.sh`**: the candidate compiling the compiler, in CPU seconds against `scripts/self-compile-baseline.json` (**6.3 s idle**), tripping past **4×**; `native-fixpoint.sh` now prints the same quantity for its stage 4. **Half that factor pays for contention, and the first cut proved it the hard way**: committed at the idle number with a factor of 2, the gate row went red on its own ladder at 12.7 s against a 12.6 s line — CPU seconds are the honest column under load but they are not contention-proof, and the same build reads 12.2–12.7 s inside a fanned-out `gate.sh` at load 164 against 6.0–6.3 s idle. The baseline stays the IDLE reading, which is reproducible on any box and survives a careless re-baseline, and the FACTOR carries the contention; it is read from the baseline file so the number and the band travel together. It warms the `.cwasm` sidecar untimed first, because Cranelift-compiling a freshly refreshed seed is 7.9 s of the 14.2 s a cold run measures and would have tripped the wire on whichever gate row reached the new seed first — warmed, it reads 6.0–6.3 s cold-start and 6.2–7.4 s at load 54. The old `tests/vl_module_predicate_scan_test.ts` is folded in as the family's `functions` axis. (`docs/internals/profiling-the-compiler.md` §Guards; CLAUDE.md §"A COST REGRESSION SHOWS UP ONE BOOTSTRAP STEP LATE")

- **Guard rails against comment sprawl — two lint rules on a self-deleting ratchet** — `compiler/*.vl` is 171k lines of which 42% are `//` comments, and the drift is not only length: three wrong fixes in one day came from comments that were confidently STALE (a kind ladder said to have no variant cell that had two; a canon arm said to widen a literal run that does not; a residue priced "both verdicts LOUD" whose cells were SILENT). So `compiler/lint.vl` gains **`comment-block-too-long`** (a maximal run of own-line `//` lines, budget 12 — 40 for the MODULE HEADER, the first block with no code before it, blank lines and the leading `import` region allowed, which is #2413's `format.vl` shape; the message names which budget applied) and **`comment-measurement-uncited`** (a block stating a measurement — a count with a unit, a denominator, a date, a graded verdict beside a count, `measured`, `byte-identical` — while citing no `D<row>` / `DECISIONS` / `.md` home, at ANY length). Comments are lexer trivia the parse path never carries (the per-module token cache banks tokens and no comments), so the driver hands the module SOURCE in through `lintSetSource` — the `fmtSetSource` idiom — and the scan consumes it, one fused left-to-right pass per comment line. Baseline on landing: **1,488 blocks over budget and 477 uncited, across 37 files**, so the tree cannot go to zero in one PR and both rules ride a per-file RATCHET (`scripts/comment-budget.py --check`, a `gate.sh` row and a CI step: a file may only go down or stay; `--write-baseline` lowers it beside a trim). `scripts/lint-self.sh` holds exactly these two codes out of its `info` gate — the allow-list is READ FROM the baseline, so the exemption deletes itself at zero instead of needing to be remembered. The lint and the script are two implementations of one definition, so `tests/vl_comment_budget_test.ts` runs both over four fixtures — a clean one, one carrying a 13-line block, a 40-line block, an uncited measurement and the same measurement cited two ways, and two pinning the header split (30 lines at the top passes, the same 30 below code fires, a 45-line header fires and its message names the 40-line budget) — and compares the hit LINES; they agree on all 40 tree files today, per code and per line. The rule's own bound is written down: a `//` opening a line inside a multi-line template literal counts as a comment, in both implementations, and the tree has none.
- **Comment trim, pilot — `parser.vl`, `format.vl` and `emit_sections.vl` to the 12-line comment-block budget, with a byte-identical seed** — `compiler/*.vl` measured **42% comment lines with 694 blocks of 20+ lines**, and the long ones are lab notebooks: census counts, probe output, A/B tables, the history of how a line came to be, living in the code. The three pilot files went from **72 blocks over 12 lines to 2**, and both survivors are module HEADERS carrying their own 40-line budget (16 and 29 lines); **648 comment lines left the compiler and none was deleted** — every trimmed block's text is archived verbatim in `docs/internals/parser-notes.md`, `format-notes.md` and `emit-sections-notes.md`, one section per block, while the comment that stays keeps the invariant, the WHY, and a pointer to the inventory row / DECISIONS section / notes heading that owns the rest. **The safety proof is byte identity**: `refresh-compiler.sh` before and after produces the same 1,765,387-byte seed (`cmp` clean), and the diff carries no non-comment line at all. **The campaign's second product is that a comment is never re-run by a gate, so a measurement inside one is a claim with no grader — and three in these three files were already false.** `parser.vl`'s header still read "side-by-side with `compiler/parser.ts`", with two more sites naming `parser.ts` (deleted in #466); `format.vl`'s header named `compiler/format.ts` (#458) and `scripts/vl-compiler-driver.vl`, neither of which exists; and `emit_sections.vl`'s `$fnsig`-key census claimed "`driver.vl`'s two `<` are the only ones there" when `driver.vl` carries no `<` literal at all. The trimmed comments drop all three, and each notes file names the staleness above the archived text.
- **Comment trim, batch 2 — `emit_mono`, `emit_state`, `emit_base`, `emit_rewrite`, `tyname` and `ast` to the 12-line budget, byte-identical seed** — the six files carried **234 blocks over budget and 88 uncited measurements**; both are **0**, with **2,584 comment lines gone** (9,081 → 6,497, across 18,146 → 15,562 total lines) and the longest non-header block at **12**. **The pilot's notes-file archive is NOT repeated**: #2413 moved every trimmed block verbatim into `docs/internals/*-notes.md`, and the owner's direction for this batch is that a claim belongs in the GRADED channel or not at all — so each surviving block keeps the invariant, the WHY that stops the next "simplification", and a pointer to a `D<row>` / `DECISIONS.md` § / `docs/internals/*.md` home, while every one-off lab number no harness re-runs was dropped with its qualitative argument kept (the byte A/Bs behind a declined tokenizer, the corpus percentages behind a sparse column, the invocation counts behind a probe). **The safety proof is byte identity, twice over**: `refresh-compiler.sh` before and after produces the same **1,824,510-byte** seed (`cmp` rc 0), and stripping every own-line `//` from both revisions leaves each file's remaining source **byte-for-byte identical** (3,763 · 440 · 1,937 · 1,065 · 426 · 1,434 lines, all unchanged) — a stronger check than the diff filter, since it also catches a blank line moved into or out of a block. **And the trim caught eleven claims that were already FALSE**, each verified against today's tree rather than assumed: `ast.vl` carried an orphaned doc paragraph describing `fnRequiredArity` glued to the top of `fillArgDefaults`'s header while `fnRequiredArity` itself sat undocumented thirty-seven lines below (moved back), and called `nodeChildren` a two-consumer helper when six modules now import it; `tyname.vl`'s header roster listed the file's bodies and was missing **eight of forty-three** — the exact failure its own text warned about — and its space-rule census routed to `emit_classify.spacelessName` and its generic-argument cut to `splitTypeName` / `splitGenArgs`, none of which exist; `emit_state.vl` cited `toWasm.ts` and `compiler/builtins/maps.ts`, both deleted, and ten symbols through them; `emit_rewrite.vl` named `drwEveryInstanceTakesField`, renamed to `drwAnyInstanceTakesField` when unanimity was relaxed; `emit_base.vl` carried two ORPHANED function headers above unrelated functions plus four dead copy-sites (`monoUnwrapParens`, `nameIsSingleShape`, `internNonLowerableFieldShapes`, `internShapeFieldElems`) and named `typecheck.vl` as the home of four grammars that live in `tyname.vl` now; `emit_mono.vl` narrated a `nominalizeFnType` that is only `nominalizeFnTypeOfTy` today. The ratchet drops to **1,255 over budget / 389 uncited** (`scripts/comment-budget.py --write-baseline`); the two codes stay on `lint-self.sh`'s allow-list because that list is read from the baseline TOTAL, which `emit_classify.vl`, `typecheck.vl`, `wasmEmit.vl` and `emit_collect.vl` still hold above zero.
- **Comment trim, batch 3 — `emit_collect.vl` to the 12-line budget, byte-identical seed** — the file carried **124 blocks over budget and 46 uncited measurements**; both are **0**, with **1,325 comment lines gone** (5,872 → 4,547, across 13,895 → 12,570 total lines) and the longest surviving block the **14-line module header**, inside its own 40-line budget. Batch 2's rule is kept: no notes-file archive, every surviving block reduced to the invariant, the WHY that stops the next "simplification", and a pointer to a `D<row>` / `DECISIONS.md` § / `docs/internals/*.md` home, with every one-off lab number no harness re-runs dropped and its qualitative argument kept (the dual-write disagreement counts behind each arena conversion, the census cell counts behind a measured decline, the corpus reach counts behind a coverage gate). **The safety proof is byte identity on the MERGED tree**: `vl build compiler/entry.vl` from `origin/master` and from this branch, through the same pinned seed, gives the same **1,831,804-byte** module (`cmp` rc 0, identical md5), and stripping every own-line `//` from both revisions leaves **8,023 identical lines** of remaining source — the stronger check, since it also catches a blank line moved into or out of a block. **Three ORPHANED function headers were found and moved back to the functions they document**: `forceGenAppArgTypes`, `collectA` and `collectTyReachRegister` each had no header of their own while their prose sat above an unrelated function further up the file — the same class `ast.vl` and `emit_base.vl` turned up in batch 2, and the reason the block count RISES by three. **Two stale citations were corrected**: `toWasm.ts`, deleted in #466 (batch 2 fixed the `emit_state.vl` copies and this was the last one in this file), and `xfail-miscompile-permuted-struct-fields.vl`, renamed `types/permuted-named-alias-shares-row.vl` in #1501. The ratchet drops to **1,131 over budget / 343 uncited**; the two codes stay on `lint-self.sh`'s allow-list because that list is read from the baseline TOTAL, which `emit_classify.vl`, `typecheck.vl` and `wasmEmit.vl` still hold above zero.
- **Comment trim, batch 4 — `typecheck.vl`, the campaign's largest file, to the 12-line budget, byte-identical seed** — the checker carried **365 blocks over budget and 69 uncited measurements**; both are **0**, with **3,937 comment lines gone** (17,095 → 13,158, across 39,843 → 35,906 total lines) and the longest surviving block the **28-line module header**, inside its own 40-line budget. The block COUNT is unchanged at 2,355, which is the check that no blank line moved into or out of a block. - **The defect inventory splits into ONE FILE PER ROW — the script, the consumers on both forms, and the two gates the shared tail was hiding** — `docs/internals/silent-class-inventory.md` was one ~38,000-line file that every defect PR appended to, so two concurrent PRs conflicted in its tail nearly every hour; on 2026-09-02 one such resolution spliced two rows into the middle of a third (gate red twice) and another **silently DELETED a row**, whose citations still stand in `DECISIONS.md`, `ROADMAP.md`, `compiler/check_state.vl` and a test. `scripts/inventory/split.py` writes `docs/internals/inventory/D<id>.md` per row plus a generated `INDEX.md`, moves the non-row prose to `README.md` verbatim, and leaves the monolith as a ten-line pointer so the ~60 citations that name the path do not 404. **It lands by being RUN on merge-day master, not as a hand-maintained diff** — a 38,000-line diff rebases wrongly and does it silently, which is the failure being fixed — so it is idempotent, and `--apply` refuses to write unless five losslessness checks pass: block coverage (the parsed blocks re-concatenate to the source byte for byte), unique ids, each row file a VERBATIM substring, each row file a PREFIX of its block with only blank lines and a lone `---` dropped after it, and a rejoin in id order. `scripts/inventory/selftest.py` makes all five FIRE on specimens whose fault is known by construction — and caught a real one: the first separator check was computed from the same function that produced the files, so it could not fail whatever the input. **Two directories, not one**: the inventories number independently and D1..D14 exist in BOTH. Consumers read either form — `check-filed-witnesses.py` takes a directory (a directory with no rows yet falls back to the monolith named in its own README, one marker line read by python and by deno), `tests/vl_inventory_rows_test.ts` reads the directories and now also requires a row's heading id to equal its file stem, and `scripts/inventory/ls.py --status open` replaces the `grep '^### D' … | tail` that answered with a row's TITLE where the grader reads its STATUS. - **The position-matrix harness — one template, every delivery, both faces, graded** — `scripts/capability-probes/matrix.py` reads a `matrix/*.matrix.vl` template (prelude, value, its type spelling, and a proof over the bound name `v` that prints something only a correct conversion can produce) and generates one standalone program per POSITION × FACE, grading each in `run.py`'s vocabulary — `RUNS` / `WRONG` / `check refuses` / `emit refuses` / `SILENT` / `COMPILER TRAP`. **Twenty positions**: binding, inferred and annotated return, argument, struct-field init and assignment, array element, element assignment, **`.push`**, module global init, global-to-global assignment, map value, closure capture, `is`-in-`if`/`while`/`&&`/`!`, `else if`, the early-return guard, and two instances in one module — each in the ANNOTATED and UN-ANNOTATED face, because the two land in different clauses. CLAUDE.md's rule was already the rule and the grids were still hand-written, which is where the misses come from: D965 lost global assignment (eight callers of the sibling read like the complete list and were not), D1193 was silent at seven of nine, #2406 missed the un-annotated return face and the early-return guard. `--before`/`--after` grade two seeds side by side and the exit is non-zero on `runs → not-runs` or any `SILENT` after; `--keep` leaves the cells so a red one is filed as a probe. **The grading is `run.py`'s, imported rather than copied** — one `vl` invocation per healthy cell (`run` first, `check` only to name a failure's channel), so `run.py` got faster and both read one scale. Four templates ship as the instrument's own controls, and the load-bearing one is **D1197's `array_push`, which grades `SILENT`** — a probe nobody has seen fire is measuring nothing (`tests/vl_capability_matrix_test.ts`). Three findings fell out on first use, none of them the row under test: an INFERRED anon struct whose field holds a union value is `emitProgram: object literal matches no union variant` at all three union templates while the annotated destination runs; an un-annotated PARAMETER loses the literal-`is` complement narrowing its annotated twin has; and a closure capturing a struct local declared inside a block is `emitProgram: field access receiver is not a struct` (ablated — the narrowing is scenery, the block scope is the ingredient).
- **D1242 / D1243 / D1244 — the three defects the position-matrix harness found on its FIRST use, filed with witnesses, ablations, both faces and probes** — none of them was the row under test, which is the harness's own argument: a capability is enforced in one place and served in many, and the positions nobody hand-writes are where the misses live. Each was reproduced from scratch on the merged tree, delta-debugged to a minimal witness, and ablated one ingredient at a time, so the family is the ABLATION and not the message. **D1242 — an INFERRED anonymous struct whose field holds a union value** is `emitProgram: object literal matches no union variant` on a three-line program (`const u: i32 | null = 5` / `const w = { f: u }` / `print(w.f ?? 0)`), `vl check` rc 0, while the annotated destination prints `5`. The ablation names the real mechanism, and it is not the annotation: **declaring `type W = { f: i32 | null }` and never mentioning `W` again makes the same un-annotated binding run**. The rescue is shape REGISTRATION — a `type` declaration registers the shape, inference never does, and the emitter's fallback for an unregistered literal is `emitUnionBox`, whose `objVariantName` answers `""`, which is why a program with no union type in it gets a message about union variants. It is shape-keyed (a different field name does not help; the same field name with a non-union type mis-registers it and the failure moves downstream), and the checker VOLUNTEERS the breaking edit as `[HINT]: redundant type annotation … remove it to lean on inference`. Its new matrix template grades **19 of 28 · 9 other**: every annotated cell runs and **nine of fourteen un-annotated cells refuse in four different messages**, which the row lists as a grading list rather than asserting as one family. **D1243 — an un-annotated parameter has the `is` HIT arm but not the COMPLEMENT**: `if a is "err" { print(a + "!") }` prints `err!` under `function take(a)`, so the positive arm genuinely narrows; swap the arms and `vl check` refuses with `operator '*' is not defined for i32 | "err" and i32` while the annotated twin prints `10`. The complement is `subtractTy(cur, tIdx)` and `subtractTy` answers -1 the moment its input is -1, which a hole parameter's declared type is; the struct-arm spelling prints the mechanism out loud as `expected A | {s: _}, got A | B` — the else arm's field read contributed a structural member to a UNIFIED hole instead of being subtracted from a declaration. Early-return guards, `!` and `&&` all lose it identically, an inferred LOCAL keeps it, and the `as i32` workaround is **check-clean invalid wasm** (ablated to a different mechanism — it refuses with the guard removed — so it is named in the grading list, not merged into the row). No DECISIONS entry says inferred parameters are not narrowed, and the directory already files two hole-parameter gaps: clause 2. **D1244 — a closure capturing a ref local declared in a MODULE-SCOPE block** is `emitProgram: field access receiver is not a struct`, and the reported headline was half right: it is not "a block", it is a block whose enclosing scope is the MODULE — the identical `if` body inside a function runs at every depth. At module scope `if` / `else` / `while` / `for` / bare all refuse; the capture is load-bearing (a parameter or a module-scope `p` runs), the annotation is not (both spellings refuse), and it is **every ref rep with two of them silent** — a captured `i32` runs, a struct field read is this loud refusal and a field write its assignment twin, while a captured `i32[]`, a captured `string` and a struct passed THROUGH the closure are check-clean invalid wasm, all three of which run when the same block is inside a function. **The harness cannot express D1244** — none of its twenty positions opens a module-scope block, so `closure_capture` grades that capability green while the row is live; a `block_*` position family is the fix and the row says so. Three probes ship with the rows (`run.py` 72 of 86 → **72 of 89**, all three GAP), two new matrix templates, and the second one found a further unfiled silent cell (`map_value`/un-annotated at the nullable spelling). No compiler change: this is the filing.
- **D1251 / D1252 / D1253, and the `block_*` position family that makes D1244's shape gradeable** — the three defects #2420's agent found and could not file, each minimised from scratch on the merged tree, plus the harness gap that row asked for by name. **Every one of the three ablated AWAY from the cell it was found in**, which is the entry's own argument for delta-debugging before filing. **D1251 — a numeric `as` cast on a HOLE parameter is lowered as the IDENTITY**: D1243 handed over `print((a as i32) * 2)` inside an `is` else arm; the arithmetic is scenery, the guard is scenery, and the witness is five lines with no `is` in it (`const u: i32 | null = 5` / `function take(a) { print(a as i32) }` / `take(u)`), `vl check` rc 0 and `type mismatch: expected i32, found (ref $type)`. The disassembly is one instruction — `(func $take (param $0 (ref $1)) (call $__print_i32__ (local.get $0)))` — because BOTH gates read the operand's arena type and a hole's is a `TyVar`: `checkCastNode`'s trio arm needs a `TyUnion` to subtract from, `isNumeric` answers true for a `TyVar` on purpose so an unresolved hole does not cascade, and the emitter's `asExprIsUnionCast` declines for the same reason, leaving the plain conversion ladder with nothing to name. The whole trio is affected and the FACES differ by suffix: at `as?`/`as!` the annotated twin prints `5` (a capability lost), at bare `as` it is a correct check reject naming the fix (so the hole face is `check` admitting what the design forbids). The cast is not always a no-op — a hole solved to a scalar emits `i32.trunc_f64_s` / `f64.convert_i32_s` — and that control is what identifies the union rep as the ingredient; a second, quieter face is `take(2.5)` + `as i32` PRINTING `2` at the hole where the annotated `f64` twin refuses, i.e. D1041's exact-or-fail ruling bypassed the same way. A hand position matrix confines it to the PARAMETER (a hole LOCAL is a loud check reject at both faces) and records the guard split: an `is null` early-return rescues the cast, an `is "err"` one does not. **D1252 — a REBIND of an already-narrowed nullable, re-tested with `is null`**, found at `map_value`/un-annotated and ablated away from the map AND from the hole parameter: four lines, `const u: i32 | null = 5` / `if u != null { const v = u; if v is null { print(0) } else { print(v) } }`, check-clean invalid wasm with `expected (ref null $type), found i32`. The checker KNOWS `v` is `i32` — `v != null` at the same site is a loud `cannot compare i32 with null` — and admits `v is null` anyway; the failing instruction is the COMPLEMENT ARM'S READ, not the test, proved by the no-read variant whose disassembly shows the rebind unboxed and the test already folded to `i32.const 0`, and by the annotated twin, whose `v` IS the box and whose else arm carries exactly the `struct.get`-behind-`ref.cast` the validator is complaining about. It is the four numeric value-niche reps and only those (`string`, a struct, `i32[]` and `boolean` all run), and the RESCUE is the annotation — inference is right about the type and the annotation is what agrees with the emitter, which is the reverse of the usual direction. **D1253 — a bare `{ … }` block is `emitProgram: unsupported statement in body` at EVERY scope**, noted in D1244 and now filed with its own witness: the parser mints a `Block` node on purpose ("A `{` at statement position is a BLOCK, UNLESS it shapes up as an object literal") and the checker gives it its own scope (its `const n` neither collides with an outer `n` nor escapes its own unused-variable warning), so two of three phases implement the construct and only `emitStmt` has no arm. Twelve spellings — function body, lambda body, module scope, nested, inside an `if`/`while`/`for`, empty, with a local, with a closure — one sentence; the only edit that changes the outcome is deleting the braces. Adjacent and separately loud: a bare block on the line after a CALL statement is a PARSE error instead (``expected an identifier but found `1` ``, pointing into the call's argument list), which a `;` or a `const` restores. **THE HARNESS GAINS SIX POSITIONS, 20 → 26**: `block_if`, `block_while` and `block_bare`, each with a `_capture` variant, delivering the value and its proof inside a MODULE-SCOPE block — the scope none of the original twenty opened, which is why `closure_capture` graded D1244's capability green while the row was live. D1244 now grades in three templates: `module-block-capture-struct` is the LOUD cell (`field access receiver is not a struct` at all three block kinds, both faces, with `block_if`/`block_while` RUNS as the control) and `-list` / `-string` put `block_if_capture` and `block_while_capture` into **SILENT**, four cells each — the two ref reps the row names. The family reaches the older templates too: all nine are now red at `block_bare` (18 of 18 cells, D1253's floor with no exceptions), and `orerr-generic-pin` gains four SILENT block cells, which flips that suite's exit-code assertion from 0 to non-zero — pinned by cell name in `tests/vl_capability_matrix_test.ts` rather than by the number, with `module-block-capture-struct` taking over as the exit-0 control. Capability probes **74 of 90 → 74 of 93**, the three new ones all GAP; filed witnesses **494 graded · 494 as filed · 0 MOVED · 0 not graded**. No compiler change: this is the filing and the instrument.
- **The self-compile spent 72% of its time in three whole-arena scans — memoised, ~6–8× faster, byte-identical** — a function-level guest profile (`VL_PROFILE_GUEST`, ranked by `scripts/profile-rank.py`; method in `docs/internals/profiling-the-compiler.md`) put `moduleHasUnionAs` at **29.8% self**, `moduleHasNumCast` at **29.4%** and `fieldClosureFeOfRecv` at **12.8%** of one self-compile — 40,532 samples, 72.0% of the run in three functions. The first two are MODULE-wide booleans — their own header says so, because a hand-walk that misses a node KIND under-reserves a scratch slot, which is invalid wasm and not a missed optimisation — and `emitFuncCode` asked each once per emitted FUNCTION, so the compiler (4,399 functions) scanned its whole arena 8,798 times to answer two questions whose answer cannot change; the worst case is a module with NO such node, because then every scan runs to the end, and that is the compiler's own source. Both now bank the answer on an arena PREFIX (`modUnionAsSeen`/`Hit`, `modNumCastSeen`/`Hit`), which is exact rather than merely fast: a pass that appends nodes after a call (the monomorphizer clones `AsExpr`s) is answered by scanning only the new tail, so every caller sees what an unmemoised scan would have seen at that moment. `emitProgram` clears all four — the LSP and the wasm test harness drive many programs through one instance, and a surviving `…Seen` would start the next program's scan inside a prefix belonging to nobody. The third was not a memo but a **missing gate**: every terminal in the `fieldClosureFeOf*` family is `fieldValueFeOf(objFieldVal(…))`, which resolves only a lambda field or a bare function-NAME field, and both flip `fnValUsed` — so with that flag clear the family cannot return anything but -1, and its hole-param arm was scanning the whole arena per member call to prove it (the same gate `capturedBindingOf` already carries). **Measured 2026-09-02, alternating A/B with both arms compiling master's own source so they see one box load** (the box was contended at 60–430 all day, so user time is the honest column): **real 112.1 / 64.5 / 56.7 s → 10.1 / 6.0 / 12.5 s**, **user 70.8 / 68.1 / 49.5 → 15.0 / 5.6 / 10.5**. On an idle box the equivalent pair was **116.7 s → 6.2 s** (99.9 → 5.7 user). The ratio held at 6–8× across all five master heads the branch was rebased onto, with byte identity re-proven at each. Profile samples 40,532 → 10,648 on one head, and on the merged tree no function is above **19.2%** self time — `__str_eq__`, which is the name-keyed registries' linear lookups (`variantIndexOf` 3.4%, `isUName` 2.8%, `__map_probe__` 2.1%, `declaredSlotOf` 1.0%): the registry-keying design track, not a hot spot. **Byte-identical output**: master's own compiler and this one emit the same bytes for the same input (an archived checkout of master's tree, master's arm seeded from a pre-change compiler so it never runs this branch's code), re-proven at every rebase; both fixpoints hold at L1 and L2 under `timeout 300`; `regress.py` `no cell changed class`. Guarded by `tests/vl_module_predicate_scan_test.ts` (1–4 s): two programs with the same statement count, one folded into 20× fewer functions — equal lowering work, so a per-function module scan is the only thing that can separate them, and startup, machine speed and box load all cancel. It measures 1.1× after and **10.0× before**, bar 2.5, validated against master's compiler as the control, which it reds on. `tests/vl_instance_state_leak_test.ts` gains a program that ARMS the new memo, so a missing clear surfaces in its NONE family. (`compiler/emit_classify.vl`, `compiler/emit_state.vl`, `compiler/emit_sections.vl`, `scripts/profile-rank.py`)

- **The state-leak harness — the instrument two real defects slipped past in one week** — `tests/vl_instance_state_leak_test.ts` drives ~30 curated programs through ONE `WebAssembly.Instance` in three orders (listed, reversed, and a MINTING SANDWICH that puts every minter immediately before every non-minter) and requires each emitted module to be byte-identical to a fresh-instance oracle. `vl` compiles once per process, so the CLI, the corpus sweep and every native suite are blind to this class **at any corpus size**; the two drivers that are not blind — `cases_wasm_test.ts` and the LSP server — surface it as a scatter of unrelated failures, which is how D986 (`ba8Used` & siblings, a V8-only invalid module) cost a bisect and D1003 (stale `ufcsAlias` rows) reached the editor. The oracle is proven by a real `WebAssembly.instantiate` + start-function run per program, so byte-identity is what licenses skipping the instantiate per sequence; every emission is also `WebAssembly.validate`d so a leak that produces invalid wasm is NAMED as that. **It found two live leaks on its first run, both invisible to the listed and reversed orders** — D1006/D1007, `startFnDetectScratch` writing 20 of the 24 `fnUses*` frame flags, with the missing two each carrying a DUPLICATED `= false` in `emitFuncCode` where the second copy was meant for the other builder. Measured: 23 of 1,922 gradeable corpus programs shift a following `print(1)`. Both are pinned as failing-shaped rows that red when fixed rather than reddening the tree today. Sabotage-validated by reverting #2218's four resets: 29/32, 20/32 and 159/162 compiles diverge, each report naming the first divergent compile and its predecessor, and the LSP `compile()` surface reddens too. 353 ms, seven tests. The module-scope-state audit it is the instrument for — 445 emitter mutables, 141 cleared in `emitProgram`'s prologue, 142 by a pass, 80 nowhere — is `docs/internals/emitter-module-state.md`, re-derivable with `scripts/emitter-state-audit.py` so it cannot go stale in the direction that ships bugs.

- **Destringify types — the programme is CLOSED** — the terminal condition was *"no structural decision is made by comparing rendered names"*, and the programme's own published standing check (`docs/internals/destringify-types-program.md` § "How to verify") passes: the render-comparison grep returns 7 hits, **all of them comments** describing what was replaced, and the name-keyed-table grep returns 11, every one a permitted nominal `table[i] == name` lookup. Zero measured disagreements across all three routes a rendered name could reach a decision by — banked on a node by canon, banked in a checker column, or used as an interner key (that third one never existed; the keys were always interned i32 ids). The spelling-PARSE axis is down **87%** (`splitUnionAtoms` 126,675 → ~17,000 calls, 180,866 → ~32,000 atom allocations) across ~300 logged slices, with no answer changing on any corpus file. **What still renders does so for three deliberate reasons**, each refused with a mechanism rather than left as debt: interner keys (a key is an identity token), nominal identity (the name IS the answer — refused six times), and boundary resolution (a source lexeme must become a type). The one forward question it leaves is a design change, not a conversion: the emitter's registries are keyed on the canon-softened spelling because that is the REP, not the type. **ROADMAP's "#1 priority — destringify" headline outlived the work by ~30 slices** and was demoted the same day the check was re-run — the inventory is never the file the fixer edits.
