A whole-module byte snapshot only pins two properties, both already covered more strongly upstream: **determinism** — the native fixpoint (`native-fixpoint.sh`, stage3 == stage4 byte-identical) proves byte-exact self-reproduction on the 660 KB compiler, a far larger surface than 14 tiny programs; and **correctness** — the functional corpus (`cases_wasm` + the `selfhost_native_*` suites) compiles AND runs the programs and checks behavior, where a byte-snapshot only flags that bytes *changed*, never whether the change was good. (This mirrors real compilers: self-hosting toolchains verify determinism by build-twice-and-compare / bootstrap stage comparison — rustc, Go, GCC, reproducible-builds — not committed binary goldens; where they snapshot codegen at all it's *textual + pattern-based* — LLVM FileCheck, Rust `codegen`/`assembly` tests, Go `asmcheck` — asserting specific properties, not whole-module byte-identity.) This was also the last byte-pin among the TS-era redundant test harnesses (the TS-vs-VL parity suites — `checker-parity-sweep`, `selfhost_emit_*`, `cases_test`, `cli_*` — were already removed across the kill-TS PRs). (`tests/golden/`, `tests/selfhost/`, `scripts/native-golden-check.ts`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`)

- **compile-time perf: the declaration-fill done-set is O(1), not a scan** — `fillDone` walked `cFillDoneIx` (a list of the arena entries already filled) once per type declaration while the list grew once per type declaration, i.e. O(#typedecls²) across pass 0b. It is now a FLAG COLUMN indexed BY the arena index (`cFillDoneAt`), which is available because `addTy` appends without interning, so a placeholder's index is dense and unique. Measured on N `type S = { a: i32 }` declarations with process startup subtracted per compiler and the `vl check` pump collector pinned to `null` (`VL_PUMP_GC=null`) so GC scheduling cannot alias the curve: analysis time goes 29/76/235 ms → 18/35/73 ms at N = 4000/8000/16000, i.e. delta ratios 2.6 and 3.1 (a linear term plus a quadratic one) collapse to 1.9 and 2.1 (pure linear). **The KEY is unchanged** — arena index, never name and never declaration statement — which is what keeps a redeclared type name filling its one shared placeholder exactly once and keeps the fill order-independent. Three structures were built and timed against each other — the flag column, a name-keyed `Map`, and an arena-index-keyed `Map` — plus a statement-keyed flag column; at N = 16000 all four are indistinguishable (72–74 ms median of 21 interleaved reps, mins 75–76), so nothing was traded for the exact key. The statement-keyed one is the one that would have been chosen for looking natural, and it is UNSOUND: two statements fill the one shared placeholder twice and merge the two bodies, so a field neither declaration wrote type-checks and the emitter then dies on it. No corpus file declared a type name twice, so all 1962 emitted modules were byte-identical under that wrong key; `tests/cases/types/redeclared-type-fills-one-placeholder-once.vl` is the file that catches it. The compiler's own 67 type declarations cannot exercise this (`vl check compiler/entry.vl` is unchanged), which is why the stress input is constructed. (`compiler/typecheck.vl`)

## Parser (Track G — complete)

- **A leading `.` / `?.` on a new line CONTINUES the postfix chain, and `vl fmt` lays chains out fit-or-break** — owner ruling, 2026-09-02 (DECISIONS.md §"A leading `.` on a new line continues the chain"): *"for long chains, allowing the `.` on the next line is basically required or we have to deal with long lines."* Parser: `parsePostfix`'s loop gains a NEWLINE arm that LOOKS past the run of newlines and continues iff the next kind is `DOT` / `QUESTION_DOT`, leaving them untouched otherwise — look-before-consume, because a line starting with `(` is a legal parenthesised statement and one starting with `[` a legal array literal, and eating the newline before either would silently glue two statements into a call or an index. NEWLINE only, not `skipNewlines`: a `;` ends the statement outright. **The rule reinterprets only programs that are parse errors today** — grepped rather than asserted, **0 of 10,355 `.vl` files in the tree begin a line with `.` or `?.`**, and `.5` is already a DOT parse error in the lexer's NUMBER arm — so no existing program changes meaning. Trailing-dot (`expect(x).` ⏎ `toEqual(y)`) stays refused (one form only, pinned as an error fixture); comment lines between links are free, since the lexer keeps `//` as trivia and never puts it in `P.toks`. **The formatter was the real half**: `format.vl` printed chains inline, so `fmt --check` would have re-joined every broken chain and made the form unusable in a tree `lint-self.sh` gates. It now lays a chain out fit-or-break against the same `fmtWidth` `wrapList` uses — inline while it fits, else one `.link(args)` per line at one extra indent from the FIRST link — with `callExpr`'s argument-list tail split out as `callTail` so the chain serves its links through the SAME width test and trailing-lambda hug rather than a second spelling of them. **The threshold is two links, and a link starts at the first step CARRYING A CALL**: a leading plain `.field` merges into the head, which is what keeps the rule off this compiler's dominant shape — `P.toks.push({ … })` keeps `wrapList`'s answer instead of shattering into `P` / `.toks` / `.push({ … })`, and a call-less path like `node.callArgNames.length` never breaks at all. Without that merge the one shape reformatted `driver.vl`, `lint-harness.vl` and a corpus case, at every width, for the worse — the overflow is in the ARGUMENT, and the argument list already knew how to wrap it. **The fit is measured FLAT** (interior lists forbidden to wrap first), because `wrapList` runs before the chain is ever consulted and would otherwise absorb every overflow; a flat form that fits is what the ordinary path produced anyway, so a fitting chain costs one render and prints byte for byte as before. The discarded measurement is gated on no comment lying in the chain's span, the same guard and the same reason as the one-line `if` collapse (`cmtCursor` is one-way). **Cost measured as a same-tree A/B over two seeds, not asserted**: of **10,355 `.vl` files** formatted under the master compiler and under this one, **exactly one pre-existing file's output changed** — `tests/cases/arrays/map-struct-to-struct.vl`, a 92-column three-link chain the new rule breaks — and **zero under `compiler/`, `std/` or `scripts/`**, the fmt-gated half. Three files changed rc 2 → 0: the new fixtures, which is the feature. New corpus cases `parser/leading-dot-continues-chain.vl` (2, 3 and blank-line-separated links), `leading-dot-optional-link.vl`, `leading-dot-comment-between-links.vl`, `newline-paren-bracket-start-statements.vl` (the interleaved logs are what distinguish two statements from one glued call/index), `trailing-dot-still-parse-error.vl`; two `tests/vl_fmt_test.ts` pins — fit/break/idempotence with the broken form RE-RUN through `vl run` (fmt returns unparseable input verbatim, so idempotency alone would pass on a spelling the parser rejects), and the head-merge threshold. LSP untouched — no new token kinds. (#2382)

- **ONE interpolation syntax, `\{expr}`, in BOTH quoted forms — plain strings gained holes and backtick templates MIGRATED theirs off `${`** — owner ruling, 2026-09-01 ("OK do `\{`"). `"v=\{x} done"` now interpolates, `` `v=\{x} done` `` still does, and the two are the SAME construct: same desugar, same absolute binding to `std:fmt`, same hole domain, same refusal, same nesting rules. **The trigger lives in the ESCAPE namespace, and that is what makes it free.** `"a\{b"` was a hard `Unknown escape sequence` parse error before this (measured), so no string's meaning could change, and `{` stays ORDINARY DATA in every string forever — the permanent tax a `{`- or `${`-triggered interpolator would have levied on every JSON, wasm-text and format literal not yet written. Swift's `\(` is the precedent; the spelling is the owner's. Measured on the tree it landed against: **119 of 32,071** double-quoted VL string literals carry a literal `{` (10,312 `.vl` files) — smaller than the 4,821 the proposal carried, which reproduces under no population constructible here (189 with `{` or `}`; 121 `{` occurrences; 996 across `.vl`+`.ts`+`.rs`+`.md`+`.json`), and recorded because a citation is a measurement with a date on it. **The template migration was one mechanical pass**: templates were SIX DAYS old (#2188) and the only `${` users in the tree were their own eleven fixtures, so `${` is ordinary text now and `\$` is retired — with a targeted sentence (``\$` is not an escape — write `$` (an interpolation hole is `\{…}`)`) because that one becomes an error either way, and NO hint for `${`, because that one becomes a legal program and a diagnostic for a legal program would be speculative (measured: zero `${` remain). **ONE SCANNER, one escape decoder.** `scanQuoted` gains a single `holes` predicate (`"` and `` ` ``, never `'` — a char literal could not hold a hole) with the `\{` test in FRONT of the escape arm, so `\\{` is an escaped backslash before an ordinary brace; the `"` call site gains the split-run arm the backtick site already had; a fourth stack (`gTplQuote`) records each open run's delimiter so the `}` arm resumes in the mode the run opened in and an unterminated run names the literal the AUTHOR opened (`Unterminated string literal`, not `template`). A holed string mints the same `TEMPLATE_HEAD`/`MID`/`TAIL` kinds, so **nothing past the lexer learned a second literal form exists** — parser desugar, `binTpl` verbatim reprint, `checkCallNode`'s type-directed half, semantic-token class 5, all untouched code serving twice the surface. **Proved by byte identity**: `print("v=\{x}")`, `` print(`v=\{x}`) `` and `import { toString } from "std:fmt"` + `print("v=" + x.toString())` are all **17,089 bytes, one sha**. Multiline stays backtick-only — a raw newline still ends a `"…"` string, the one rule the two grammars still disagree about — while a HOLE is expression context in both and may span lines. **The four-way module gate now scans BOTH literal forms** (`cliHasTplHole` + `has_template_hole` + `moduleGate.ts`): a plain-string hole needs `std:fmt` injected exactly as a template hole does, and a gate that answers `false` where the compiler answers `true` fails SILENTLY — `tests/module_gate_agreement_test.ts` grew anchors naming the `"` arm and the `holes` flag, and four new rows in the shared table (plain-string hole arms; `{plain}` does not; `\\{x}` does not; `` `${x}` `` no longer does). Editor: TextMate hole rules on BOTH string rules, placed AHEAD of the escape rule so `\{` is not eaten as an escape; `vlLex.ts` factors the hole state machine into one `scanHole` reached from both literal scanners — required, not cosmetic, since a `"` inside a hole would otherwise terminate the outer string and misread the rest of the document; signature help re-enters a hole in either form. Corpus movement **0 of 7,564 cells**; dual-run against a git-archive control over 2,577 pre-change programs moved **9**, every one of them a `${`-spelled template fixture (the migration) and none of them anything else. Six migrated fixtures, six new ones (`string-holes.vl`, `brace-stays-literal.vl`, `cross-form-nesting.vl`, `err-string-unterminated-hole.vl`, `err-string-hole-newline.vl`, `err-dollar-escape-retired.vl`), a fmt round-trip pin over both forms, and DECISIONS.md records the escape-namespace ruling and the naming deviations (`TEMPLATE_*` kinds and `cliHasTplHole` now undersell what they cover, deliberately).

- **A MISSING LIST SEPARATOR IS INSERTED, NEVER SKIPPED PAST — stage 2's first lossless-recovery conversion, and the first phantom pin retired (5 → 4)** — `f(1 2)` was never an arity bug. The parser had NO separator arm: an element-starting token simply ended the list and fell through to `expectClose`, whose bounded scan ran forward to the `)` and **deleted the `2`** — so the call re-parsed hole-free as `f(1)` and `wrong number of arguments: expected 2, got 1` was a count nobody had written. Skipping was the defect; the phantom was its symptom. A missing separator is now DIAGNOSED and INSERTED (``expected `,` but found `2```), the list keeps every element the user wrote, and the diagnostic is marked LOSSLESS — so the checker runs and the type error four lines down rides along. Four list sites are wired (`parseArgs`, `parseArrayLit`, `parseObjLit`, `parseParamList`), each gated on **its own** element-start test, because "another element" is a different set per list: an expression for a call / array literal (`startsExprTok` — `startsStmt` minus the statement keywords, plus `if`), a field key for an object literal, a parameter name for a parameter list. **`expectClose` itself is now two events rather than one**: a scan that consumed NOTHING inserted only the closer and IS lossless (`print(1` at end of line, a block whose `}` never arrives — all twenty call sites gain this without being touched); a scan that ate tokens on the way is not, and still gates. **`{` is deliberately NOT an element start** — after a complete element it is far more often a missing closer than a missing comma, and it is already `expectClose`'s own scan bound — so `[{x: 1} {x: 2}]` keeps the lossy skip and keeps the bail. **AND THE INSERT IS SAME-LINE ONLY**, which the first cut of this change got wrong and review caught: every list site skips NEWLINEs (a list may span lines), so an ungated insert read a missing CLOSER at end of line as a missing COMMA and swallowed the NEXT STATEMENT as an element — `const xs = [1, 2` / `print(xs.length)` invented ``xs` is used before it is assigned` and `list element expects a value, got void`, with `expectClose` then reaching EOF at zero skip and marking the whole thing LOSSLESS. That is the exact phantom class the pins exist to stop, reintroduced by the change that retired one of them. Guarded on the token stream (`skipNewlines` leaves its NEWLINE at `P.pos - 1`), all three shapes are now byte-for-byte master's single diagnostic, verified against a pristine master control. **The price**: a missing comma at a line end inside a MULTI-LINE list is not inserted either — a missing closer and a missing separator are indistinguishable there — so that spelling behaves exactly as master does; a capability not GAINED, not one lost. Four shapes pinned as `NEWLINE_GATED` against master's own output, each requiring a real type error after the mistake to be ABSENT, and validated against the unguarded build, which produces every forbidden message. Measured on the built candidate, one program per spelling with a REAL type error placed after the mistake so "no phantom" cannot be confused with "the checker never ran": `f(1 2)`, `f(1 2 3)`, `g(f(1 2), 3)`, `[1 2]`, `{x: 1 y: 2}` and `function f(a: i32 b: i32)` all report their separator diagnostic AND their type error and no phantom; `[{x: 1} {x: 2}]` is correctly still gated. **The strongest witness is the arity error that DOES fire**: `f(1 2 3)` against a two-parameter `f` reports `wrong number of arguments: expected 2, got 3` — the phantom's own message with the right number in it. `vl fmt` is unaffected and must stay so (the comma goes into the TREE, not the file): it keeps the ANY-diagnostic bail, refuses, and leaves the source byte-identical. **The LSP suite's lossy CONTROL had to move with the conversion** — it used `f(1 2)`, which would have left the test green with nothing left to control; it now uses the `[{x: 1} {x: 2}]` skip. Corpus: three fixtures re-worded (the message changed from the closer's to the separator's) plus new `parser/call-missing-comma-typechecks.vl`; distilled corpus **0 of 255,504 cells moved**, all eleven gates green. DECISIONS.md §"A missing list separator is inserted, never skipped past"; next stage-2 conversion is the `then`-removal arm in `parseIf`. (#2397)

- **A recovered parse is TYPECHECKED — "missing brace" and "type error four lines down" are reported TOGETHER** — owner ruling, 2026-09-01 ("seems straightforward"), stage 1 of the driver lossless-recovery flag. `checkSrc`/`checkSrcSym`/`compileSrc`/`lintSrc`/`lintGraph`/`modCompile` all returned at `P.diags.length > 0`, so ONE missing brace blanked every type and lint diagnostic in the file — worst in the LSP, which compiles per keystroke and therefore reads a file mid-edit most of the time. The gate now quantifies over the diagnostics rather than counting them: the checker runs **iff EVERY parse diagnostic in the file carries a LOSSLESS flag**. The flag is a SPARSE index-keyed column beside `P.diags` (`dgLossless`, `compiler/ast.vl`) — the same shape as the driver's `vcDg*` tokenless-diag table, reset from the same `vcDgReset` the seven pipeline entry points already call in lockstep, and sparse on purpose: a dense column would need pushing by every `P.diags.push` in the tree, and absent must mean "not known to be lossless" so a site that has never heard of the table gets the SAFE default. **Exactly one site sets it** — `parseBracedBody`'s unbraced-body arm (#2115/#2165), where `parseStmt` consumes the arm exactly as a braced body would have, so no token is dropped and none invented and a type error over that AST is real. `parseBlock`'s fall-through is not marked (`expectClose` skips to a closer, which drops tokens), and the `then`-removal arm is deliberately left unmarked as the cheapest stage-2 candidate. **EMIT never proceeds past a parse diagnostic**: a recovered program CHECKS, it does not BUILD — `vl build`/`vl run` keep rc 1, write no module, and print the same parse message with the newly-found type errors beside it. `formatSrc` keeps the ANY reading for its own reason: `fmt -w` writes back over the file, so printing a recovered AST would silently re-spell the mistake as the braced form and erase the diagnostic with it (pinned). **The ALL quantifier is what makes it safe by construction**, and the price of the ANY reading was re-measured rather than quoted: lifting the bail wholesale fails exactly FIVE corpus cases, each inventing a phantom type error over fiction the parser guessed at — `parser/call-missing-comma-recovers.vl` (`wrong number of arguments: expected 2, got 1`; `f(1 2)` re-parses hole-free to `f(1)`), `functions/trailing-comma-illegal.vl` (`expected 0, got 1`), `objects/error-equality-not-overloadable.vl` (`redeclared ==`/`!=`), `index/operator-unannotated-self.vl` (`cannot index non-array Box`), `parser/coalesce-logical-mix-error.vl` (`operator '&&' expects boolean operands`). All five are pinned in `tests/vl_lossless_recovery_test.ts` by the message that must NOT appear, and that suite was validated in BOTH directions — sabotage the gate to never block and two tests fail, sabotage it to always block and five fail. Stage 2 converts the lossy skip sites one at a time, each conversion deleting its pin deliberately. **Ordering needed no decision**: the driver stream is parse-then-type and `vl run`/`build` print it that way, while `vl check`'s report has stable-sorted every tier by `(line, col)` since long before this — the sink already merged three sources and now merges four. New: `tests/vl_lossless_recovery_test.ts` (8 CLI/`vl check` cases), `tests/lsp_lossless_recovery_wasm_test.ts` (5 through the editor's own `wasmChecker` surface — check, lint, hover, the lossy negative, and the column-reset regression, which is the ONLY test that catches a missing reset and does so with the real phantom; wired into ci.yml's editor step), corpus `parser/recovered-body-still-typechecks.vl` + `parser/lossy-parse-suppresses-typecheck.vl`. Distilled corpus: **0 of 7,564 cells moved** (the corpus is parse-clean, so the gate is unreachable from it); 349/349 filed witnesses as filed. DECISIONS.md §"A recovered parse IS typechecked" records the ruling and the stage-2 path. (#2210)

- **Backtick TEMPLATE literals — `` `v=${x} done` ``** — owner ruling, 2026-09-01 ("1 is a go"). ADDITIVE syntax: a backtick did not lex at all before (`Unexpected character '`'`), so no existing program's meaning can change, and the distilled corpus moved **0 of 7,564 cells**. Multiline as in JS (a raw newline is content); ``\` `` and `\$` join the string escape set, which is otherwise SHARED — one scanner (`scanQuoted` in template mode), one escape grammar, and a purely lexical part→`"…"` rewrite (`tplPartStrLex`) rather than a decode/re-encode round trip, so no second decoder exists to drift. Holes lex as ordinary tokens between `TEMPLATE_HEAD`/`MID`/`TAIL` parts; a `}` ends a hole only at that hole's own brace depth, so **templates NEST for free** and an object literal, a nested string, or a nested template inside a hole all just work. A newline INSIDE a hole at hole depth emits no NEWLINE (a hole is an expression), so a hole may span lines. **HOLES BIND ABSOLUTELY to `std:fmt`'s renderer, never by scope pickup** — a string literal's meaning must not depend on the file's imports (DECISIONS.md). The mechanism: the parser desugars to `"v=" + $tpl$render(x) + " done"` naming an identifier **no program can spell** (`$` is not an identifier character), `modScan` pushes a BARE `std:fmt` import edge — `impName`/`impLocal` both empty, the same row a bare `import "…"` makes — for any module holding a hole, and `modBuildRename` maps the unspellable local onto the merged `toStr$mN`. So `std:fmt` is fetched, ordered, parsed and merged by the machinery an author's own import uses, with **no user-visible binding**: `toStr` stays undeclared, a user-declared `toStr` is unaffected, and completion (which filters on the entry's imports) never offers it. **Proved by byte identity, not by reading**: `` print(`v=${x}`) `` compiles BYTE-IDENTICALLY to `import { toStr } from "std:fmt"` + `print("v=" + x.toStr())` (17,089 bytes, 59 functions); a hole-less template compiles byte-identically to the plain string (1,878 bytes, 7 functions — nothing injected); a module that ALREADY imports `toStr` and also interpolates is byte-identical to its hand-written twin, so the module merges exactly ONCE. **The hole domain is the RENDERER'S, read off its declared parameter — never spelled in the compiler**, and both the admission test and the refusal's own sentence come from it. `string` is delivered directly (the renderer does not take one); everything the renderer takes goes through it. That property paid immediately: the branch was written against `i32 | i64 | boolean`, serde Stage 0's `renderF64` widened the renderer mid-rebase, and `` `v=${1.5}` `` started printing `1.5` **with no template-side edit at all** — the fixture that pinned the f64 refusal flipped to pinning the widening (`hole-f64-rides-the-renderer.vl`). Anything else is a TEMPLATE-shaped refusal AT THE HOLE — ``a template hole is `string` or i32 | i64 | boolean | f64 — this one is P`` — rather than `argument 1: expected …` about a call the author never wrote; the type-directed half lives at the one line in `checkCallNode` where the hole's type first exists. `vl fmt` reprints the author's bytes verbatim (a `binTpl` faithful-surface marker on the root `+`, the `binCompound` shape) including a multiline one, and the `+`-chain flattener stops at a template so `"a" + `b${x}c` + "d"` survives. Editor: the four template kinds get lexical class 5 (string) — a template is not one token, so leaving it to TextMate would paint a hole's identifiers as string content — plus a TextMate `string.template.vital` rule whose holes re-enter `$self`, backtick auto-close/surround pairs, a Monarch rule, and `vlLex` scanning a template WHOLE so a hole's braces open no fold region. **Module mode is armed by a fourth textual gate** (`cliHasTplHole` + its Rust/TS twins): the host closes the module graph before any lexing, so a real comment-and-literal-skipping scan decides it — `contains("`")` would have moved 2,409 corpus files off the single-source path. **Measured cost, recorded rather than discovered**: the gate is token-level, so a template whose only holes are STRINGS still pulls `std:fmt`+`std:str` (17,120 vs 1,920 bytes — the f64 halves serde Stage 0 added to `std:fmt` are most of it, per that module's own dated header) even though the renderer is never CALLED (byte-identical to an import-and-never-call control). The fix is whole-program DCE, which `std/fmt.vl`'s own header already names for the identical symptom. Every template diagnostic carries a full SPAN, not a one-column caret (#2182's `diagSpan`): an unterminated template underlines its first line from the opening backtick — the honest span, since `diagSpan` is one column pair on one line and a template is the one literal that crosses lines — and `diagEndCol`'s token-derived end is clamped to the anchor token's first line for the same reason. New `tests/cases/templates/` (6 accepting + 5 error spellings), a fmt round-trip pin, an LSP semantic-token pin, an LSP check-path pin, two folding pins, and a template inside `tests/fixtures/vl-test/pass.test.vl`. DECISIONS.md records the absolute binding, the domain, and the nesting / backtick-in-hole rulings. (#2188)

- **Scientific-notation float literals — `1e3`, `1.5e-7`, `2E+10`** — serde design doc, Stage 0: VL's own float rendering has to be re-parseable, and `print(1e3)` was a PARSE error at the lexer (`expected `)` but found `e3``). The grammar is now `digits ('.' digits)? ([eE] [+-]? digits)?` with the `_` separator rule unchanged in both digit runs (`1_0e1_0`). **It is a SPELLING, not a new literal kind**: the same `NumLit` node, f64 by default, the same contextual-f32 grant — measured running in 17 positions (global, list element, argument, return, `f32` binding, struct field, map value, negation, comparison, inferred `const`, assignment, `as i32`, …) — and `vl fmt` keeps the author's bytes, `1.50` and `1.5E-7` alike. **The mantissa grammar did NOT widen** (measured on the pre-change compiler, then pinned as two fixtures): VL has no bare `.5` or `1.`, so `.5e3` is still a DOT parse error and `1.e3` is still member access `.e3`. **Values are correctly rounded.** The exponent scales the SAME exact bignum rational the plain spelling already built — `mant * 10^(exp - fracDigits)` as one num/den pair, rounded once — so there is no `mantissa * 10^exp` product in f64 to lose an ULP in; differentially checked against CPython's `strtod` on 396 random literals (396/396 exact) plus `1e23`, `8.98846567431158e307`, `2.2250738585072011e-308`, `5e-324` and `1.7976931348623157e308`, each pinned by its shortest-round-trip print. A magnitude past 10^±400 short-circuits to ±inf / ±0 rather than building a million-bit denominator, and the overflow PRESCREEN learned the exponent — without that `1e400` reported one integer digit, sailed past the `< 309` gate and reached the emitter's `emitFail` backstop instead of the checker's `float literal overflows f64`. Error spellings report AT the literal, not at the parser: `1e`, `1e+` and `1e_5` all give `float exponent has no digits after `e``. **One home for "is this lexeme a float?"** — `typecheck.hasDot` and `emit_base.numTextIsFloat` were two independent `.`-scans that would have had to learn `e`/`E` separately (a checker calling `1e3` an integer while the emitter calls it a float is check-clean invalid wasm by construction); both retire into `emit_bignum.numLexIsFloat`, the leaf both sides can reach. Distilled corpus: **0 of 7,564 cells moved**. (#2173)

- **`else` requires braces too — block or `if`, nothing else** — owner ruling, 2026-09-01: *"make brace on else required."* `else <stmt>` is removed, so `else print(2)`, `else x = 2` and the value-position `const x = if c { 1 } else 2` are parse diagnostics rather than sugar. This is the `then` removal's other half — after `then` went, every branch in the grammar took a brace block except this one, and the asymmetry actively misled: `if c print(1)` had just become a diagnostic while `else print(1)` on the next line of the same file stayed silent. The `else` arm now calls the same `parseBracedBody` the other three bodies use, so the change is one call site and no new machinery: exactly ONE diagnostic — `` an `else` body requires braces: `else { … }` ``, anchored on the offending statement's first token — and the parse continues with that statement taken as the arm. The `startsStmt` gate comes with it, which makes `else` behave IDENTICALLY to its `if` twin on every non-statement-start: `else }`, `else )` and an `else` at end of line give the same message, count and span shape as `if c }`, `if c )` and `if c` (measured pairwise; the last is a wording change on a path that already failed — `else` at end of line was never legal and used to read `expected an expression but found NEWLINE`). **`else if` is untouched** in statement and value position alike — a chain is an `if` in the else slot, not a body — and so is `else { a: 2 }`, which is a braced OBJECT LITERAL in value position and stays `looksLikeObject`'s question rather than the brace rule's. **Cost, measured rather than assumed:** the distilled corpus moved **0 of 7,564 cells**, and `compiler/`/`std/` write no unbraced `else` (nor could they — `lint-self.sh` runs `vl fmt --check` over both and fmt has always normalized the form to braced, which is why every formatted file in the tree was already compliant). But `tests/` is excluded from fmt-check by construction, and **six sites in five fixtures did write it** (`conditionals/tail-if-else-value.vl` ×2, `functions/recursion.vl`, `inference/hole-is-guard-alternative.vl`, `inference/hole-is-guard-return-join.vl`, `soundness/hole-is-guard-return-join-reject.vl`) plus an incidental `else 8` in `parser/then-removed.vl` — all migrated in place, line-count-preserving. A grep that reads only the fmt-checked half of the tree reports zero here and is wrong by six. fmt keeps no dead path: the unbraced arm was printed by `bareBodyInline`, the general one-statement-Block-inline helper that braced blocks reach too. New fixture `tests/cases/parser/else-body-braces-recovers.vl`; `unbraced-body-no-recovery.vl` gains the `else }` twin; `tests/vl_unbraced_body_recovery_test.ts` re-pinned from "stays legal" to the ruling. DECISIONS.md records the choice.

- **An unbraced `if` / `while` / `for` body is ONE diagnostic, and the parse continues** — a missing brace used to cascade: `expect("LBRACE")` diagnosed and left the cursor put, `parseBlock` then swallowed the rest of the file as the body, and its `expectClose` reported a phantom `expected `}` but found end of input` on a line the user never wrote (three diagnostics when the body held an `=`, whose `=` re-entered as an expression). `parseBracedBody` now takes the one statement as the arm — statement `if`, the `if` after an `else`, value-position `if`, `while` (labelled too), and both `for` forms — emitting one message that names the construct and shows the fix (`` an `if` body requires braces: `if cond { … }` ``), anchored on the offending statement's first token. The recovered arm is a synthesized one-statement Block, the shape the braced form produces, so nothing past the parser knows a body was recovered. Recovery is GATED on `startsStmt`: a closer or a truncated construct (`if c }`, `if c` at end of input) keeps the plain `expected `{`` — a body that was not written at all is not a brace mistake. `else` is untouched here (an unbraced branch there was still legal, not recovered — no diagnostic, and fmt braced it); the owner ruled on that the next day and it now rides this same substrate, see the entry above. Corpus: no cell changed class.

- **The `then` keyword is REMOVED** — never designed (host-parity sugar from #270, June 2026; the ported-from TS compiler is retired), zero organic uses in the tree, braces cover both of its positions, and `vl fmt` was the only producer of the form (it canonicalized if-EXPRESSIONS into `then`; a `then`-spelled statement chain even made fmt refuse its own output — fixed en route). fmt now renders if-expressions braced-inline; 47 files respelled line-count-preserving (161+/161−); old spelling gets a targeted refusal (`` `then` was removed — wrap the branch in braces ``) with recovery reporting every occurrence in one pass; `then` stays legal as an identifier. Corpus: no cell changed class. DECISIONS.md records the choice. (#2094)

- **A `>>` closing two nested generics banked its second `>`, and the next `|` / `&` / `[]` spent that credit on the ARGUMENT — so `Box<Box<i32>> | i32` was one type, not two arms** — the native lexer fuses `>>`/`>>>` into a single SHR/USHR token (the compiler's own sources are generics-free, so the shift reading is unambiguous there), which means one token has to close TWO generic levels: `expectTypeGt` consumes it and BANKS the extra `>`s as a credit the enclosing close drains. While a credit is outstanding the enclosing argument list is still OPEN and the only token that may follow is its close — but the argument is parsed by `parseTypeName`, whose union loop reads the raw next token, so the OUTER continuation was folded INTO the argument. Three continuation loops read it that way (`|` in `parseTypeName`, `&` in `parseTypeIsect`, `[]` in `parseTypeAtom`); the generic argument list's own `,` loop already consulted the credit, which is why a multi-ARGUMENT application never had this and a NESTED one always did. `atTypeCont` is that same test given one home, and all four sites now read it. **The mis-built types, from the diagnostics that printed them**: `Box<Box<i32>> | i32` → `Box<Box<i32>|i32>`, `Box<Box<i32>>[]` → `Box<Box<i32>[]>`, `Box<Box<i32>> & W` → `Box<{v:i32,w:i32}>` (absorbed, then simplified), `Box<Box<Box<i32>>> | i32` → `Box<Box<Box<i32>|i32>>` (the `|` lands at the INNERMOST level — the USHR banks two, so the credit is spent one rung deeper). **THE UNION-ARM POSITION WAS SILENT AND THE OTHER ELEVEN WERE LOUD, which is what made it look like two defects**: with both arms folded into one type there is no union at all, so the value took a plain-struct rep and `if u is Box<Box<i32>>` reached `monoStaticIsResult` and **CONST-FOLDED TO FALSE** for a value that IS a member of that arm — `vl check` rc 0, no diagnostic, wrong branch, confirmed as `i32.const 0` / `if` in the disassembly with no `{tag, value}` box anywhere in the module; and the assignment side accepted `const u: Box<Box<i32>> | i32 = { v: 5 }`, an `i32` where `Box<i32>` is demanded, because the FOLDED argument's union makes `v: 5` well typed. Every other position — array, intersection, nullable niche, param, return, struct field, generic argument — was a loud type error against the mis-built type. **Genericity was never the axis; the fused close token is.** Depth-1 `Box<i32> | i32` banks nothing and was always correct, and the named (`type Outer = { v: Inner }`) and inline (`{v: {v: i32}} | i32`) spellings of the same depth-2 shape were already rejecting the same literal — that non-union control (`const u: Box<Box<i32>> = { v: 5 }`, correctly rejected, no trailing `|` for the credit to leak into) is what discriminated. **The credit, not the token, is the discriminator**: `Box<Box<i32> | i32>` closed with a plain `>` banks nothing, so its `|` still extends the argument — two spellings, two trees, from the same continuation token, and that control is pinned. Measured over a 12-cell continuation grid (positions × continuations): **11 of 12 wrong before, 0 after** (the 12th, `type Id<T> = T`, is an unrelated identity-alias gap and is unmoved, though it now names its type correctly). Blast radius: **every corpus file that can bank a `>` credit is BYTE-IDENTICAL, 11/11** (the 15 `.vl` files under `tests/cases/` containing `>>`, less the 4 added here) — and no other `.vl` source in the tree can reach the changed predicate at all, since a credit requires a consumed SHR/USHR inside a generic argument list and the only `>>` in `std/`/`bench/` is an expression shift. Full suite **4203/4203, 0 failed, 7 ignored**; with the guard made inert, exactly the predicted **6 tests redden** (the 3 `>>`-carrying fixtures × the corpus-oracle and native-align suites) and nothing else moves. **A SECOND, INDEPENDENT ROOT is left standing and is now pinned rather than hidden behind this one**: a union variant carrying a STRUCT-TYPED field has no emitted read, so the depth-2 struct arm construct (✓), its `is` discrimination (✓) and a SCALAR sibling field read (✓) all work while `u.v` itself reports `emitProgram: field access receiver is not a struct`. Fixing the parser is what moves the generic spelling out of the silent column and into that loud one beside the named and inline spellings — the inert leg leaves that fixture green, which is the measurement that the two roots are separate. (`tests/cases/generics/nested-application-close-continuation.vl`, `nested-application-union-arm.vl`, `nested-application-union-arm-literal-reject.vl`, `tests/cases/unions/error-struct-typed-variant-field-read.vl`)
- **G Hand-written parser** — replaced antlr4 with hand-written TS lexer + recursive-descent/Pratt parser emitting the typed AST directly; antlr4/Gradle/generated dirs gone. → `DECISIONS.md`
- **G AST source spans** — `NodeSpans` + `spanOf` publicly exposed via `toAST`/`compile`; unblocks D4/D6/D7.
- **G Comment-carrying tokens** — comments retained with spans (flat `comments` list + per-token `leading`/`trailing` trivia) without entering the grammar stream; unblocks AST-driven formatter.
- **G8 Soft-newline statement boundaries** — newlines are never force-required; statements abut on one line. Fixed `return <expr>` followed by a same-line statement (`return 1 print(9)`): the trailing dead statement was mistaken for the block's implicit return value and spuriously checked against an annotated return type (`expected i32, got null`) — now `return 1` carries the value and the trailing statement is left for the next position (flagged by the unreachable-code lint). → `DECISIONS.md` (G8)

## Self-hosting & modules (Track H)

- **H0 Module system phase 1** — relative-path named `import { a, b as c } from "./util"` + `export` modifier on `function`/`let`/`const`/`type`; whole-program resolver walks import graph, detects cycles, type-checks across modules, merges into ONE wasm module with per-module name mangling. `compileProgram`/`checkProgram`. (#96; → `DECISIONS.md`, `docs/modules-design.md`)
- **H-reexport — `export { a, b as c } from "./mod"` (re-export with a STABLE bare ABI name)** — a module can now re-surface another module's exports under its own public names. The merge mangles every module's symbols to `name$mN` (so two modules can both export `foo`), but a library wasm — the compiler itself — needs *some* exports to stay bare and stable for its host (`compileSrc`, not `compileSrc$m7`). A re-export is the mechanism: it records BOTH an import (pull the symbol + the dependency edge, so the host fetches the module) AND a public-name alias; the emitter then adds an export-section entry mapping the **bare** public name to the merged (mangled) target function's index, so `export { compute, helper as helped } from "./dep"` yields callable bare `compute`/`helped` exports (the `as` alias honored). The re-exported names are also bound locally (the merge pulls them in), so the re-exporting module may use them too. Touches the parser (skip `export { … } from` like an import — no AST node), the module subsystem (`modScan` records the re-export, `modCompile` resolves each public name → its `$mN` target), the emitter's export section (the bare alias entries), and the host's two module-fetch gates (`vl build`/`run` in `main.rs`, `vl check`/`--fix` via cli.vl's `cliLineIsImport`) so a re-export arms the fetch loop. Native fixpoint byte-identical; this is the keystone enabling the compiler's own source to migrate from `cat`-concatenation to real `import`/`export` modules while keeping its host ABI stable. (`tests/cases/modules/reexport/`)
- **H-self-modules — the compiler builds from REAL `import`/`export` modules (no more `cat`/sed/rename)** — the self-host build flipped from concatenating the nine source files into one blob (stripping their `import` lines, sed-renaming the lexer's `Tok`/`Diag`/`advance` to dodge the flat-namespace clash) to a genuine module graph: `vl build compiler/entry.vl` resolves `entry → driver → {lexer, ast, parser, typecheck, wasmEmit, lint, format} + cli`. `compiler/entry.vl` re-exports the full host ABI (191 names — the embedding surface, the corpus harness, the LSP query families) under bare, stable names (H-reexport). The driver moved into `compiler/` (so its relative imports resolve) and became a real module importing the pipeline. Every cross-module reference is now an explicit `export`/`import` (targeted, not export-everything); two backward edges that the flat namespace had hidden were broken by relocating their definitions — the value-union NAME classifier (`isValueUnionName` + `splitUnionAtoms`/`unionMemberCount`/`valueAtomKind`) moved wasmEmit → typecheck (it is type-classification the checker needs too), and the re-export alias tables (`reExpName`/`reExpTarget`) moved driver → wasmEmit (the consumer). The formatter learned to preserve a re-export (`emitImports` recovers `export { … } from` verbatim, like an `import`). `refresh-compiler.sh`/`native-fixpoint.sh`/`lint-self.sh` lost their sed/cat/rename glue — they just build/check the entry. The lexer `Tok`/`Diag` clash simply evaporates (each module has its own namespace). The seed re-mints to the module-built bytes; the native fixpoint (`vl build entry` ⇒ stage3 == stage4) holds, the deno corpus (533) and native sweep (PASS=400) pass, and the bare ABI is verified complete. (`compiler/entry.vl`, `compiler/driver.vl`, the nine module files, `scripts/{refresh-compiler,native-fixpoint,lint-self}.sh`)
- **H-split-bignum — first cohesive carve-out of the 26K-line emitter** — now that real module boundaries exist (H-self-modules), `wasmEmit.vl` can shed self-contained clusters. The first: the arbitrary-precision integer math + numeric-literal helpers (`big*` — add/sub/cmp/shift/divmod over little-endian base-2^16 limbs — plus `mulAdd64`, `parseI32`/`parseI64Pair`, `numLexFitsI32`/`numLexIs2Pow31`) move to a new leaf `compiler/emit_bignum.vl`, with the one `gDivRemNonzero` side-channel global moving alongside them (the emitter imports it back). A genuine LEAF — it calls nothing in the emitter and touches no emitter state — so there is no import cycle; the emitter (and the few other modules that used these) import what they need. Behavior-identical: the seed re-mints to the new function ordering, the native fixpoint holds, the deno corpus (533) and native sweep (PASS=400) pass. The pattern (`emit_*.vl` cohesive leaves) is set for further carve-outs. (`compiler/emit_bignum.vl`, `compiler/wasmEmit.vl`)
- **H-split-emitter-vocab — carve the emitter's pure vocabulary + queries (131 functions) into two modules** — the big follow-on to H-split-bignum: every remaining PURE helper (state-free, calls only other pure helpers) leaves `wasmEmit.vl` for two new leaf modules, split along a verified-acyclic seam. `compiler/emit_base.vl` (85 fns) is the VOCABULARY — type-NAME analysis (`name*`/`ty*`/`ann*`/`ret*`/`nul*`), monomorphization name logic (`mono*`/`gae*`), and low-level string/byte/opcode helpers (which are mutually recursive with the type-name code, so they share one module); `compiler/emit_query.vl` (46 fns) is the QUERIES — binding/value-kind predicates (`param*`/`let*`/`is*`/`union*`) and control-flow / valued-return / arr-new scans (`if*`/`block*`/`expr*`/`nli*`), depending only on `emit_base`. The call graph was checked to confirm no `base → query` edge (so the layering `emit_bignum → emit_base → emit_query → wasmEmit` is a DAG, and the module system's cycle rejection is satisfied). Behavior-identical: the seed re-mints to the new ordering, native fixpoint holds, deno corpus (533) and native sweep (PASS=400) pass. **`wasmEmit.vl`: 25698 → 22836 lines** (≈26K → 22.8K across the two split PRs). (`compiler/emit_base.vl`, `compiler/emit_query.vl`, `compiler/wasmEmit.vl`)
- **H-split-emitter-state+bytes — factor the emitter's shared state, then its byte-emission layer** — the stateful core finally yields. First `compiler/emit_state.vl` collects the emitter's 191 shared MUTABLE globals (the output buffer `W`, the WasmGC type-index globals `cloStructIdx`/`aTypeIdx`/`sHeapIdx`/…, the collection tables `localIsRef`/`fnNames`/…, scratch bases, `fnUses*` flags) + the `Emitter` type into a declarations-only LEAF — the emitter and its sub-modules import these and mutate them in place (cross-module global writes work). That move is BYTE-IDENTICAL (globals emit in the same order regardless of file). With state externalized, the byte-emission layer becomes a clean DAG layer: `compiler/emit_bytes.vl` (68 fns) holds the streaming writers (`wU8`/`wULEB`/`wSLEB`/`wName`/`wSection`) and the `fb*` instruction/type encoders (`fbValtype`, `fbStructNew`, `fbCallRef`, …) plus `emitFail` and the map-type-index helpers — its downward call-closure (computed with string/comment-stripped edges, so `emitFail("emitProgram: …")` error text doesn't masquerade as a call) reaches NO lowering function, so `emit_state → emit_bytes → wasmEmit` is acyclic. Behavior-identical: native fixpoint holds, deno corpus (533) and native sweep (PASS=400) pass. **`wasmEmit.vl`: 22836 → 20953 lines** — ≈26K → ≈21K across the split arc, the emitter now layered `{emit_bignum, emit_base, emit_query} → emit_state → emit_bytes → wasmEmit` (the lowering). (`compiler/emit_state.vl`, `compiler/emit_bytes.vl`, `compiler/wasmEmit.vl`)
- **H-split-typecheck-lsp — carve the LSP query layer out of the type-checker** — applying the emitter-split pattern to the second-biggest file. The checker's read-only LSP QUERY layer (63 functions — symbol occurrences / go-to-def / find-refs / hover `sym*`, redundant-type reports `redun*`, inlay hints `inlay*`) moves to `compiler/check_query.vl`, and the LSP STATE it reads (38 symbol-occurrence / redun / inlay table globals) to a declarations-only leaf `compiler/check_state.vl`. The seam is verified acyclic via a TRANSITIVE reachability check: the 78-function LSP closure minus everything reachable from the checker core leaves exactly the read-only queries (the boundary functions the checker also calls — `symResolve`, `symOccHasTok`, `tyToStr` — correctly stay). The checker's `Ty`/`Checker` type system and the two `Checker`-typed globals (`T`, `cUserTypes`) STAY in typecheck (moving them would drag the whole type-algebra across the boundary); `check_query` imports them. So `check_state → typecheck → check_query` is a DAG. Behavior-identical: native fixpoint holds, deno corpus (533) and native sweep (PASS=400) pass. **`typecheck.vl`: 8100 → 7496 lines.** (`compiler/check_state.vl`, `compiler/check_query.vl`, `compiler/typecheck.vl`)
- **H-split-format — split the pure helpers out of `format.vl`** — 30 state-free formatting helpers (whitespace/indent/line-splitting, comment + chain/precedence predicates, `normalizeProgram`/`joinLines`/…) move to a new leaf `compiler/fmt_util.vl`. Their call-closure touches no `format.vl` module-state global (only the parser arena `P` + AST node variants from `./ast`), so it is a clean leaf the formatter imports; no other module imported the moved helpers, and the host ABI (`formatSrc`/`fmtLen`/`fmtByteAt` via the driver) is untouched. Behavior-identical: native fixpoint holds, deno corpus (533) and native sweep (PASS=400) pass. **`format.vl`: 1954 → 1553 lines.** (`compiler/fmt_util.vl`, `compiler/format.vl`)
- **H-split-cli — split the pure helpers out of `cli.vl`** — 21 state-free CLI helpers (ANSI colouring, detab / visual-width, line splitting, severity rank/validation, `--exclude` glob matching, import-line detection) move to a new leaf `compiler/cli_util.vl`. State-free (no `cli.vl` module global — they call only `ast`'s `i32ToStr` + a few driver helpers), a clean leaf the CLI imports; the host ABI (`cliArgReset`/`cliNext`/… via `entry.vl`) is untouched. Behavior-identical: native fixpoint holds, deno corpus (533) and native sweep (PASS=400) pass. **`cli.vl`: 1195 → 957 lines.** (`compiler/cli_util.vl`, `compiler/cli.vl`)
- **H-M1 Distribute via `deno compile`** — same as C5.
- **H1 Parser self-hostable** — same as Track G above.
- **H2 gap-1 Push non-nullable struct array** — `Tok[]` works; backing slot nullable-widened to `(ref null $T)`; reads `ref.as_non_null` to surface non-null type. Unblocks AST-node lists.
- **H2 gap-2 Module-level mutable `let` through a function** — scalar top-level bindings lower to shared wasm `global` (`global.get`/`global.set`). (`tests/cases/globals/`)
- **H2 gap-3 String escapes** — `\n`/`\t`/`\xXX`/`\uXXXX`/… decoded in lexer.
- **H2 gap-4 `toString` prototype-chain leak fix** — scope lookup uses `Object.hasOwn` everywhere (closes `constructor`/`valueOf`/etc. hazards).
- **H2 gap-5 `fromCodePoint(code): string` builtin** — code-point-named; replaces JS-ism `fromCharCode`.
- **H2 gap-6 Ref/string module-globals through a function** — extends gap-2's scalar-only support to ref/string cells.
- **H2 gap-7 One-char string literal `.length`** — string literals soften to nominal `string`; no longer mis-types as a char.
- **H2 char literals + `toString`/stringify** — both landed as part of H2 gap work.
- **H3-gap3 `checkProgram` in value position** — resolved by #89 (void/statement-position value drop); a discarded value is dropped in statement position, so `checkProgram(...)` as a bare statement (or `let r = ...`) no longer hits "Expected numeric type" in codegen. (detail: `docs/selfhost-gaps.md` §3)
- **H4.2 Value-level bitwise/shift operators** — shipped in #99 (see B2 above).
- **H4.3 Unsigned right-shift** (`>>>`) — resolved by #99 (`>>>` is now a native operator); `ulebToArr` in `wasmEmit.vl` uses `v >>> 7` for all i32 values including those with bit 31 set. (detail: `docs/selfhost-gaps.md` §H4.3)
- **H4.4 Signed `%` sign fix** — resolved via H4.2 (#99): `& 0x7f` / `& 0xff` bitwise masks replace the arithmetic correction branches; naturally unsigned, no special-casing needed. (detail: `docs/selfhost-gaps.md` §H4.4)
- **H-pipeline VL-in-VL front end end-to-end** — `lexer.vl → parser.vl → typecheck.vl` chain driving source text through a wired pipeline; proves the front end self-hosts. (`tests/selfhost_pipeline_test.ts` + `tests/selfhost/pipeline_harness.vl`)
- **H-emitProgram structs** — `emitProgram` parses + emits WasmGC struct types, `struct.new`, and `struct.get`; construct + field-read proven by real `WebAssembly.instantiate`. (#137)
- **H-emitProgram arrays** — `emitProgram` parses + emits WasmGC array ops: literal (`array.new_fixed`), index read/set, `.length`; 8 new live-instantiation cases. (#145)
- **H-emitProgram strings** — `emitProgram` lowers string literals + `.length`/`s[i]` to the array-i32 code-point representation (a VL string is CURRENTLY an `array i32` of code points, reusing the arrays slice's `(array (mut i32))` machinery); string-typed locals/params/returns carry the array ref valtype; 7 live-instantiation cases. Concat (`+`), value-equality (`==`/`!=`), and `.slice` land in G6; the UTF-8 `array i8` storage migration (B7) is deferred.
- **H-emitProgram growable arrays / push** — `emitProgram` now lowers `i32[]` to the growable `{ backing, len, cap }` wrapper struct (mirroring `toWasm.ts`'s list rep): `[…]` literals build it, `.push(x)` grows the backing in place (2× / floor 4) when full via `array.new_default` + `array.copy` + `struct.set` then writes + bumps `len`, `.length` reads the `len` field, and `a[i]`/`a[i]=v` go through the backing. `string` stays the raw fixed `(array (mut i32))` rep (immutable, no push). 6 new live-instantiation cases (grow past initial capacity, `while`-loop build-then-sum, `[]`+push+`.length`, push→set→read, list across a function boundary).
- **H-exports Host-callable wasm exports** — entry-module `export function`s become host-callable wasm exports via a thin scalar no-env wrapper; non-entry exports remain DCE-able. (#141; → `DECISIONS.md`)
- **H-emitProgram unions + is** — `emitProgram` now lowers discriminated `type N = A | B | …` struct unions with `is`-narrowing (G1, the bootstrap keystone), mirroring `toWasm.ts`'s boxed tagged-struct rep (`docs/unions.md`): a union value is a `{ tag: i32, value: anyref }` box wrapping the variant payload struct; construction is `struct.new $box (i32.const tagOf(V)) (struct.new $V …)` with global tags assigned by sorted variant structural signature; `n is V` is the box-tag compare (`struct.get $box 0` then `i32.eq`); a narrowed field read `n.f` (inside `if n is V`) recovers + `ref.cast`s the payload then `struct.get`s the field. The type section lifts the one-struct cap (multiple variant struct heap types + the union box). `compiler/parser.vl`/`compiler/ast.vl` gained the union-alias decl + `x is T` guard (the self-host parser parsed neither before). 7 new live-instantiation cases (construct+narrow+read, false-`is` other branch, 2-variant dispatch, 3-variant dispatch, multi-field variant, union local→helper, union local discriminated in place). Deferred: arrays-of-unions (`Node[]`, the G7-ref follow-up), unions mixing scalars + structs, and `!is`/negated guards.
- **H-emitProgram ref-element lists / arrays-of-structs-and-unions (G7-ref)** — `emitProgram` now lowers growable lists whose ELEMENT is a reference — `Tok[]` (a struct ref) and `Node[]` (the union box ref), the self-host parser's `P.nodes: Node[]` arena + token stream shapes. The `{ backing, len, cap }` wrapper is reused, but the backing array slot is `(ref null $elem)` (`0x5e 0x63 <elem> 0x01` — nullable-WIDENED so `array.new_default` defaults spare slots to null; verified against `toWasm.ts`'s `arraySlotWasmType`/`arrayReadCast`); an index READ `array.get`s the slot then `ref.as_non_null` (`0xd4`) recovers the non-null element (reads in `[0,len)` are always populated). `.push`/index-set reuse the i32-list grow/store sequence over the ref list/backing type indices + a ref scratch triple. For a union-element list `ns[i]` yields the union box, usable with `is`-narrowing (`let n0 = ns[i]; if n0 is A { n0.av }`). One ref-element list per program (struct OR union element), alongside the existing i32 list. 6 new live-instantiation cases (struct push+index-a-field+length, `while`-loop build-then-sum, `T[]` literal, struct index-set, union push+index+`is`-narrow, a `Node[]`-shaped mini arena narrowing each element). No `parser.vl`/`ast.vl` change needed (`S[]`/`N[]` already parse to a `TypeRef` with the `[]` suffix).
- **H-emitProgram logical `&&`/`||`/`!` + value-typed `if` (G4)** — `emitProgram` now lowers the short-circuit logical operators, introducing the first VALUE-TYPED `if` (the existing statement `if` stays VOID, blocktype `0x40`). `&&`/`||` are EXPRESSIONS that yield an i32, so they emit an `if` with an i32 RESULT-TYPE blocktype (`0x04 0x7f`) where both arms leave one i32: `a && b` ≡ `if (a) { b } else { 0 }` (then = `b`, `else 0x05`, else = `i32.const 0`, `end 0x0b`); `a || b` ≡ `if (a) { 1 } else { b }` — mirroring `toWasm.ts`'s `m.if(left, right, i32.const 0)` / `m.if(left, i32.const 1, right)` so the RHS is genuinely SKIPPED when short-circuited. `!a` (logical not) is `i32.eqz` (`0x45`) — a `boolean` rides in an i32, so eqz maps 0→1 / non-zero→0, exactly `a == 0`. 8 new live-instantiation cases (`&&` + `||` truth tables, `!a`, `&&`/`||` short-circuit OBSERVED via a global a skipped helper would have written — confirmed untouched, then written when run, on one shared instance, a char-class predicate `(x > 0) && (x < 10)` driving a branch, and a combined `!(a && b) || c`). The value-typed `if` is reusable for any future value-position `if`. No `parser.vl`/`ast.vl` change needed (`&&`/`||` already parse via the precedence table, `!` via `parseUnary`).
- **H-emitProgram boolean params/locals/returns + BoolLit/CharLit (G3)** — `emitProgram` now accepts `boolean` as a valid scalar wherever i32 is (boolean param in `checkParams`, boolean local in `checkLocalI32`, boolean return via `emitExpr`), treating it as the SAME i32 wasm valtype (`0x7f`) since a `boolean` already rides in an i32 (0/1) — no separate boolean valtype is introduced (`vtKindOfType`/`vtKindOfParam` already fall through to i32). `BoolLit` lowers to `i32.const 1` (true) / `i32.const 0` (false) from the already-decoded `boolVal`; `CharLit` lowers to `i32.const <code point>`, decoding `charText` the SAME way string literals decode (`decodeStr` strips the quotes + resolves escapes, yielding exactly one code point). Comparisons/branches on booleans already worked via i32. This unblocks the ~40+ self-host predicates that return `boolean`. 7 new live-instantiation cases (boolean param returned true→1/false→0, `if true`/`if false` BoolLit conditions, a function returning `boolean` (a comparison) used in a branch, a boolean local driving an `if`, `'a'`→97, and a char local + arithmetic `'A' + 1`→66). f64 stays out of scope. No `parser.vl`/`ast.vl` change needed (`boolean`, `true`/`false`, and char literals already parse).
- **H-emitProgram struct field write + module globals (G2)** — `emitProgram` now lowers struct field WRITES (`s.field = v` → `struct.set $0 <fieldidx>`, `0xfb 0x05`, struct-ref-then-value operand order, reusing the `emitPush` field-store shape) and module-level mutable GLOBALS: top-level `let`/`const` lower to a wasm global section (id 6, `<valtype> 0x01 <constexpr-init> 0x0b`) collected by `collectFns` in declaration order, with bare-identifier reads/writes routed to `global.get`/`global.set` (`0x23`/`0x24`) when the name resolves to a global rather than a local. Globals init via constant expressions only — i32 (`i32.const`), string (`array.new_fixed`), struct (`struct.new`), and `i32[]` (`struct.new` of `array.new_fixed`) literals — so no start function is needed (the `__program__` start-fn fallback for non-constexpr initializers is deferred). A bare top-level call statement (helper invoked for its global side effect) now emits the call + `drop`. 9 new live-instantiation cases (field write-then-read, both fields, read-modify-write, field mutated in a `while` loop, i32 global read+written, a counter bumped by a helper across calls, two globals one seeded non-zero, a struct global field-mutated, an array global indexed + `.length`).
- **H-emitProgram string `+`/`==`/slice (G6)** — `emitProgram` now lowers the three string operators the self-host sources lean on (diagnostics build messages with `+`, the lexer keyword tables compare with `==`, lexeme extraction uses `gSrc.slice(start, end)`). A string is the SAME `(array (mut i32))` of code points, so all three lower INLINE (no helper functions, unlike `toWasm.ts`'s `__string_eq__`/`__string_slice__`): `a + b` allocates a new array of `len(a)+len(b)` (`array.new_default`, `0xfb 0x07`) and `array.copy`s (`0xfb 0x11`) a into `[0,lenA)` and b into `[lenA, lenA+lenB)`; `a == b`/`a != b` are ELEMENT-WISE VALUE-equality (a value-typed `block`/`loop`: `false` on a length mismatch, else a per-code-point compare loop, all-equal → 1; `!=` adds `i32.eqz`) — a correctness FIX, since the prior i32 `==` path would have emitted `i32.eq` = WRONG ref-identity for strings; `s.slice(start, end)` clamps each bound JS-style (negative-from-end then `[0,len]`, via `select` `0x1b`) and `array.copy`s the half-open range into a fresh array. Only STRING-typed operands take these paths (via the existing `exprString` tracking) — i32/other-type `+`/`==`/`!=` are unchanged. A shared per-function scratch frame (3 string refs + 4 i32 temps, reserved after the push triples when `fnHasStrOp`) stashes operands so a NESTED string op completes before any scratch write; `exprString` now also recognizes string concat + `.slice` as string-producing (so `let s = a + b` / `let s = x.slice(…)` get the string ref valtype). 14 new live-instantiation cases (concat `.length` + index checks, concat of two locals, `==` same/different-content/different-length, value-equality of two BUILT-UP strings (not ref identity), `!=`, `.slice` compared with `==` + length/index + out-of-range clamp, keyword-table `if word == "let"` dispatch hit + miss, concat built in a `while` loop). `.indexOf`/`.includes`/`.charCodeAt`/`fromCodePoint` and the UTF-8 `array i8` storage migration (B7) stay deferred. No `parser.vl`/`ast.vl` change needed (`+`/`==`/`!=` parse via the precedence table, `.slice(…)` as a member-call).
- **H-emitProgram string-keyed maps via parallel lists (G8)** — `emitProgram` now lowers `{[string]: i32}` maps — the shape the self-host checker (`typecheck.vl`) uses for its scope chain (`Map()`, `m[k] = v`, `m.has(k)`, `m[k] ?? -1`). DELIBERATELY the SIMPLEST correct rep, NOT `toWasm.ts`'s open-addressing hash map: a map is two PARALLEL growable lists + LINEAR SCAN — a 2-field struct `{ keys: (ref $keysList), vals: (ref $i32List) }` reusing the G6/G7 `{backing,len,cap}` wrapper twice (a string-ref keys list over `(array (mut (ref null $strArr)))`, and the existing i32 vals list), with NO hashing/probing/new wasm primitives. `Map()` builds two empty lists boxed into the struct; `m[k]=v` scans `keys` via element-wise string `==` (the just-merged G6 compare) and overwrites `vals[i]` on a hit else `keys.push(k); vals.push(v)`; `m[k] ?? d` is a FUSED scan-then-`vals[i]`-or-`d`; `m.has(k)`/`k in m` scans → 1/0. The map struct grows to 5 fields `{ keys, vals, index, count, size }`: `keys`/`vals` remain the insertion-ordered entry lists (so order is preserved and the G6/G7 grow machinery is reused for append), `index` is a raw i32 array of hash slots → entry-position + 1 (0 = empty, initial cap 8), and `count`/`size` track appended/live entries. `Map()` allocates the lists + an 8-slot zero index; every op HASHES the key (FNV-1a over its code points → non-negative i32, `emitMapHashOf`) into `index` and LINEAR-PROBES (wrapping, `emitMapProbe`) to a free-or-matching slot, comparing keys with the G6 element-wise `==` — no O(n) scan. `m[k]=v` overwrites `vals[entry-1]` on a hit else appends an ordered entry, links `index[slot]=count+1`, bumps count/size, and RESIZES (`emitMapResize`) when `size*2 ≥ cap`: a fresh `2×` index is rebuilt from the ordered entries (hash + inner-probe each, keys/vals untouched). `m[k] ?? d` / `m.has(k)` read the probe result. DELETE/tombstones (the host's `live` array + compaction) are DEFERRED: the checker's op set has no delete, and the struct shape stays forward-compatible for adding a `live` array later. No `parser.vl`/`ast.vl` change.

The self-host checker now models every type the emitter does (i32/f64/bool/string/struct/union/array; maps are the last core-vocabulary gap). With that, a **full-corpus sweep** (all 422 single-file cases driven through `lexer.vl → parser.vl → typecheck.vl` in per-file crash isolation) grew the conformance whitelist from 57 to **156 files** — **64 ACCEPTED** (clean programs VL parses + checks with zero diagnostics) + **92 REJECTED** (invalid programs VL refuses: type errors the checker raises, lexer errors, parser syntax errors). Each entry is VL behaving correctly per the directive (verdict conformance; some advanced `@error` files are refused because the construct is outside VL's subset — a correct refusal, and the test self-corrects if a file later flips). The 266 remaining disagreements are the work left: clean files VL can't yet PARSE (`for`-loops, lambdas, generics, `if/then/else` expressions) and `@error` files VL doesn't yet CATCH (redeclaration, const-reassign). (`compiler/typecheck.vl`, `tests/selfhost_corpus_test.ts`)
- **H-check Phase 2.6: FOR-loops (parser + ast + checker) — ledger 156 → 179** — the single biggest corpus blocker was `for`: 82 valid files used it and the self-host parser had ZERO support. Added two AST nodes — `ForRange` (`for v in A to B [step S] { … }`, a numeric range) and `ForIn` (`for v in arr { … }`, array iteration) — with `mkForRange`/`mkForIn` (`ast.vl`); `parseFor` in `parser.vl` (dispatched from `parseStmt` on the `FOR` keyword; `in`/`to`/`step` are SOFT keywords matched by text, the range-vs-in form decided by whether a soft `to` follows the first expression); and `checkNode` cases in `typecheck.vl` (range bounds + step must be i32, loop var is i32 in the body scope; for-in binds the var to the array's element type and rejects a non-array iterable). Purely additive — no existing self-host test uses `for`, and the compiler's own source is `while`-only, so the golden/fixpoint bytes are unchanged. A re-sweep grew the ledger from 156 to **179** (+23 valid `for` programs now conform; the `for` `@error` files — non-i32 bound, for-in over a non-array — are correctly rejected by the new checks). (`compiler/ast.vl`, `compiler/parser.vl`, `compiler/typecheck.vl`, `tests/selfhost_corpus_test.ts`)
- **H-check Phase 2.7: inline UNION type annotations — ledger 179 → 182** — the largest remaining parser blocker was `|` in type position (`x: A | B`, `T | null`): the self-host parser only did `type N = A | B` decls, not inline annotations. `parseTypeName` now parses a `|`-chain of type atoms into a synthetic name `"A|B|null"` (mirroring the `i32[]`/`{[K]:V}` synthetic names; `null` is accepted as a member; safe because `parseTypeName` is only reached in type position, where `|` is a union separator not the bitwise-OR operator, and `parseTypeDecl` parses its own variants). `nameToTy` splits the synthetic name on `|` (checked BEFORE the `[]`/map shape so a member's suffix isn't misread) and builds a `TyUnion` (or `TyNullable` when a `null` member is present), reusing the existing union/nullable `assignable`. Net +3 (re-sweep: +6 valid union-using programs conform; −3 `@error` union files that now PARSE but whose error VL doesn't yet catch are honestly dropped). COMPLEMENT (negative) narrowing — refining `x` to its type-minus-`T` after a diverging `if x is T { … return }` — was implemented and REVERTED: plain `is T` complement made VL MISS real errors in soundness files that need richer flow narrowing (`!(x is T)`, `== null`, value-kind unions), a net verdict regression, so it is deliberately deferred until done properly. (`compiler/parser.vl`, `compiler/typecheck.vl`, `tests/selfhost_corpus_test.ts`)
- **H3 codegen-bug pay-down: the workaround-forcing host bugs are FIXED — pinned + de-contorted** — the four historical host miscompiles that forced the self-host `.vl` sources into workaround style were re-tested and are ALL resolved by intervening host fixes: (1) two functions `is`-narrowing the SAME union, mutually recursive (the "Finding 2" mono-visitor constraint); (2) a per-variant helper taking the NARROWED variant struct and recursing back; (3) a struct-typed value passed into a mutually-recursive function group ("Unhandled AST → WASM Never"); (4) `.pop()` discarded at statement position on a struct-field array + a discarded/`let`-bound call return at module scale (PR #4/#5 gaps). Each is pinned by a new corpus case (`types/union-two-visitors.vl`, `types/union-narrowed-helper-recursion.vl`, `functions/struct-param-mutual-recursion-global.vl`, `lists/struct-field-pop-statement.vl`, `statements/discarded-call-return.vl`). The `typecheck.vl` mega-visitor is then DE-CONTORTED as the module-scale proof: the `Call`/`FuncDecl`/`Program` arms move out of `checkNode` into natural per-kind helpers (`checkCallNode(n: Call, ix)`, `checkFuncDeclNode(n: FuncDecl)`, `checkProgramNode(n: Program)`) that take the narrowed variant and recurse back — four functions now narrow the `Node` union in the largest concatenated module and everything passes (corpus 182/182, check→emit, pipeline). `popScope` drops the `_dropped` binding; `checkProgram` drops the `_root` indirection (its own body now exercises the discarded-call shape). Stale gap notes in `ast.vl`/`parser.vl`/`typecheck.vl` updated — `P`/`T` as globals is now a documented STYLE choice, not a forced workaround. This unblocks writing all future self-host code in natural, idiomatic shape (the Phase A step-1 of the self-hosting plan). (`compiler/typecheck.vl`, `compiler/ast.vl`, `compiler/parser.vl`, `tests/cases/…`)
- **H-check Phase 2.8: bare-expression bodies + RETURN-TYPE INFERENCE — ledger 182 → 219** — the "inference everywhere" idiom lands in the self-host front end. `parser.vl`: a function with no `{` after its signature (`function dbl(x: i32) x * 2`) parses its single expression into a synthetic one-statement Block (the same shape as a braced trailing-expression body). `typecheck.vl`: an UN-ANNOTATED return type is INFERRED — the function hoists with a `-2` PENDING sentinel; checking its body accumulates witnesses (each `return e` and the trailing expression, via `noteInferredRet` under the pending `curRet`; first concrete type wins, an in-cycle call contributes only "err"); the result is PATCHED into the hoisted `TyFunc` IN PLACE so every caller sees it. A forward call to a not-yet-inferred callee triggers DEMAND inference (`checkCallNode` checks the callee's FuncDecl via the new `fnDeclIx` name→decl map, with an `inferStack` in-progress guard; pass-2 then skips the already-inferred body so diagnostics aren't duplicated). A base-case-less cycle (`ping(){return pong()}` ↔ `pong(){return ping()}`) has no concrete witness and reports "cannot infer a return type — annotate" (matching the host's A17 contract); a self-recursive function WITH a base case infers fine (the in-cycle call types as the err hole, the base case provides the witness). Re-sweep: **+37 files** (the `functions/*` bucket — bare bodies, nested fns, forward/mutual recursion with inference — plus inference-dependent strays). `++`/`--` was considered and deliberately SKIPPED: a parse-time desugar would bake wrong post-increment value semantics into the AST (debt); proper inc/dec nodes come with emit support. (`compiler/parser.vl`, `compiler/typecheck.vl`, `tests/selfhost_corpus_test.ts`)

(3) NULL-NARROWING over a simple identifier: `if x != null { … }` refines a nullable `x` to its inner type in the THEN branch; `if x == null { … } else { … }` refines the ELSE; and a diverging then (`if x == null { return … }` — return/break/continue last) makes `x` non-null for the REST of the block (the guard-clause idiom).
